GATE Space raised €6.3M via the EIC Accelerator and its propulsion system will fly on BeaconSat, Austria's first military satellite. This is a hardware manufacturer with no public developer/API surface; the profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company identity record.

providers.name: Letel
providers.description: Shanghai Letel Communication Equipment (Group) Co., Ltd. (上海乐通通信设备（集团）股份有限公司) is a Chinese manufacturer of information and communication network infrastructure, founded in March 1992 and headquartered in Shanghai with over 1,500 employees and 20+ service locations nationwide. Letel builds data center physical infrastructure — cabinet micromodules, cold aisle micromodules, containerized micromodules, pallet IT cabins, and cabinets — alongside communication cabling equipment, optical communication devices, data communication equipment, broadband access equipment, and structural components for notebooks and servers. It operates through subsidiaries including Zhongle Communication Technology Co., Ltd. Letel publishes no public API, developer portal, or developer documentation; this is a company profile in the API Evangelist network, surfaced as a Qiming Venture Partners portfolio company.

providers.name: Aerialoop
providers.description: Aerialoop is a drone technology and urban logistics company that designs, builds, and operates intelligent aerial networks for cargo delivery, surveillance, and infrastructure inspection. Founded in 2020 and headquartered in Miami with operations rooted in Quito, Ecuador, it is one of the fastest-growing drone delivery operations in Latin America. Its ALT 6-8 delivery drone carries a 5kg payload for urban logistics, while the ALT 6-ISR line adds HD, infrared, and night-vision cameras with AI-powered intrusion detection; extended-range variants operate up to 120km using LEO satellite connectivity for beyond-visual-line-of-sight flights. The company has completed over 50,000 flights across six countries. Aerialoop is a Techstars Miami (powered by J.P. Morgan) portfolio company. It currently publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Kano Computing
providers.description: Kano Computing is a London-based technology company founded in 2013 by Alex Klein, Saul Klein and Yonatan Raz-Fridman that began by shipping build-it-yourself computer and coding kits designed to teach STEM and creative computing to children on top of Raspberry Pi hardware. Its catalog spanned the Kano Computer Kit, motion-sensor and Harry Potter / Star Wars coding wands, the Windows-based Kano PC built with Microsoft, and the Stem Player and Stem Video Projector consumer devices. Kano paired the hardware with Kano Code, a block-to-text creative-coding platform, and Kano World, an online making and sharing community. The company entered administration in 2023 and its assets now trade under the Stem brand; its developer footprint survives as open-source tooling in the KanoComputing GitHub organization and the npm @kano scope rather than a hosted API.

providers.name: Occamnetworks
providers.description: Occam Networks was a broadband access equipment vendor that developed and marketed systems enabling telecommunications carriers to profitably deliver emerging voice, video, and high-speed data (triple-play) services over copper and fiber, including its BLC 6000 access platform and ONT/ONU customer-premises hardware. The company was acquired by Calix in early 2011 and no longer operates independently. The occamnetworks.com domain currently serves an archived circa-2010 marketing site (products, solutions, support, news, whitepapers) with no developer program, API, SDK, or documentation surface. Enrichment found no API artifacts to harvest.

providers.name: Sandbar
providers.description: Sandbar is a consumer hardware and AI company behind Stream, a private voice ring and conversational notes app. Worn on the finger, Stream pairs a discreet private microphone, a glass touchpad, and silent haptics with an on-device "Inner Voice" assistant so people can capture notes, reminders, and todos, dictate speech-to-text across any iOS or Mac app, and think aloud without reaching for a phone. Backed by Kindred Ventures and True Ventures, Sandbar is a preorder-stage consumer product; it publishes a marketing site, an About/Us page, and a Careers page, but no public developer portal, API, or SDK surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Standardkernel
providers.description: Standard Kernel Co. is an AI infrastructure company that automatically generates high-performance compute kernels for GPUs and TPUs. It targets the traditionally manual, expertise-intensive process of writing optimized low-level accelerator code, operating at the CUDA and PTX level to fully exploit new hardware features rather than relying on higher-level abstractions, delivering better performance on compute-bound machine-learning workloads and newer accelerator architectures. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Felicis and added to the API Evangelist network; the company is early-stage and publishes no public API, developer portal, or specification at this time.

providers.name: Carpenter Technology
providers.description: Carpenter Technology Corporation is a U.S.-based producer and distributor of premium specialty alloys — including titanium alloys, powder metals, high-temperature stainless steels, tool steels, and soft magnetic alloys — serving the aerospace, defense, medical, transportation, energy, and industrial end markets. The company supports customers through technical product resources such as its Alloy Finder, alloy technical data sheets, conversion tables, and a member-only Customer Portal for order and account self-service, but does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Dotterel
providers.description: Dotterel Technologies is an Auckland, New Zealand acoustics and audio-hardware company founded in 2015 out of the Callaghan Innovation C-Prize. It began by solving drone noise, building acoustic shrouds, low-noise propellers, and onboard active audio-recording systems for UAVs used in film, security, and noise mapping. That work led to Konos (now marketed as Konos Digital), an 80-element directional MEMS microphone array with a continuously variable 60-300 degree beam width that streams four channels of AES67 / SMPTE ST 2110 audio over a single Power-over-Ethernet cable, targeting film, broadcast, and live-sports production. The microphone exposes a firmware-updatable on-device HTTP control interface (a web page plus a POST control endpoint for beam steering) rather than a public developer web API. Dotterel is backed by Techstars (Adelaide 2017 cohort) and is tracked here as a hardware company; it publishes no public API specification, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: KEENON Robotics
providers.description: KEENON Robotics is a global commercial service-robotics company founded in 2010 and headquartered in Shanghai, China, designing and manufacturing autonomous service robots deployed across more than 70 countries and 600+ cities. Its product lines span catering and delivery robots (the T-series and W3), the KLEENBOT commercial floor-cleaning range (C20/C30/C40/C55), heavy-load delivery robots (S100/S300), humanoid service robots (XMAN-R1/XMAN-F1), hospital and hotel logistics solutions (including the WITMED medical line), and the Keenmow K1 domestic robot. KEENON is a hardware-and-solutions company; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI. This record is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: Nothing
providers.description: Nothing is a London-based consumer technology company designing smartphones (Phone series), wireless earbuds (Ear series), and other consumer hardware under the Nothing and CMF by Nothing brands, backed by EQT Ventures and GV. Surfaced as a portfolio-company lead in the API Evangelist network. An enrichment pass confirmed Nothing publishes a consumer web presence (support centre, community, careers, playground) but no public developer API, API documentation, developer portal, SDK, or webhook surface as of this pass.

providers.name: Remora
providers.description: Remora is a carbon-capture startup (legally Echeneidae Inc.) founded in 2020 and based in Wixom, Michigan, that retrofits semi-trucks and locomotives with zero-backpressure devices which extract and purify up to 90 percent of the CO2 from vehicle exhaust while cutting other pollutants. The company then sells the captured, purified carbon dioxide and shares the resulting revenue with the transportation operators it partners with. Remora is a hardware and climate-technology business with no public API or developer platform; this profile tracks it as an API Evangelist network company for portfolio and discovery purposes.

providers.name: Unconventional AI
providers.description: Unconventional AI (unconv.ai) is rethinking the foundations of the computer to optimize energy efficiency for AI, working to bring biology-scale efficiency to artificial intelligence through analog, dynamical-system hardware co-evolved with neural software. Founded by experts in AI systems, analog circuits, computing theory, and neuroscience, and backed by Felicis, the company publishes research including the Un-0 image-generation model built on coupled Kuramoto oscillators and an instruction set architecture for dynamical-system hardware, but does not yet publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Unconventional AI
providers.description: Unconventional AI is rethinking the foundations of compute to bring biology-scale energy efficiency to AI. The company researches dynamical systems such as coupled Kuramoto oscillators as a computing substrate that maps onto analog and physical hardware, pointing toward on the order of 1000x lower energy for AI than today's digital accelerators. Its open-source Un-0 reference implementation generates images by integrating the phase dynamics of coupled oscillators. Backed by DCVC, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Lux Capital, and Wing Venture Capital. The company does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Mips
providers.description: MIPS is a processor IP and compute company building embedded and edge AI silicon for automotive, robotics, and mission-critical systems. Its portfolio spans the MIPS RISC-V CPU families (M8500, I8500, P8700, S8200), the ARC processor and NPX/VPX accelerator lines, and development tooling such as MIPS Atlas Explorer virtual platforms and the ASIP Designer / ASIP Programmer toolchains. MIPS frames its offering around a "Sense, Think, Act, Communicate" signal chain for real-time autonomy — what it calls Physical AI at the edge. MIPS is a semiconductor IP licensor rather than a public web-API provider; this profile was surfaced as a Mayfield portfolio company and enriched with identity and probed security posture.

providers.name: Libra Robotics
providers.description: Libra Robotics is a Silicon Valley robotics startup building autonomous robots that install solar panels in the field, targeting projects from 1 MW upward across utility-scale, commercial and industrial, community solar, and agrivoltaic applications. The company's field system — marketed as Libra 001 — combines purpose-built end-effectors, suction-based panel handling and transport, vision and positioning systems that align each module with the tracker structure, and fastener workflows compatible with multiple commercial racking systems, operating across day and night shifts. Libra Robotics was founded by Yaojing Huang and Jermaine Zhao, is part of the Y Combinator Summer 2026 batch, and operates out of Newark, California. As of this profile the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications; its web presence is a six-page marketing site covering solutions, technology, safety, company, and contact.

providers.name: Praan
providers.description: Praan (Praan Climate Technologies) is a deep-tech climate startup working to democratize access to clean, healthy air and to rebuild the atmosphere by capturing air pollution and greenhouse gases with novel filterless technology. Its products include HIVE, an air-purification device for homes and commercial spaces paired with a companion mobile application, and MK II, an air-purification system for industrial environments. Praan is backed by Prosus Ventures. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and enriched through the API Evangelist pipeline; as of this pass Praan publishes a consumer hardware and mobile-app surface but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation.

providers.name: Anki
providers.description: Anki, Inc. was a consumer robotics and artificial-intelligence company based in San Francisco, founded in 2010 and backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Index Ventures, and J.P. Morgan. It was known for the Cozmo and Vector companion robots and the Anki Drive / Overdrive robotic racing system, which combined computer vision, on-device AI, and mapping/navigation. Anki debuted at Apple's WWDC in 2013, shipped Cozmo in 2016 and Vector in 2018, and published first-party Python and C# SDKs so developers could program the robots over a local connection. Anki ceased operations in May 2019 and its assets were later acquired by Digital Dream Labs. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the robot SDKs remain the company's public developer surface.

providers.name: HUM Industries
providers.description: HUM Industries is a consumer hardware company building a wearable AI assistant designed to enhance social presence. The device records conversations locally, maintains a rolling buffer of recent audio, and surfaces contextual information such as names, personal details, and commitments back to the wearer through subtle audio cues. The company frames the product as giving people "the freedom to forget" by offloading memory to the device so they can stay present in the moment. At the time of profiling the product is pre-launch, offered through a preorder waitlist, with no public API, developer portal, or third-party integration surface. Backed by a16z; added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead.

providers.name: 83 Sciences
providers.description: 83 Sciences is an AI-native materials-discovery company (Y Combinator Summer 2026) that helps research labs unlock value from unpublished and discarded experimental data. Roughly 90% of experimental data never reaches publication; 83 Sciences works on-site with researchers to capture and structure that hidden data into a queryable database, then applies AI-powered analysis and generative models to learn from a lab's full experimental history — including failed experiments — to surface novel materials, co-authored manuscripts, and patents. Founded by researchers from MIT, Stanford, Harvard, and Columbia and based in San Francisco. The company currently ships no public API or developer surface; this profile tracks its identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Anoria
providers.description: Anoria is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) human-interaction company building a wearable bracelet for the EQ era that measures and tracks emotional states in real time. The device uses the company's proprietary SOMI (state-of-mind inference) model to correlate roughly 150 audio and biometric signals into a "Flow Score" that reflects a user's energy, mood, and focus, then explains why the user feels that way and what they can do about it. Anoria targets founders and creatives who treat their mental state as a performance asset, with the goal of making emotional intelligence trainable. As of mid-2026 the company is an early-stage prototype running an early-access waitlist; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation yet, so this API Evangelist profile captures verified company identity only.

providers.name: Artiphon
providers.description: Artiphon is a Nashville-based music technology company that designs smart, portable musical instruments for everyday creativity. Its products, including the Instrument 1, Orba, Orba 2, Orba 3, and Chorda, combine strumming, tapping, sliding, and looping into palm-sized MIDI controllers and synthesizers, paired with companion apps that let anyone make beats, loop sounds, and explore music anywhere. Artiphon sells direct and through retailers such as Guitar Center and Sweetwater. It does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a consumer-hardware company reference.

providers.name: ConvenientPower
providers.description: ConvenientPower (Chengdu ConvenientPower Semiconductor, 成都市易冲半导体有限公司) is an analog and mixed-signal integrated-circuit design company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Chengdu, Sichuan, China, with offices in Beijing, Shanghai, Xi'an, Shenzhen, Hong Kong, Taiwan, and Silicon Valley. The company designs high-performance power-management ICs spanning the full link from 220V mains to battery: wireless-charging transmitters and receivers (Qi, up to 100W), USB Power Delivery and UFCS protocol controllers, AC/DC flyback and synchronous rectifier controllers, GaN-integrated solutions, battery-charging management, LDOs and DC/DC converters, and automotive-grade power ICs (wireless charging, LED lighting, eFuse protection, switches). Its parts ship into consumer electronics, accessories, and automotive markets, with more than 330 million units shipped and 160+ patents; automotive ICs are AEC-Q100 qualified. As a hardware semiconductor vendor, ConvenientPower exposes developer resources as chip SDK toolkits, reference designs, and design software rather than a public web API. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: EnerVenue
providers.description: EnerVenue is a Fremont, California-based energy infrastructure company building long-duration stationary energy storage using a metal-hydrogen (nickel-hydrogen) battery chemistry derived from NASA-heritage technology that has powered the Hubble Space Telescope and the International Space Station since the 1980s. Co-founded by Stanford materials scientist Professor Yi Cui, EnerVenue refined the orbital nickel-hydrogen cell into a grid-scale "Energy Storage Vessel" (ESV) targeting a 30-year, 30,000+ cycle service life with 100% usable depth of discharge, ~90% round-trip efficiency, an operating range of -20 C to +60 C, no thermal runaway risk, and no active thermal management. The ESV's aqueous metal cell (AMC) uses a nickel hydroxide cathode, a nickel-alloy anode, an alkaline electrolyte, and hermetically sealed hydrogen gas storage built from steel, nickel, fiberglass, resin, and water — no lithium, cobalt, or rare earths. EnerVenue is scaling manufacturing through a one-million- square-foot gigafactory in Shelby County, Kentucky (1 GWh phase one, scaling toward 20 GWh per year with ~$1B of follow-on investment) plus a high-volume line in Changzhou, China (250 MWh by Q3 2026, 1 GWh in 2027). Customer commitments exceed 7 GWh and include Pine Gate Renewables (2.4 GWh, multi-year), Green Energy Renewable Solutions (Nicon Industries), Sonnell Power Solutions, and VedantaESS. The company closed a $300M Series B in 2026 to fund the gigafactory build-out. EnerVenue sells hardware, EPC-integrated storage systems, and long-duration service warranties — it does not publish a developer API, SDK, public OpenAPI specification, or open-source repository.

providers.name: Manufactured
providers.description: Manufactured is a supply-chain and production platform for hardware and consumer-product brands, backed by Bullpen Capital. Its web application (app.manufactured.com) helps teams run overseas production end to end — issuing sourcing requests to vendors, managing supplier and vendor profiles, negotiating order estimates and contracts under master procurement agreements, tracking production timelines and calendars, and financing purchase orders through production and repayment terms. The product also embeds an AI assistant built on LangChain. At the time of enrichment the public marketing site and the api/docs/developer subdomains were unreachable, and the GraphQL, Lambda and bot backends are private and authentication-gated (introspection blocked), so no public API specification, developer portal, or documentation could be harvested. This profile captures the real, observable surface only.

providers.name: Maquoketa Research
providers.description: Maquoketa Research is a defense-technology startup (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) building autonomous terminal-guidance systems for one-way attack drones. Its platform-agnostic guidance modules add custom computer-vision object tracking to low-cost FPV drone hardware, raising strike success rates from under 25% to roughly 80% while maintaining target lock through GPS jamming and signal loss. Founded in 2025 and based in San Francisco, the five-person team ships hardware modules (product lines include GCS, Magpie, Odin, and TGS) that integrate with existing drone flight controllers rather than a public developer API. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched from the company's public website; it currently exposes no public API, SDK, or developer platform surface.

providers.name: Cambium
providers.description: Cambium is an advanced materials company (Cambium Biomaterials, El Segundo, California, founded 2019) that molecularly re-engineers polymers from first principles, pairing AI-driven molecular design with chemistry, materials science, biology, and agile domestic manufacturing to develop and scale next-generation materials roughly 10x faster than traditional methods. Product lines span thermal protection systems, high-temperature structural polymers, and laser/directed-energy protection, serving aerospace, space, defense, motorsport, automotive, marine, and industrial customers. Its SHD Advanced Composites business runs rapid-response prepreg manufacturing across the US, UK, and EU. Backed by 8VC. Cambium publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; this profile captures corporate identity and probed domain security only.

providers.name: iTAC Software
providers.description: iTAC Software AG is an independent company of the Duerr Group and a leading provider of Manufacturing Execution System (MES) and Manufacturing Operations Management (MOM) software for discrete manufacturing. Its iTAC.MOM.Suite delivers production control, end-to-end traceability, quality management, and AI-supported analytics that help automotive, electronics, and medical-technology manufacturers implement Industry 4.0 and smart-factory operations. iTAC does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; system integration is delivered through the MOM platform's IoT and connectivity layers as part of a project engagement.

providers.name: Lynq
providers.description: Lynq Networks develops infrastructure-free, long-range wireless connectivity for enterprise and OEM devices, bridging the gap between short-range Bluetooth and infrastructure-dependent cellular/5G. Its technology lets original equipment manufacturers build large-area device networks without deploying traditional network infrastructure, targeting construction, agriculture, military, and public-safety use cases. Lynq is a Techstars-backed portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API documentation; this profile captures its identity and a domain-security probe for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Machindustries
providers.description: Mach Industries develops and manufactures asymmetric aerospace and defense systems and components, aiming to produce them by the millions to deter conflict and advance prosperity. Its product line includes Viper (a turbojet vertical-takeoff attack drone), Glide and Pike precision strike munitions, Stratos high-altitude platforms, Dart counter-drone interceptors, and an Energetics propulsion and explosives testing practice. The company is a Khosla Ventures portfolio company. It is a hardware and manufacturing business with no public developer API surface at this time; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company identity and monitoring.

providers.name: Nitricity
providers.description: Nitricity is a climate-tech and agricultural-technology company that produces nitrogen fertilizer on-farm from only air, water, and renewable electricity. Founded in 2018 by Stanford graduate researchers Nicolas Pinkowski and Joshua McEnaney, the company uses a solar-powered plasma / electrochemical process to fix atmospheric nitrogen and produce nitric acid and calcium nitrate fertilizers on-site and on-demand, eliminating the fossil-fuel-intensive Haber-Bosch process and long-distance transportation that make conventional fertilizer responsible for roughly 5% of global greenhouse gas emissions. Backed by Khosla Ventures, Fine Structure Ventures, Lowercarbon Capital, and strategic investor Chipotle, Nitricity is a hardware and physical-product company; it publishes a corporate website, blog, and field-trial program but exposes no public API, developer portal, or technical integration surface.

providers.name: Openlight
providers.description: OpenLight Photonics is a silicon photonics company that designs and manufactures custom Photonic Application-Specific Integrated Circuits (PASICs) using a heterogeneously integrated, open silicon photonics platform that builds active components such as lasers and modulators onto the same chip as passive waveguides. Operating an open foundry model out of Goleta, California, OpenLight offers three services: design enablement through its Process Design Kit (PDK) with component libraries, evaluation kits, and a PDK Sampler; in-house custom PASIC design; and production manufacturing. Its technology targets datacom, telecom, AI data-center interconnect, lidar, HPC, healthcare, quantum, and IoT sensing. Spun out of Synopsys as an independent, venture-backed company in 2025, OpenLight has raised roughly $84M (a $34M Series A in 2025 and a $50M Series A-1 in 2026) from investors including Mayfield. This is a hardware/semiconductor company; it publishes no public web API, developer portal, or OpenAPI at this time — its developer surface is the chip-design PDK.

providers.name: Substrate
providers.description: Substrate is a semiconductor manufacturing company building America's next-generation chip foundry, with the stated mission of returning the United States to dominance in advanced semiconductor fabrication. Rather than designing chips, the company is inventing manufacturing technology intended to extend Moore's Law while lowering the cost of building state-of-the-art fabs and the wafers they produce. Substrate is a hard-tech / advanced-manufacturing venture backed by General Catalyst; it is a physical-infrastructure company and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced from the General Catalyst portfolio and enriched with the provider's public identity and security surface.

providers.name: Tile
providers.description: Tile is a consumer-electronics company known for its Bluetooth tracker devices, used to locate everyday items such as keys, wallets, bags, and phones through a companion mobile app and a crowd-sourced Find network. Tile was acquired by Life360 in 2021; its former site thetileapp.com now 301-redirects to life360.com. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners, Tile publishes no public developer API — this profile captures its security posture (security.txt, a HackerOne responsible-disclosure program, and probed domain security).

providers.name: Upverter
providers.description: Upverter is a browser-based, collaborative electronic design automation (EDA) platform for schematic capture and PCB layout, founded in Toronto in 2010 (Y Combinator W11) and acquired by Altium in 2017. Surfaced as a Version One Ventures portfolio company. As of the July 2026 enrichment probe the upverter.com platform returns HTTP 502 on every path, its docs/blog/status subdomains no longer resolve, and no public API surface remains; the GitHub organization is dormant since 2019.

providers.name: Vaire Computing
providers.description: Vaire Computing is a deep-tech semiconductor startup building reversible computing chips for near-zero energy computing. Its reversible logic gates recover and recycle the energy of computation instead of dissipating it as heat, aiming to decouple energy consumption from growth in computing power. The company was co-founded by Rodolfo Rosini (CEO) and Dr Hannah Earley (CTO), is backed by Seedcamp, 7percent Ventures, and Lifeline Ventures, and publishes technology and software whitepapers. Vaire currently publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Vertical Semiconductor
providers.description: Vertical Semiconductor is an MIT spinout developing next-generation vertical Gallium Nitride (GaN) power devices for AI data centers and grid infrastructure. Built on a decade of research from MIT's Palacios Group, its vertical GaN transistors push energy conversion closer to the chip with less power loss and heat, targeting high-voltage applications from 100V to over 2kV. The company claims up to 30% higher efficiency, a 50% smaller power footprint, and 10% lower total cost of ownership versus silicon, and has demonstrated its platform on 8-inch wafers using standard silicon CMOS manufacturing. It is a hardware/deep-tech power-electronics company with no public API, developer portal, SDK, or OpenAPI surface. Backed by Playground Global.

providers.name: Gas POS
providers.description: Gas Pos is a North Little Rock, Arkansas technology company (founded 2015) that builds cloud-based point-of-sale systems and EMV-certified fuel dispensers for gas stations and truck stops across the United States. Delivered as equipment-as-a-service with no upfront hardware cost, the platform pairs touchscreen POS terminals, barcode scanners, and back-office inventory and pricing tools with PCI-compliant, EMV-certified payment processing at both the register and the pump. It accepts major fleet cards including Comdata, Comchek, EFS, T-Chek, Voyager, and Fleetone, and lets operators manage item pricing and inventory remotely from a phone. Backed by 500 Global and Pioneer Fund. Added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API surface has been located to date.

providers.name: Habana Labs
providers.description: Habana Labs is an artificial-intelligence processor company, now part of Intel, that designs deep-learning accelerators for AI training and inference. Its Gaudi (training) and Goya (inference) processors — sold today as the Intel Gaudi 2 and Gaudi 3 AI accelerators — are programmed through the SynapseAI software suite, which integrates with PyTorch and DeepSpeed and ships reference models, containers, and installation tooling. Habana was founded in 2016 in Israel and acquired by Intel in 2019. Its public developer surface is not a hosted web API but an open-source SDK and toolchain: the HabanaAI GitHub organization (reference models, PyTorch bridge, setup/install, plus vLLM and Megatron forks) and the Intel Gaudi documentation at docs.habana.ai. This profile catalogs that developer footprint for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: LINSOL Co.,Ltd.
providers.description: LINSOL Co.,Ltd. (린솔) is a safety-technology company headquartered in Daejeon, South Korea, founded as an in-house venture spun out of Hanwha Aerospace. LINSOL adapts acoustic detection techniques originally developed for defense landmine applications into commercial real-time hazard, accident, and environmental detection. Its product line includes Karang F (driving-environment detection), Karang S (precision acoustic signal transmission), SkyShield (fall detection), BR, Acoustic Eye (aerial security), and Safety Nova (smart integrated safety platform), sold into industrial safety, ESG, and defense security use cases. The company operates a Daejeon headquarters and research center plus a Goheung branch. LINSOL ships hardware and integrated platforms; as of a 2026-07-19 probe it publishes no public developer API, portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Hexcel
providers.description: Hexcel Corporation (NYSE: HXL) is a global leader in advanced composite materials for the aerospace, defense and space, and industrial markets. Headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut and operating roughly 18 manufacturing facilities worldwide with about 5,800 employees, Hexcel produces HexTow carbon fiber, HexPly prepregs, HexWeb honeycomb, HexForce reinforcements, HexBond adhesives, HexFlow infusion resins, and HexTool tooling materials supplied into commercial aircraft, military platforms, space launch vehicles, wind energy blades, and industrial structures. Hexcel is a critical materials supplier to Boeing and Airbus and supports more than 100 defense programs; it has no public developer portal, REST APIs, SDKs, or machine-readable product catalog. Customer interaction with technical resources is PDF-based (datasheets, technology manuals, brochures), and the company's GitHub organization (github.com/Hexcel) is registered but empty.

providers.name: BYD
providers.description: BYD Company Ltd. is a Chinese multinational manufacturing conglomerate headquartered in Shenzhen, founded in 1995 by Wang Chuanfu and publicly listed in Hong Kong (1211) and Shenzhen (002594). Originally a rechargeable-battery maker, BYD has grown into one of the world's largest producers of new-energy vehicles (battery-electric and plug-in hybrid cars, buses, and trucks), power batteries (including the Blade Battery), consumer and automotive electronics, rail transit systems (SkyRail/SkyShuttle), forklifts, and solar and energy-storage products. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of hongshan and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; BYD is a hardware and manufacturing company and does not publish a public developer or API program.

providers.name: Dabee
providers.description: Dabee (dabee.com.br) is a Brazilian consumer-technology review and comparison website that helps shoppers make informed purchasing decisions about electronics and gadgets. It publishes hands-on reviews, side-by-side comparisons, and buying guides across notebooks, smartphones, tablets, monitors, smartwatches, gaming consoles, smart TVs, and networking equipment, with 'vale a pena' (is-it-worth-it) verdicts and price tracking pulled from Amazon Brazil. The site monetizes through affiliate commissions. As of this profile it exposes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal; it was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead.

providers.name: Gbatteries
providers.description: GBatteries (GBatteries Energy Canada Inc.) is an Ottawa, Ontario battery technology company developing lithium-metal battery cells and an intelligent, adaptive battery management system for the next generation of electric mobility, from land to air. Its technology targets fast charging (sub-15-minute charge), high energy density (450+ Wh/kg), extended cycle life, and enhanced safety by actively reducing irreversible internal cell damage. The company reports 60+ granted or pending patents and 9+ years of R&D, and was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company. GBatteries is a hardware and battery-management deeptech firm; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Ideal Power Converters
providers.description: Ideal Power Inc. (NASDAQ: IPWR), formerly Ideal Power Converters, is an Austin, Texas power semiconductor company developing bidirectional bipolar junction transistor (B-TRAN) technology for ultra-low conduction losses, bidirectional current flow, and fast fault protection and switching. Its product portfolio includes B-TRAN power switches, SymCool power modules, and B-TRAN Known Good Die, targeting data centers, energy storage systems, power grids, solid-state circuit breakers, and EV charging infrastructure. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Battery Ventures portfolio company; the company publishes a corporate and investor web presence but no public developer API or programmatic surface at this time.

providers.name: NcodiN
providers.description: NcodiN is a French deep-tech company developing optical interconnect technology for high-performance computing and AI infrastructure. Founded in Palaiseau, France, the company builds miniaturized lasers integrated directly on silicon to replace traditional copper connections between chiplets and processors, aiming to break the "copper wall" that limits AI scaling. Its photonic interconnects promise petabit-per-second bandwidth with roughly a thousand times less energy to move data than copper links, targeting AI, telecommunications, autonomous driving, smart cities, healthcare, and climate modeling. NcodiN is backed by venture firms including Earlybird, Elaia, OVNI Capital, and Verve Ventures, is advised by major chip and equipment makers such as NVIDIA, Qualcomm, Intel, and ASML, and joined the FrenchTech2030 cohort in November 2025. As a semiconductor and photonics hardware company it sells to chipmakers and does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or developer documentation surface.

providers.name: Physical Property Testing
providers.description: Physical Properties Testers (PPT) Group is a Halifax, UK based multinational manufacturer of physical property test and measurement instrumentation, built through acquisition around four brands: James Heal (textile testing including bursting strength, abrasion and tear), Mecmesin (universal testing machines, torque testers and digital force gauges), Alluris (handheld force gauges and force/torque instrumentation) and Lansmont (shock, vibration and drop testing systems). The group designs, produces and services testing equipment that verifies the physical integrity and quality of raw materials, components and finished products across textiles, packaging, manufacturing and consumer goods. It is a hardware and laboratory-instrumentation business with no public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface. Registered in England and Wales (company no. 09210539); a portfolio company of SK Capital Partners since March 2025 (previously backed by Battery Ventures). This profile was surfaced as a VC portfolio lead and enriched with company identity from public sources.

providers.name: Samsara Eco
providers.description: Samsara Eco is an Australian climate-technology company pioneering enzymatic recycling, a process that uses engineered enzymes to break plastics and synthetic textiles down into their molecular building blocks so they can be infinitely remade into new materials with no loss of quality. Spun out of the Australian National University, the company recovers nylon and polyester from mixed and coloured textile and plastic waste and partners with global brands to build a circular materials supply chain. It is a materials-science and biotech company rather than an API provider, and has no public developer, API, or technical integration surface at this time.

providers.name: Sunrise
providers.description: Sunrise Robotics builds intelligent, two-armed autonomous robotic cells for manufacturing. The AI-driven system combines built-in perception and environmental awareness with autonomous execution to transform existing production processes, increase capacity, and free human workers for higher-value tasks. Cells deploy quickly (needing only a three-phase outlet), are flexible across manufacturing applications, and are built to ISO 10218 / TS 15066 safety standards. The company is backed by Seedcamp and Slow Ventures.

providers.name: SupplyHog
providers.description: SupplyHog is an ecommerce platform built specifically for hardware and building-materials retailers, giving independent hardware and building-supply stores a branded online storefront to sell their products. The platform provides co-op and custom product catalogs, flexible fulfillment (in-store pickup, ship-to-store, local delivery, and ship-to-home with Shippo shipping labels), Stripe-powered payments, TaxJar tax calculation, real-time ERP inventory and pricing synchronization, custom branding and domains, location-aware search, and admin tools for order fulfillment and abandoned-cart recovery. Founded in 2010 as the Nopone.com reverse-auction marketplace, SupplyHog went through the DreamIt and 500 Startups accelerators, pivoted to full ecommerce services, and was acquired by construction-supply retailer R.P. Lumber in 2016. It does not publish a public developer API surface; it acts as a consumer of Stripe, TaxJar, and Shippo.

providers.name: teaBOT
providers.description: teaBOT is a Toronto-based hardware startup (Y Combinator, Summer 2015) that builds an automated loose-leaf tea-making robot offered to offices, showrooms, and lounges as an amenity-as-a-service. For a flat monthly fee, teams use the companion teaBOT app to explore premium teas and dispense a custom-blended cup in under 30 seconds, which companies such as Google, HubSpot, and McKinsey use as a workplace recruiting and retention perk. Founded by robotics PhD Rehman Merali, teaBOT runs a physical-product and mobile-app business and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Chef Robotics
providers.description: Chef Robotics is a San Francisco, California physical-AI company building AI-enabled robots for high-mix food production. Its core product is an NSF-certified food-assembly robot that picks, scoops, and deposits a wide range of ingredients — fresh, cooked, IQF, sauces, leafy greens, mixed vegetables, and discrete piece items — into trays, burritos, wraps, pizza bases, and other containers on conveyor lines. The robots are powered by ChefOS, a proprietary Generalized Food Manipulation Model trained on tens of millions of real-world servings and tens of thousands of hours of production data, combining vision, decision-making, and robot control across a See / Think / Act stack with continuous Fleet Learning. Chef Robotics sells via a Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) model that bundles hardware, software updates, 24/7 monitoring, and customer success. Deployed customers include Amy's Kitchen, Sunbasket, Cafe Spice, and Chef Bombay, with the fleet having produced 98+ million servings across the US, Canada, and Europe. The company is venture-backed (Kleiner Perkins, Avataar Ventures-led $43M Series A, Bloomberg Beta, Construct Capital) and serves frozen meals, fresh meals, co-manufacturing, D2C meal delivery, medically tailored meals, meatpacking, airline catering, and foodservice verticals. There is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for ChefOS — the platform is operated as a closed, fleet-managed service on Chef-owned hardware deployed inside customer facilities.

providers.name: iRobot
providers.description: iRobot Corporation is a Bedford, Massachusetts consumer robotics company best known for the Roomba robot vacuum and the Braava and Braava jet robot mop product lines. Founded in 1990 by MIT roboticists, iRobot pioneered the home cleaning robot category and has sold tens of millions of units worldwide. Its current portfolio includes the Roomba Max, Roomba Plus, and Roomba 100/200 series vacuums and combo (vacuum + mop) models, along with AutoWash and AutoEmpty docks, the iRobot Home App for scheduling and mapping, and a cleaning accessories and trade-in program. The proposed acquisition by Amazon was abandoned in January 2024 after regulatory pushback from the European Commission, after which iRobot underwent a major restructuring and layoffs. iRobot's revenue model is direct robot and accessory sales plus recurring consumables; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI specification, and its homesupport documentation explicitly notes that Wi-Fi connected Roombas do not have an open API. A community of unofficial reverse-engineered libraries (dorita980, rest980, pyirobot) exists but is not endorsed by iRobot.

providers.name: Peer Robotics
providers.description: Peer Robotics builds collaborative autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) for manufacturing and warehouse material movement, designed to learn directly from humans to lower the cost and complexity of traditional automation. Its lineup includes the Peer 3000 collaborative mobile robot and the RM250 and RM500 AMRs (250kg and 500kg payloads) that handle pallets, trolleys, bin delivery, and machine tending through an intuitive human-robot dashboard interface. Backed by Techstars, the company operates a hardware and robotics product line rather than a public developer API surface; no public API, SDK, developer documentation, or GitHub repositories were found during enrichment probing.

providers.name: Photon Crystal Energy
providers.description: Photon Crystal Energy Technology Ltd. (广东光晶能源科技有限公司) is a China-based perovskite photovoltaic module manufacturer, founded May 2022 and headquartered in Foshan, Guangdong. The company commercializes full wet-process, full-printed perovskite PV modules for building-integrated photovoltaics (BIPV), photovoltaic curtain walls, rooftop distributed solar, carports and architectural solar applications. Product families include standard, semi-transparent, textured, architectural color and solar tile modules, and the firm operates a 100 MW full-printed perovskite pilot line with IEC 61215 / IEC 61730 certification milestones. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes a marketing/corporate website but no public API, SDK, or developer surface.

providers.name: Team Wildfire
providers.description: Team Wildfire develops jet engine-enabled fire suppression technology built to prevent catastrophic wildfire losses. Its mobile units, the "Hurricane" and "Storm Cell", apply fire retardant at scale to deny ground to advancing wildfires. The company offers fireground services, evacuation route hardening, asset protection, prescribed fire containment, and military base protection. Team Wildfire is a physical hardware and services company backed by Techstars; it publishes a marketing and services website but no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or developer documentation. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio lead and enriched with the identity and domain-security signals available for a non-API company.

providers.name: Unigrid
providers.description: UNIGRID Inc. is a San Diego-based sodium-ion battery company founded in 2021 out of UC San Diego Ph.D. research by Dr. Darren H. S. Tan and Dr. Erik A. Wu. Its sodium chromium oxide (NCO) chemistry and alloy anode technology deliver fire-safe, fully passive batteries rated for 30,000+ cycles and -40C to 60C operation, sold as 12V starter batteries (Na+ Fleet), BMS-less rack modules (Na+ Module), residential energy storage (Na+ Casa), and DC rack systems for commercial, industrial, and data center use (Na+ Cleo). Cells are UN38.3 and UL 9540A certified. Backed by Transition VC, Ritz Venture Capital, Union Square Ventures, and Foothill Ventures via an oversubscribed $12M Series A (2024); shipped its first sodium-ion residential batteries in July 2026. UNIGRID publishes no public API or developer program.

providers.name: Voxel Energy
providers.description: Voxel Energy is a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company building energy-independent, off-grid data centers powered by on-site solar generation and second-life EV batteries over a DC microgrid architecture. Founded in 2025 by ex-Tesla engineers Casey Spencer, Max Pfeiffer, and Evan Schmidt, the San Francisco company delivers modular, prefabricated data center power systems that bypass multi-year utility interconnection queues, taking facilities from site selection to commissioning in months. Voxel Energy is an infrastructure hardware company and does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: AMP Fund
providers.description: AMP (AMP PBC) is a public benefit corporation founded in 2025 by Anjney Midha, a former Andreessen Horowitz general partner, to build an independent "AI grid" — a pooled compute utility for frontier AI research teams. Rather than operating as a cloud provider or a conventional venture firm, AMP acts as an independent system operator: data center operators and labs contribute underutilized GPU capacity to a shared network, and member research teams draw base-load and burst compute from that pool at rates intended to sit below the volatile spot market. AMP pairs capital with compute, having raised roughly $1.3 billion for its first fund, and its PBC charter is structured so leadership can supply compute at cost without shareholder challenge. It has also committed a Public Wealth Fund of up to $500 million through 2030 toward education, workforce readiness, healthcare access, and economic resilience in communities affected by the AI transition. AMP publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Eliyan
providers.description: Eliyan Corporation is a fabless semiconductor company in Santa Clara, California that develops chiplet and chip-to-chip interconnect physical-layer (PHY) IP for multi-die and AI infrastructure systems. Its NuLink die-to-die and die-to-memory PHY, NuLink-X chip-to-chip PHY, NuLink-XD 224G PAM4 SerDes for electro-optical modules, and NuGear chiplets let designers build multi-die architectures on standard organic substrates as well as advanced packaging, using simultaneous bidirectional signaling and support for UCIe, Bunch of Wires (BoW) and its own UMI interface. Eliyan licenses silicon IP and sells chiplets to semiconductor and hyperscale customers rather than operating a public web API; the company publishes no developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Lemnos Labs
providers.description: Lemnos Labs, Inc. is an early-stage deeptech venture capital firm that invests at the earliest phases of hardware company formation, helping founders better understand their customer, anticipate problems, and leverage their assets. Lemnos contributes engineering, manufacturing, marketing, and financial capital alongside the check, and deliberately keeps a minimal public presence — its site is a single page that lists only the active portfolio. That portfolio spans robotics and autonomy (Built Robotics, Fort Robotics, Path Robotics, Scythe Robotics, Simbe Robotics, Petra), agricultural technology (FarmWise, Ceres Imaging), autonomous cargo aviation (Elroy Air), space data and precise positioning (Spire, Swift Navigation), simulation (Duality), video analytics (Lumeo), and physical security (Rhombus). Lemnos itself publishes no API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification; it is catalogued in the API Evangelist network as a venture-capital entity whose value to the network is its portfolio graph — several of its companies are meaningful API providers in their own right.

providers.name: Transphorm
providers.description: Transphorm was a GaN (gallium nitride) power-semiconductor company based in Goleta, California, known for its GaN-on-Si cascode FET technology used in power supplies, fast chargers, motor drives, solar inverters, and EV charging. It was acquired by Renesas Electronics in June 2024, and transphormusa.com now redirects to the Renesas GaN power-discretes product line. Transphorm publishes no public web API surface.

providers.name: Twolabs
providers.description: Twolabs is a San Francisco robotics startup (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) building Tobi, a modular humanoid robot platform for builders to collect data, train skills, and deploy autonomous robots. The two-founder company vertically integrates hardware and AI in-house, streamlining robot training into a Record, Upload, Train, Deploy workflow, and is initially focused on caregiving applications in senior-care facilities such as feeding, dressing, medication reminders, mobility support, and companionship. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company; it does not yet publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Jewelbots
providers.description: Jewelbots makes smart, codable friendship bracelets designed to teach kids (primarily tween girls) to code. The wearable is an Arduino-compatible, Bluetooth Low Energy device built on a Nordic nRF chipset that friends can program with an Arduino IDE library and firmware, with a companion iOS/Android app for pairing and messaging. The project is largely open source: the Jewelbots GitHub organization publishes the Arduino library, firmware, companion app, and hardware/toolchain repositories. Jewelbots was a 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio company; jewelbots.com now runs as a Shopify storefront. It is a hardware/firmware and education company rather than a web API provider, and exposes no first-party public HTTP/OpenAPI API.

providers.name: Oculus VR
providers.description: Oculus VR is the pioneering virtual reality company founded in 2012 and acquired by Facebook (now Meta) in 2014. Its Rift, Go, and Quest headsets defined consumer VR, and the Oculus brand has since been folded into Meta Quest and Meta Horizon OS. The former developer.oculus.com and oculus.com properties now redirect to Meta's developer platform. There is no distinct public REST/OpenAPI surface; developers build against SDK-based tooling (Unity, Unreal Engine, native OpenXR, and the Meta Spatial SDK) rather than a hosted web API. Backed originally by a16z; consumer VR/AR hardware and platform.

providers.name: Rfmd
providers.description: RFMD (RF Micro Devices) was a semiconductor manufacturer of radio-frequency (RF) components for mobile, infrastructure, defense, and aerospace markets. In January 2015 RFMD merged with TriQuint Semiconductor to form Qorvo, and the rfmd.com domain now redirects to qorvo.com. Qorvo designs and manufactures RF and power solutions — amplifiers, filters, integrated circuits, wireless connectivity, and power management devices — spanning mobile, defense/aerospace, network infrastructure, IoT, automotive, and consumer electronics. As a hardware semiconductor company, RFMD/Qorvo publishes no public developer web API; its developer-facing resources are simulation models, QSPICE circuit-simulation software, datasheets, evaluation boards, and a technical support forum. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio lead of norwest-venture-partners and enriched to reflect the RFMD-to-Qorvo identity; there is no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Astral Systems
providers.description: Astral Systems is a fusion-technology company based in Bristol, United Kingdom, developing Multi-State Fusion (MSF) reactors that produce high-flux neutron sources on demand. Co-founded by Talmon Firestone (CEO) and Dr. Tom Wallace-Smith (CTO), the company applies compact, modular fusion to near-term problems: large-scale medical isotope production to address the global isotope shortage affecting cancer diagnosis and treatment, spent fission fuel analysis, neutronics research, industrial neutron irradiation and accelerated lifetime testing, materials-damage testing, nuclear-waste burnup, and hybrid fission/fusion power. It is a Speedinvest deep-tech portfolio company. Astral Systems is a hardware/deep-tech provider and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specifications.

providers.name: Attotude
providers.description: AttoTude is a semiconductor and data-center infrastructure company building the first wired terahertz (THz) interconnect for AI and hyperscale networking. Its platform pairs the AttoEngine, an ASIC-based THz radio built on standard CMOS manufacturing, with AttoWire, a low-loss dielectric waveguide that carries 200/400/800 Gbit/s per lane over reaches up to roughly 40 meters, delivering the bandwidth density of optics without the cost, power, and complexity of photonics. Founded to relieve the interconnect bottleneck in everything-to-everything AI clusters, the company has raised roughly $143M across seed, Series A, Series B, and Series C rounds. This is a hardware company with no public API, developer portal, or SDK; the profile below is enriched only with the identity and domain-security facts the pipeline could verify.

providers.name: Mainspring Energy
providers.description: Mainspring Energy is a power generation company that designs and manufactures the Linear Generator, a fuel-flexible, dispatchable distributed power system that converts natural gas, biogas, propane, or hydrogen directly into electricity through a low-temperature, flameless reaction. The modular, factory-built systems deliver firm, flexible onsite power with near-zero NOx emissions and roughly 46% electrical efficiency across deployment scales, targeting data centers, utilities, enterprises, and industrial operations. Mainspring is a venture-backed hardware and energy-infrastructure company (backed by DCVC and General Catalyst) and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDK; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Monumental
providers.description: Monumental builds autonomous construction robots and the software that runs them. Its robots lay bricks and blockwork on real building sites, coordinated by Monumental's software platform (Atrium) and fleet operations (Fleet). The venture-backed company operates across the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, and the United States, and has raised multiple funding rounds (including a reported $32M raise and Series B rounds in the US and UK). Monumental was surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation - this record captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Solestial
providers.description: Solestial is a space solar energy company developing space-stable silicon photovoltaics — radiation-hardened, ultrathin flexible silicon heterojunction solar cells and modules for spacecraft. Its products are the only solar products on the market that self-cure radiation damage at operating temperatures, offering competitive performance at lower cost than III-V multijunction solar. Solestial has flight heritage across multiple spacecraft and works with customers including NASA, Boeing, and the U.S. Space Force. This is a hardware and manufacturing company with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Avnet
providers.description: Avnet is a global technology distributor and solutions provider that delivers electronic components, embedded solutions, and design and supply chain services to industrial and commercial customers.

providers.name: CMC Materials
providers.description: CMC Materials is a global supplier of consumable materials primarily to the semiconductor industry, including chemical mechanical planarization (CMP) slurries and polishing pads. Acquired by Entegris in 2022, CMC's materials portfolio is now part of the Entegris specialty chemicals and CMP solutions business, serving semiconductor manufacturers through advanced materials and process technologies.

providers.name: Majestic Labs
providers.description: Majestic Labs is a semiconductor and AI-infrastructure company building power-efficient AI servers that put memory first. Its rearchitected server uses custom chips that disaggregate memory from compute, giving processors direct access to a massive uniform, high-bandwidth memory pool (reportedly up to 128 TB per server and roughly 1000x more memory available to compute than a conventional design). The company claims a single Majestic rack can hold the memory capacity of about 25 Nvidia NVL72-class racks while consuming a fraction of the power, targeting frontier language models, agentic and reasoning AI, graph neural networks, and video generation. Founded by Ofer Shacham, Sha Rabii, and Masumi Reynders, Majestic Labs is backed by Lux Capital (2024). This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a company lead; the company does not currently publish a public developer/API surface.

providers.name: Nurotron
providers.description: Nurotron (Zhejiang Nurotron Neural Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. / 诺尔康) is a Hangzhou, China-based medical device manufacturer specializing in neural electrical stimulation. Its self-developed neural-prosthesis and neuromodulation product lines span auditory reconstruction (cochlear implants and speech processors such as the CS-10A/CS-20A/CS-30A implant bodies and Airum/NSP processors), visual reconstruction, urological and pelvic-nerve disease treatment, and brain neuromodulation. The company runs a corporate marketing and patient-support website with product, technical-support, rehabilitation-community, and news sections. It is a hardware medical-device company and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or machine-readable API surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for tracking.

providers.name: Eltek
providers.description: Eltek is a Norwegian power-electronics and telecom power-systems manufacturer (DC power rectifiers, industrial and telecom energy systems, the Flatpack product family) now operating as part of Delta Electronics. Its primary domain eltek.com 301-redirects to Delta's standard telecom power solutions catalog (www.delta-emea.com). This is a physical-hardware brand: no independent developer portal, public API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or well-known discovery surface was found. Surfaced as a portfolio-lead stub via the sierra-ventures VC pipeline; profile retained for domain-security signal and future re-check.

providers.name: Marvell Technology
providers.description: Marvell Technology, Inc. is a Fortune 500 fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Santa Clara, California. The company designs and develops data infrastructure semiconductor solutions including custom ASICs, data processing units, Ethernet controllers, optical and copper PHYs, switches, and storage controllers used in data centers, enterprise networking, carrier infrastructure, automotive, and consumer markets. This repository captures any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts associated with Marvell. Public developer documentation is gated behind a customer support portal and is not openly accessible.

providers.name: Sygaldry
providers.description: Sygaldry Technologies builds quantum-accelerated AI servers — augmenting classical data-center infrastructure with quantum processors purpose-built for AI to deliver exponential speedups on specific training and inference tasks. Founded in 2024 in Ann Arbor, Michigan by Chad Rigetti (founder of Rigetti Computing), Idalia Friedson, and Michael Keiser, the company combines multiple qubit types within a single fault-tolerant architecture to accelerate model training, fine-tuning, and token generation while cutting compute cost and energy use. A Y Combinator Spring 2025 company, Sygaldry has raised $139M ($34M seed led by Initialized Capital and a $105M Series A led by Breakthrough Energy Ventures, with Bloomberg Beta among its investors). Sygaldry currently publishes no public developer API; this profile is maintained for API Evangelist network discovery.

providers.name: Voltron Data
providers.description: Voltron Data is a Mountain View-based data infrastructure company (founded 2021) behind Theseus, a GPU-accelerated, composable distributed SQL query engine for petabyte-scale analytics and AI pipelines, distributed embedded through partners rather than as a self-serve public API. The company is a major steward of the open-source composable data stack — Apache Arrow, Ibis, Substrait, Arrow Flight SQL, and ADBC — acquired Claypot AI in January 2024, and is backed by Battery Ventures, GV, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Walden Catalyst, with an Accenture investment in 2025. As of 2026-07-21 the company website (voltrondata.com) is unreachable — the domain is registered but its DNS zone is lame-delegated — leaving the GitHub organization as the live public surface; no public API, SDK packages, or developer portal are published.

providers.name: Acacia
providers.description: Acacia (Acacia Communications) is a coherent optical networking company, an early Matrix Partners portfolio company that was acquired by Cisco. Acacia designs and manufactures high-speed coherent optical interconnect solutions built on silicon photonics, low-power DSP, and 3D siliconization, including performance-optimized modules (AC1200, CIM 8), MSA pluggable modules (CFP, CFP2, OSFP, QSFP-DD, QSFP28), and client optics components (PAM4 DSP, optical engines). These power AI scale-out and scale-across fabrics, data center interconnect, metro and long-haul networks, submarine cables, access and cable networks, and space communications. Acacia is a hardware/components provider and does not publish a public developer API or programmatic platform.

providers.name: Astro Mechanica
providers.description: Astro Mechanica is a San Francisco aerospace company, founded in 2021 by Ian Brooke, reinventing supersonic flight for a new jet age. Its flagship Duality electric combined-cycle engine is engineered to stay efficient from takeoff through Mach 3+ by reconfiguring between turbofan, turbojet, and ramjet modes using a hybrid turboelectric architecture. The company designs engines, airframes, and flight systems in-house, has been selected to develop an engine for the U.S. Air Force Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) program, and is backed by a16z, Lowercarbon Capital, and Y Combinator. It was added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company. As an aerospace hardware manufacturer, Astro Mechanica publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures the company's public web and identity surface only.

providers.name: Ateios
providers.description: Ateios Systems is an Indianapolis-based advanced battery manufacturer that produces high-energy, recyclable, PFA-free battery electrodes for global battery makers. Its proprietary RaiCure platform is a solvent-free, cure-on-command coating process using energy-curable polymers instead of solvent-based thermal drying, enabling thicker electrodes (>10 mAh/cm2), higher energy density, and roughly 5x faster coating throughput at lower cost and emissions. Ateios targets medical device, IoT, mobility, and defense markets. Founded in 2017 and backed by Techstars, TitletownTech, Good Growth Capital and others, the company is a materials/hardware manufacturer and publishes no developer API, SDK, or programmatic developer platform.

providers.name: ATMI Sales
providers.description: ATMI Sales (Advanced Technical Marketing Inc.) is a manufacturers' representative and technical sales firm serving the electronics and semiconductor industry across the Pacific Northwest and Western Canada. The company connects customers with component suppliers through a research, development, and build model — identifying suitable technology solutions, building supplier relationships, and ensuring component availability and supply-chain sourcing in the regions where products are manufactured. ATMI maintains a line card of partner technologies and works with distributors to fulfill orders. This is a non-developer B2B sales and distribution company; it publishes no public API, SDK, or developer program. Surfaced as a portfolio company of sierra-ventures and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Atom Semiconductor
providers.description: Atom Semiconductor (Atom Semiconductor Technologies Limited) is a fabless mixed-signal chip design company founded in Hong Kong in October 2020, with offices in Shenzhen and Shanghai. It designs high-performance analog and mixed-signal semiconductors for consumer and industrial IoT systems across three product lines: digital sensor chips (temperature/humidity, pressure, optical), analog-to-digital converters (24-bit Sigma-Delta, high-precision SAR, and high-speed GSPS ADCs), and microprocessors. Its first product, the AS1412 24-bit Sigma-Delta ADC, shipped for customer trials in late 2021. The company raised roughly 100M yuan in a pre-A round led by Qiming Venture Partners (with Venus Medtech and Alibaba Entrepreneurs Fund) and was named to the Forbes Asia 100 To Watch 2022. It is a hardware chip designer and does not publish a developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Axera Tech
providers.description: Axera Intelligence (爱芯元智), operating as Axera Tech, is a Chinese fabless semiconductor company building AI-inference SoCs for edge and endpoint computing. Its chips pair the Axera Tongyuan mixed-precision NPU with the Axera Zhimu AI-ISP to power on-device vision perception, smart-vehicle autonomous-driving and intelligent-cabin platforms, and multi-tier edge-AI inference across IoT and industrial scenarios. Axera Tech was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners; it is a hardware/silicon provider and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Calxeda
providers.description: Calxeda was an Austin, Texas semiconductor startup — founded in 2008 as Smooth-Stone by Barry Evans, Larry Wikelius and David Borland — that built ARM-based EnergyCore system-on-chip server processors (ECX-1000, ECX-2000/Midway) aimed at low-power, high-density data center workloads. It raised roughly $90-103M from venture investors including Battery Ventures, and its silicon shipped in Boston Limited Viridis appliances and HP Project Moonshot systems. Calxeda ceased operations in December 2013 after a refinancing round fell through, and its ARM server IP resurfaced under Silver Lining Systems in December 2014. The company published no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts, and calxeda.com is now a parked domain listed for sale, so there is no live API surface for the API Evangelist network to catalog.

providers.name: CIX Technology
providers.description: CIX Technology (此芯科技) is a Chinese fabless semiconductor company founded in 2021 that designs high-performance, general-purpose heterogeneous intelligent CPU chips for AI computing. The company builds low-power, high-efficiency compute platforms spanning personal computing (PC), vehicle/automotive computing, and edge computing, and partners across the Arm ecosystem (Arm, Arm China, Lenovo and others). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm qiming and added to the API Evangelist network. CIX is a silicon/hardware company and publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal at this time; this profile captures its verifiable public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Coolso
providers.description: Coolso develops wearable gesture-recognition technology. Using patented sensing that detects muscle-vibration signals processed through its own AI model, Coolso recognizes individual finger movements and strength levels with low-latency response, from a wrist-worn device or an ordinary smartwatch's accelerometer and gyroscope without dedicated hardware. Founded by Sheng-Kuei Hsu, Wei-Lin Lee, and Jack Wu and based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, the seed-stage company is backed by 500 Global and Alchemist Accelerator and targets AR/VR interaction, with potential expansion into medical rehabilitation and sports equipment. Coolso publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Daqstra
providers.description: Daqstra is an AI-native operating platform for complex test infrastructure, giving aerospace, energy, and robotics teams observability and orchestration for the physical world. The platform connects data-acquisition hardware (National Instruments, PLCs, and custom equipment) at the edge, centralizes and versions test data in the cloud, and orchestrates hardware sequences and test logic as code through Python and REST APIs. Daqstra Edge streams live signals from physical hardware, Daqstra Hub (Strata Hub) organizes test-campaign data with AI-powered insight, and the Daqstra API lets engineers drive test runs programmatically instead of through manual CSV workflows. The company was founded by aerospace-propulsion and avionics engineers and is backed by Y Combinator (S26 batch).

providers.name: Epirus
providers.description: Epirus is a Torrance, California-based defense technology company building solid-state, software-defined high-power microwave (HPM) directed-energy systems for counter-electronics and counter-unmanned-aerial-systems (cUAS) missions. Its flagship product is Leonidas, a non-kinetic HPM weapon system designed to defeat single drones and large drone swarms by disabling their onboard electronics, with a growing product family that includes Leonidas IFPC-HPM (Indirect Fire Protection Capability — High-Power Microwave) for the U.S. Army, Leonidas Expeditionary (ExDECS) for the U.S. Marine Corps, Leonidas H2O for maritime interdiction, the portable Leonidas Pod, and Stryker Leonidas (with General Dynamics Land Systems). Epirus also collaborates with Anduril, Northrop Grumman, L3Harris, Kodiak AI, Peraton, and Palantir, and has received contracts from the U.S. Army, U.S. Air Force, U.S. Navy, DARPA, ONR, and Singapore's DSTA. The company is privately held, has raised more than $550M across Series B/C/D, and operates under CMMC Level 2 certification. Its product surface is classified defense hardware and embedded firmware — there is no public developer portal, REST API, SDK, or open-source software offering.

providers.name: Fabheads
providers.description: Fabheads is a carbon fiber and composite manufacturing company (Fabheads Automation) that delivers end-to-end composite product development — design, analysis, tooling, prototyping, and production — using its own fiber-printing and automated-layup technology alongside traditional craftsmanship. It serves aerospace, mobility, marine, robotics, medical, and sports customers from aerospace-grade facilities, and publishes the C6 Slicer tool for composite fiber printing. Backed by Accel. As a hardware manufacturer it exposes no public developer API; this profile captures identity and domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: finern
providers.description: Finern (Finern Automation) is a China-based industrial automation company that designs and builds fully automated production lines and intelligent measurement systems for manufacturing. It serves five sectors — automotive, electronics, new energy (battery/EV), healthcare/pharmaceutical equipment, and consumer goods — with automated assembly, testing, and inspection systems. The company reports 600+ personnel, 30,000+ square meters of facilities, 100+ global clients, 8 international sites, and 4 R&D centers. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Finern publishes a corporate marketing website but does not currently expose any public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable discovery surface (no /.well-known/*, llms.txt, or OpenAPI found on probe).

providers.name: Gokin
providers.description: Gokin Solar Co., Ltd. (高景太阳能股份有限公司) is a Chinese photovoltaic manufacturer founded in 2019 and headquartered in Jiangsu, China. The company produces monocrystalline silicon ingots and wafers (N-type and P-type) and high-efficiency solar modules (GOKIN BC and FLAMINGO series), operating four major production bases with roughly 100 GW of wafer and 16 GW of module annual capacity. Ranked among the top three global silicon-wafer shippers, Gokin employs 6,000+ people, holds 500+ patents, and serves utility, commercial, and residential solar projects across 30+ countries. Backed by IDG Capital, Gokin is a solar-hardware manufacturer with a corporate marketing website and no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Holo
providers.description: Holo (Holo AM, operating under Greene Group Industries) is an advanced metal additive manufacturing company founded in 2017 and backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners. Its PureForm metal 3D printing platform uses digital light processing (DLP) with metal powder-filled photopolymer resins to produce high-resolution, complex metal components with features as small as 50 microns, in pure copper, stainless steels (17-4PH, 316), and in-development cobalt alloy, titanium, nickel superalloys, tool steels, and alumina. Customers submit CAD files and receive prototyped-to-production parts with roughly two-week turnaround, serving medical technology, precision micro-robotics, and general advanced manufacturing. Holo is a hardware manufacturer and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: LiquidLight
providers.description: LiquidLight, Inc. (Liquid Light) was an electrochemistry company based in Monmouth Junction, New Jersey that developed and licensed process technology for converting carbon dioxide into industrial chemicals. Founded in 2009 by Kyle Teamey, Emily Cole, Andrew Bocarsly, Fouad Elnaggar and Nety Krishna around technology licensed from Princeton University, the company built a portfolio of more than 100 patents covering the electrochemical production of chemicals including monoethylene glycol (MEG), propylene and acetic acid, with MEG as its lead target market. It raised seed funding from Redpoint Ventures and a $15 million Series B in September 2014 from investors including VantagePoint Capital Partners and BP Ventures, and was also a Battery Ventures portfolio investment. Avantium acquired Liquid Light on January 10, 2017 and the company ceased operating independently. LiquidLight was a materials and process-technology company: it never published a public API, developer portal, SDKs or any machine-readable developer surface, and no company web property survives the acquisition. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an accurate, non-API portfolio record.

providers.name: Nlight
providers.description: nLIGHT, Inc. (NASDAQ: LASR) is a US-based designer and manufacturer of high-power semiconductor and fiber lasers, optical fibers, and beam-control systems. For more than 25 years the company has served mission-critical directed-energy and defense, sensing, and advanced-manufacturing markets (cutting, welding, additive, medical, and battery production) from a vertically integrated stack spanning semiconductor chips to complete laser systems, with a portfolio of over 450 patents and design and manufacturing based in Camas, Washington. nLIGHT is a hardware and photonics company and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Orbital Arc
providers.description: Orbital Arc is a Houston-based deep-tech spacecraft propulsion startup founded in 2023 by Jonathan Huffman, building Gas-Phase Field Effect Electric Propulsion (Gas FEEP) thrusters and the RIOT Drive (Relativistic Ion Thrust Drive) for satellites and in-space transportation. Its ultra-lightweight electric thrusters use solid naphthalene fuel that sublimates at room temperature instead of noble gases, targeting high specific impulse for satellite constellations.
