Backed by Techstars and Capital Factory, the company completed a sub-scale physics demonstration at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (TRL 3). This is a hardware company with no public API, SDK, or developer surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: PicoJool
providers.description: PicoJool is an optical connectivity company building Vertical Cavity Surface Emitting Lasers (VCSELs) and optical engines for AI and cloud data-center infrastructure. Its 50G NRZ, 100G PAM4, and 200G PAM4 VCSEL arrays target 800G and 1.6T transceivers for PCIe, Ethernet, and InfiniBand, aiming to raise bandwidth density and cut the power cost of moving data across hyperscale AI clusters. Founded in 2024 and based in Palo Alto, California, PicoJool emerged from stealth in November 2025 with $12M led by Playground Global. It is a semiconductor/photonics hardware company with no public API or developer platform; this profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network for portfolio and market tracking.

providers.name: Quantumdiamonds
providers.description: QuantumDiamonds (QD) is a Munich-based German deep-tech company that develops diamond-based quantum sensing systems for semiconductor inspection and failure analysis. The company markets what it describes as the world's first commercially available quantum sensing system for semiconductor inspection, using nitrogen-vacancy (NV) diamond quantum microscopy to detect defects and current-flow anomalies that traditional inspection methods miss. QuantumDiamonds is a portfolio company of the venture firm Earlybird and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. As a quantum hardware and instrumentation company, it does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web presence and company identity.

providers.name: Quintessent
providers.description: Quintessent is a Goleta, California deep-tech photonics company developing quantum dot laser and optical interconnect technology to scale computing and AI infrastructure. The company builds quantum dot epitaxial wafer supply chains (in partnership with IQE) and optical connectivity solutions for AI optical interconnects, targeting the bandwidth and energy-efficiency bottlenecks of next-generation data centers. Backed by Sierra Ventures, Quintessent is a hardware and semiconductor company; as of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API documentation.

providers.name: Sagence AI
providers.description: Sagence AI is a semiconductor company building analog in-memory computing hardware for AI inference. Its "analog inference machine" combines deep subthreshold computing with multi-level flash memory cells to run large AI models at a fraction of the power and cost of conventional digital GPUs, targeting datacenter and edge workloads such as generative AI, recommendation systems, real-time defect detection, and video security. Backed by Khosla Ventures, the company positions its technology against offerings like Nvidia's B200, claiming large gains in performance-per-watt and cost efficiency for AI inference. Sagence AI is a hardware/silicon company and does not currently publish a developer API, SDK, or public developer portal.

providers.name: The Exploration Company
providers.description: The Exploration Company GmbH is a European space transportation startup building reusable space vehicles "for humanity." Its flagship program, Nyx, is a reusable capsule designed to carry cargo and, eventually, crew between Earth and low Earth orbit destinations such as commercial space stations, featuring orbital propulsion, autonomous docking, and re-entry recovery. The company is also developing Storm, a high-thrust reusable rocket engine (up to 180 tons of thrust) built through European partnerships toward a globally competitive launcher. Backed by Balderton Capital and a certified B Corp, it markets itself as one of the fastest-growing space startups in the world. The company operates a marketing and careers web presence but publishes no public developer program, API, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts at this time. Surfaced as a Balderton Capital portfolio company and enriched in the API Evangelist network with verified identity and domain-security signals.

providers.name: VXB Aerospace
providers.description: VXB Aerospace is an Australian space technology company founded in 2022 by Alexander Ryan, developing generative design software and Hall-effect plasma propulsion for the satellite market. Its platform automates the design, manufacturability analysis, multi-physics modeling and validation of complex aerospace hardware such as propulsion systems, antennas and satellite layouts, while its ZEPHYR-35 Hall-effect thruster (Argon/Krypton/Xenon) provides in-orbit mobility, refueling, servicing and de-orbiting. The company was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio lead and enriched in the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Apollo Atomics Inc
providers.description: Apollo Atomics is a Y Combinator-backed (Spring 2026 / P26) nuclear technology company building compact, power-dense pressurized water reactors for electricity generation, industrial process heat, and data-center power. Founded by Assil Halimi and Drew Walker and based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, the company modifies the steam generator of proven pressurized water reactor technology to shrink the plant by roughly an order of magnitude without sacrificing power output, turning a decade-long construction project into a factory-built machine that can ship on a truck. Apollo has announced a research collaboration with MIT's Department of Nuclear Science and Engineering to validate its reactor design and has submitted a regulatory engagement plan to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission, targeting a construction permit application in 2028. This is a hardware/energy company with no public developer or API surface at this time.

providers.name: Velaura
providers.description: Velaura AI, Inc. (formerly Auradine) is a Santa Clara, California deep-tech company delivering proven, breakthrough, ultra-low-power compute for cloud, edge, and physical AI applications. Its Titan Core silicon design and IP platform helps AI compute platforms cut power for arithmetic operations while maintaining performance, and its Teraflux line covers high-efficiency Bitcoin mining hardware, ASICs, containers, and fleet-management software. Founded in 2022 by veterans from Qualcomm, Marvell, NVIDIA, Intel, Apple, Google, and Palo Alto Networks, Velaura is backed by Mayfield, Celesta Capital, Mara, StepStone, Maverick Capital, and Premji Invest. As a semiconductor and infrastructure company it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Asetek
providers.description: Asetek designs and builds liquid cooling and thermal-management technology. Founded in 2000 and headquartered in Aalborg, Denmark, the company pioneered all-in-one (AIO) closed-loop liquid coolers for enthusiast and gaming PCs and supplies OEM cooling to major PC and workstation brands. Its data-center and high-performance-computing business delivers direct-to-chip liquid cooling for servers and racks, and its Asetek SimSports division makes premium sim-racing hardware such as force-feedback wheelbases and load-cell pedals. Asetek is a hardware manufacturer and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and enriched with what is publicly verifiable (domain-security posture).

providers.name: Cassie
providers.description: Cassie (Aircassie) develops advanced air filtration technology for healthcare and indoor environments. Its flagship CASSIE system uses patented filtration to eliminate mold, viruses, and bacteria with zero harmful emissions, contrasting with UV and ionizer systems that emit ozone. The company markets 99.9% effectiveness against viruses and bacteria, a 59-second disinfection cycle, and 24-hour air quality monitoring with real-time data. Cassie is a hardware and environmental-technology company backed by Techstars; it was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. As of this enrichment pass it publishes a marketing website (Wix) with no public API, developer documentation, SDKs, or other machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: Datost
providers.description: Datost Inc. is a New York applied research lab building hardware and intelligent systems that operate in your environment without demanding constant attention — "computers that come after the screen." Its first public product is ED1TH, a 25-gram pair of AI augmented-reality smart glasses with a 640x480 green Micro-LED in-lens display readable in direct sunlight, hot-swap battery cells, a companion steel smart ring for gesture control, and a privacy-first design with zero cameras and a single hardware-mutable microphone. ED1TH runs ED1TH-OS and handles email, calendar, turn-by-turn navigation, live translation, and meeting transcription in the wearer's field of view. Datost is backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026) and OpenAI. As a consumer hardware and applied-research company, Datost does not currently publish a public web API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Diablo Technologies
providers.description: Diablo Technologies Inc. was an enterprise memory technology company backed by Battery Ventures. It developed Memory Channel Storage (MCS), an architecture that placed flash storage directly on the DDR memory bus, and productized it as Memory1, a flash-as-DRAM DIMM the company marketed as delivering up to 256 GB of memory per module and 4 TB per dual-socket server. Diablo positioned itself as a silicon and module vendor selling through server and storage OEM partners rather than as a software or platform company: it never published a public API, developer portal, SDK, or any machine-readable specification, and no developer surface appears anywhere in the archived record of its website. The company appears to be defunct. Its corporate site is last archived intact in 2017, the domain subsequently served unrelated SEO spam, the diablo-technologies.com registration lapsed and was re-registered on 2023-10-08 through a different registrar, and the hostname today serves an unrelated consumer-gadget review blog with no connection to the memory business. No GitHub organization exists under either diablo-technologies or diablotechnologies. This profile is retained as a historical company record with no API surface.

providers.name: Helion Energy
providers.description: Helion Energy is an Everett, Washington fusion power company building commercial fusion electricity generators using a pulsed, magneto-inertial field-reversed configuration (FRC) approach burning deuterium and helium-3. Helion forms two FRC plasmas at opposite ends of its machine, accelerates them toward each other, merges them, and uses pulsed magnetic compression to drive them to fusion conditions; the expanding plasma pushes against the confining magnetic field and induces current directly back into the machine's capacitor bank via Faraday's Law, recapturing electricity without a steam cycle. Founded in 2013 by David Kirtley, John Slough, Chris Pihl, and George Votroubek, Helion is chaired by Sam Altman and has progressed through seven generations of prototypes (IPA, Venti, Trenta, and most recently Polaris) on its way to commercial generators. Polaris, brought online in late 2024, is the company's seventh-generation machine and the first privately developed fusion device to demonstrate measurable deuterium-tritium fusion, reaching 150 million degrees Celsius in February 2026. In May 2023, Helion signed the world's first commercial fusion power purchase agreement, committing to deliver 50 MWe to Microsoft starting in 2028, with the Orion plant planned for the Malaga, Washington area; a subsequent agreement with Nucor targets a 500-MWe facility. Helion is funded by Sam Altman, SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Nucor, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and others, with a reported $5.4B valuation as of early 2025. The company's revenue model is fusion electricity sales under long-term PPAs; Helion has no public developer API, SDK, or open-source software product, and its public GitHub organization (Helion-Energy) contains only forks of plasma-physics simulation tools (WarpX, FerroX, pyamrex, maestrowf).

providers.name: Ion Mobility
providers.description: ION Mobility is a Singapore-headquartered technology and automotive company that designs and builds affordable, zero-emission smart electric motorcycles for riders across Southeast Asia, with its flagship M1-S model and a companion rider mobile app. The company combines advanced hardware and software with human-centred design, spanning electric two-wheelers and energy charging and storage solutions, with additional offices in Jakarta and Shenzhen and backing from investors including 500 Global. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public developer and identity surface; ION Mobility currently publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI specification, operating a consumer waitlist/test-ride site and an internal open-source tooling estate on GitHub.

providers.name: MatX
providers.description: MatX is an AI-hardware company designing specialized semiconductors optimized for large language model workloads. Its flagship MatX One chip targets high-throughput, low-latency training, inference, and reinforcement learning for large dense and Mixture-of-Experts models, storing weights in SRAM to cut latency and reaching over 2,000 output tokens per second on large models. MatX is a hardware and research company with no public developer API surface; this profile captures its identity, research/blog output, open-source codebases, and domain-security posture. Backed by Jane Street, Spark Capital, and Situational Awareness LP.

providers.name: Moxion Power
providers.description: Moxion Power was a Richmond, California-based mobile battery energy storage (BESS) company founded in 2020 that designed, manufactured, and deployed large-scale mobile lithium-iron-phosphate battery units (the MP-75 and related platforms) intended to displace diesel generators across construction sites, film and television production, live events, utility work, and emergency response. The company built a 40,000 square-foot factory in Richmond, raised approximately $100 million in a Series B at a reported $1.5 billion valuation led by Tamarack Global with participation from Amazon's Climate Pledge Fund and Microsoft's Climate Innovation Fund, and signed a multi-year fleet partnership with Sunbelt Rentals. After delivering 400+ units it announced cessation of operations on July 29, 2024, laid off its entire workforce, and filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy in the District of Delaware in August 2024 with approximately $201,980 in cash on hand and estimated liabilities of $100M–$500M. In September–October 2024, Viridi Parente acquired Moxion's Richmond facility, battery inventory, intellectual property, patents, and the Sunbelt Rentals relationship through the bankruptcy auction for approximately $7 million. Moxion Power had no public developer API, SDK, or open source release; its GitHub organization (github.com/moxion-power) contains zero public repositories. This profile is preserved for historical reference.

providers.name: petkit
providers.description: PetKit is a consumer smart pet-technology company that designs and sells connected pet-care hardware — automated feeders, smart water fountains, self-cleaning litter boxes, cameras, and health-monitoring accessories — paired with the PetKit mobile app that controls the devices over the cloud. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm qiming and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass, PetKit publishes no dedicated first-party developer portal or public API; petkit.com is operated as a Shopify storefront, so the only machine discoverable surface on the domain is Shopify's Customer Account OAuth/OIDC discovery documents. Third-party (community, reverse-engineered) integrations exist for the mobile-app backend but there is no officially documented API.

providers.name: Qphox
providers.description: QphoX is a Delft, Netherlands-based quantum technology company founded in 2021 and spun out of Delft University of Technology (TU Delft). It develops quantum networking hardware to tackle the scaling challenges of quantum computing, centered on its Quantum Transducer, described as the first quantum interface between single optical and single microwave photons, enabling optical interconnects between superconducting quantum processors. Alongside the transducer, QphoX offers an Optical Control System for delivering RF signals into extreme cryogenic environments and a CryoSwitch Control Module for use with Radiall's cryogenic latching actuator. The company publishes open-source Python instrument-control libraries (QCoDeS drivers) on GitHub for operating its hardware. QphoX is backed by Speedinvest. QphoX exposes no public web API or developer portal.

providers.name: Snowcap Compute
providers.description: Snowcap Compute is building the world's first commercial superconducting computing platform, operating at 4.5 Kelvin to deliver breakthrough energy efficiency and performance for AI and data-center workloads. Launched in June 2025 with $23 million in seed funding led by Playground Global, the company is developing superconducting chips and systems aimed at the next era of AI and quantum-adjacent compute. As a hardware and deep-tech company it publishes a marketing and careers presence but no public API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: Zibra Labs
providers.description: Zibra Labs is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) startup building distributed compute infrastructure for AI workloads at scale. The platform gives teams access to the cheapest CPUs and GPUs across hyperscalers and neoclouds, orchestrating clusters of 100 to 50,000 mixed hardware nodes with sub-50ms task-dispatch overhead and millions of parallel tasks on spot instances across regions. Target workloads include quantitative-trading backtesting and parameter sweeps, AI post-training and reinforcement-learning pipelines, multi-modal data processing, batch and high-volume inference, and long-horizon agentic workflows. The founding team previously built three LinkedIn databases (Venice, Liquid, Espresso) and were tech leads on the open-source Ray compute framework. As of this profile Zibra Labs publishes only a corporate marketing site; no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs are available yet.

providers.name: XtalPi
providers.description: XtalPi is an AI-and-quantum-physics drug discovery and materials research platform company with headquarters in Cambridge, Massachusetts and major operations in Beijing, Shanghai, and Shenzhen, publicly listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange under stock code 2228.HK. The company combines a hybrid AI plus quantum mechanics (QM) discovery engine with large-scale robotic laboratory automation to accelerate molecular research and development for pharmaceutical, agrochemical, and materials customers, including engagements with Pfizer, Eli Lilly, and Novartis. XtalPi's offering spans proprietary software platforms — PatSight for patent extraction, XFEP for free-energy perturbation binding-affinity prediction, XMolGen for generative chemistry, and XtalGazer for solid-state research — and intelligent automation hardware including the XmartChem intelligent synthesis workstation and ChemPlus desktop solid dispenser. Its drug discovery services cover hit discovery, hit/lead optimization, biology capabilities, focused library synthesis, and the PepiX peptide platform, complemented by sister brands Ailux (biology) and AiFChem (chemistry). XtalPi's products are delivered as enterprise collaborations, licensed software, and CRO-style services; there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release.

providers.name: Amca
providers.description: Amca (Advanced Manufacturing Company of America) is an El Segundo, California aerospace and defense manufacturer rebuilding America's industrial base by acquiring specialized component suppliers and expanding competition and capacity for critical parts — actuators, switches, hydraulics, pressure sensors, power electronics, and flight-control electronics. Founded in 2024 by Eli Giovanetti and Jai Malik, Amca combines design, testing, and production into a single RAPID platform across a network of AS9100D-certified factories (Electro-Mech Components, Electrocube, Aerospace Control Products, Payne Magnetics, Cal-Draulics, BC Power Systems), and serves nearly every major aerospace and defense prime and Tier 1 supplier — Boeing, Lockheed Martin, Airbus, GE Aerospace, Honeywell, Textron, BAE Systems, and the Defense Logistics Agency. It is a hardware manufacturing company with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Atlas Motion Systems
providers.description: Atlas Motion Systems (atlasmotion.com) designs and builds brushless DC (BLDC) motors and actuators for defense and robotics applications, engineered around a customer's specific program and manufactured at scale. The public web presence is a single-page marketing site (hero plus a contact page); it is a hardware company that does not publish a developer portal, public API, SDKs, documentation, or well-known discovery surface. This profile was seeded as a Homebrew-portfolio lead and enriched with verifiable identity and live domain-security probe data only. Enrichment found no API surface to harvest.

providers.name: FIMI Technology
providers.description: FIMI Technology Ltd. (Beijing FIMI Technology Co., Ltd. / Shenzhen FIMI Robot Technology Co., Ltd.) is a consumer aerial-imaging hardware manufacturer founded in May 2014 as a member of the Xiaomi ecosystem. FIMI designs and sells affordable camera drones, handheld gimbal cameras, and smartphone gimbals, with a product lineup that includes the X8 series (X8 SE, X8 Pro, X8 Tele, X8T enterprise), the compact Mini 3, the Manta VTOL fixed-wing drone, and the PALM series gimbal cameras. The company holds hundreds of patents across flight control, wireless transmission links, mechatronic design, gimbal image-stabilization, and computer vision. FIMI is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. This is a consumer-electronics company with no public developer program, API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Heaviside Industries
providers.description: Heaviside Industries is a defense-technology company founded in 2024 in Los Angeles, California, building autonomous precision munitions for U.S. and allied special operations and conventional forces. Its products — MOTH (land electromagnetic signal intelligence and spectrum awareness), TYR (autonomous aerial munition), and HYDRA (autonomous underwater munition) — are designed to deliver hyper-precise strike capabilities across air, land, and sea in GPS-denied and contested environments. Named after physicist Oliver Heaviside, whose electromagnetic theory enabled miniaturized electronics, the company emerged from stealth in May 2026 with a $28M Series A. It does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: Mauna Kea Semiconductors
providers.description: Mauna Kea Semiconductors (mk-semi.com) is a Silicon Valley-based fabless semiconductor company founded by industry veterans to develop what it describes as the world's lowest-power Ultra-Wideband (UWB) solution for high precision location and direction-finding applications. Its UWB chips, modules, and integrated System-on-Chip solutions target smartphones, wearables, IoT devices, and automotive use cases, combining digital and analog/mixed-signal design expertise. Headquartered in Cupertino, California, with engineering operations in Shanghai, Beijing, and Shenzhen, the company is led by CEO Dr. Yifeng Zhang and is backed by Qiming. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Qiming; it is a hardware/silicon vendor with no public API or developer surface at this time (documentation, blog, and careers pages are marked "Coming Soon").

providers.name: Misfit
providers.description: Misfit is a consumer wearables brand — fitness trackers and smartwatches such as the Misfit Shine, Flash, Ray and Vapor — founded in 2011 by Sonny Vu, John Sculley and Sridhar Iyengar and backed by Norwest Venture Partners, Khosla Ventures, Founders Fund, GGV Capital and Xiaomi before being acquired by Fossil Group in 2015. Misfit ran a developer program (the Misfit Cloud API, Device SDK and Scientific Library) at build.misfit.com with 30+ launch partners. Fossil discontinued the Misfit backend, Cloud API and companion app in spring 2023, so the hosted API and all misfit.com domains are now unreachable. The only surviving developer surface is the official Misfit-Developers GitHub organization and its unmaintained iOS SDKs on CocoaPods.

providers.name: MOLG
providers.description: MOLG (molg.ai) is a circular manufacturing company tackling electronic waste. It operates autonomous robotic microfactories that disassemble complex devices like laptops and servers to recover components and materials for reuse, remanufacturing, and recycling. MOLG also partners with manufacturers on design-for-circularity (modular snap/press-fit/latch assembly instead of screws and adhesives) and offers OriginMark, a traceability platform for tracking devices, components, and materials across their lifecycle to calculate embodied carbon and supply-chain transparency. As of this enrichment pass MOLG publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or technical documentation; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Periodic
providers.description: Periodic (Periodic Labs) is an AI research company building "AI scientists" paired with autonomous laboratories to accelerate discovery in the physical sciences, with an early focus on materials science and higher-temperature superconductors. Their systems hypothesize, run physical experiments, and learn from the results, and they partner with industry to optimize experimental processes. Surfaced as a portfolio company of CRV and Felicis, the company is at an early stage and does not currently publish a public API, developer documentation, or developer platform. This profile records that honest result; it is not penalized for having no API surface.

providers.name: Pixcel
providers.description: PIXCEL Inc. is an early-stage deep-tech startup developing cutting-edge silicon photonics solutions and photonic integrated circuits (PICs) for optical communications and related systems. Based in Matawan, NJ, and co-founded by silicon photonics veteran Long Chen (previously at Cisco Systems and Acacia Communications), the company designs passive and active photonic components and collaborates with foundry partners to optimize process design kits (PDKs). PIXCEL is a hardware and semiconductor company with no public API, developer portal, or software product surface at this time; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of Matrix Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. This profile reflects an enrichment pass that confirmed there is no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: NuScale Power
providers.description: NuScale Power is a Portland, Oregon-based small modular reactor (SMR) company developing the NuScale Power Module (NPM), a 77 MWe pressurized light-water reactor that is the first — and to date one of only two — SMR designs to receive design approval from the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Originally certified in 2020 at 50 MWe and uprated to 77 MWe under the US460 Standard Design Approval issued by the NRC on May 29, 2025, the NPM is delivered as a factory-fabricated, rail-shippable cylindrical containment vessel using passive natural-circulation safety features. Its commercial offering, the VOYGR SMR power plant, is sold in 4-, 6-, and 12-module configurations (308, 462, and 924 MWe respectively) and is targeted at utilities, data centers, hydrogen production, district heating, desalination, and industrial process heat. NuScale traces its origins to Oregon State University research begun in 2000 and was formally founded in 2007; Fluor Corporation became majority investor in 2011. The company went public on the NYSE in 2022 (ticker SMR) through a SPAC merger with Spring Valley Acquisition Corp., becoming the first publicly traded pure-play SMR vendor. NuScale partners exclusively with ENTRA1 Energy for global commercialization and operates Energy Exploration (E2) Centers — full control-room simulators hosted at Oregon State University, Texas A&M, the University of Idaho, and SNU in South Korea — for operator and regulator training. The high-profile Utah Associated Municipal Power Systems (UAMPS) Carbon Free Power Project at Idaho National Laboratory was terminated in November 2023 after costs rose from $58 to $89/MWh and subscription targets fell short, leaving NuScale without a first-of-a-kind US deployment and prompting a focus on data-center, industrial, and international (Romania RoPower, Poland KGHM, Ghana, Standard Power) opportunities. NuScale's revenue model is power-module sales/leasing, EPC services, and plant lifecycle services — there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release. NPM design data, topical reports, and safety analysis are conveyed through NRC docket filings and topical reports rather than a developer portal.

providers.name: Pacific Fusion
providers.description: Pacific Fusion is a fusion energy company based in Fremont, California developing commercial fusion power using pulsed magnetic inertial fusion. Its modular system pairs a fast electric pulser, a meter-scale fusion chamber, and centimeter-scale fuel targets to pursue net facility gain with practical, affordable manufacturing. Building on breakthroughs from US National Laboratories (Lawrence Livermore, Sandia) and partners such as General Atomics, the company aims to deliver limitless, clean, on-demand power. Surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC, General Catalyst, and Lightspeed Venture Partners, this profile has been enriched through the API Evangelist network. Pacific Fusion is a hardware and energy company and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: AICE
providers.description: AICE is a defense-technology company building the next generation of underwater defense systems: autonomous swarms of modular marine drones that secure naval assets and coastal infrastructure against evolving underwater threats. Founded in 2026 by former NASA engineer Gregoire Chomette and European Robotics Champion Remi Bouteiller, the company is part of the Y Combinator Spring 2026 batch, is based in the San Francisco Bay Area with hardware manufactured in France, and applies swarm robotics and AI to surveillance, detection, and protection of critical subsea infrastructure. AICE currently ships hardware and does not publish a public API, SDK, or developer platform; this profile tracks the company for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Aquantia
providers.description: Aquantia Corporation was a fabless semiconductor company headquartered in San Jose, California, that designed and marketed multi-gigabit Ethernet connectivity — AQtion client network controllers, Atlantic controllers, and multi-gig PHY transceivers for enterprise, data center, automotive, and consumer networking. Aquantia was acquired by Marvell Technology in 2019; the aquantia.com domain now redirects to marvell.com. It operated no public HTTP/developer API or developer portal — its published developer surface is silicon: Linux kernel and DPDK "Atlantic" NIC drivers, firmware, and tooling in the github.com/Aquantia organization. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-lead stub; there is no API to enrich.

providers.name: Atom Computing
providers.description: Atom Computing is a Berkeley, California neutral-atom quantum computing company building large-scale, gate-based quantum computers using optically-trapped Ytterbium-171 nuclear-spin qubits. Founded in 2018 by Ben Bloom, the company became the first in the industry to exceed 1,000 qubits in a gate-based quantum computer with its second-generation platform in October 2023 (1,180 qubits across 1,225 sites). Its current commercial product, AC1000, is a universal gate-based, on-premises quantum computing system with 1,200+ physical qubits, all-to-all connectivity, mid-circuit measurement with qubit reuse and reset, real-time conditional branching, and better-than-threshold fidelities (>99.9% single-qubit, >99.6% two-qubit, >99.8% SPAM). The platform is programmable via OpenQASM and QIR (Quantum Intermediate Representation) and ships with a 20-qubit classical emulator. In January 2025 Atom Computing and Microsoft announced an on-premises 50-logical-qubit system (Magne), with additional strategic collaborations across Cisco (networked/distributed quantum, March 2026), NVIDIA NVQLink integration (March 2026), and a Letter of Intent for $100M from the U.S. Department of Commerce (May 2026). The commercial model centers on enterprise and national-lab on-premises system sales and partnerships; there is no public cloud API or self-serve developer portal — programmatic access is via the standard OpenQASM/QIR toolchains targeting customer-deployed AC1000 hardware.

providers.name: Baya Systems
providers.description: Baya Systems is a semiconductor IP company accelerating intelligent compute with chiplets. Backed by Matrix Partners and Intel Capital and based in Santa Clara, California (with offices in Austin, Texas and Bengaluru, India), Baya provides the WeaverPro software platform and the WeaveIP unified fabric and cache IP portfolio. Together they let system architects analyze, design and post-silicon tune optimal single-die or multi-die, chiplet-ready Network-on-Chip (NoC) interconnect systems, with multi-level coherency and multicast for AI acceleration scaling into petabytes per second across hyperscale, enterprise, AI, automotive, GPU and IoT markets. Baya Systems does not publish a public developer API, portal or SDK at this time; this API Evangelist network profile tracks the company as a portfolio lead awaiting a public API surface.

providers.name: Bouffalo Lab
providers.description: Bouffalo Lab (博流智能) is a fabless chip design company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Nanjing, China, focused on ultra-low-power AIoT (AI + IoT) and edge-computing system chips. Its product line centers on RISC-V based microcontrollers with integrated wireless connectivity — the BL602/BL604 (Wi-Fi 2.4G + BLE 5.0), BL702/BL704/BL706 (Zigbee 3.0 + BLE 5.0), BL606P (quad-mode dual-core Wi-Fi/BT/BLE/Zigbee), and the BL616/BL618 and BL808 families — combining wireless radios, audio/video processing, and on-device AI algorithms. The company ships the open-source BouffaloSDK (a merge of bl_mcu_sdk and bl_iot_sdk) under Apache 2.0 through its public GitHub organization, along with hardware abstraction drivers, Matter/Thread support, and NuttX RTOS ports. Bouffalo Lab is a hardware/firmware provider rather than a web-API provider; it exposes no public HTTP/REST developer API, so the enrichment pipeline captures its developer surface (GitHub SDK org) and domain security posture. It is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: Cuspai
providers.description: CuspAI is a Cambridge, UK artificial intelligence company, founded in 2024, building generative AI for materials discovery. Its platform lets users specify desired physical and chemical properties — such as selective CO2 binding — and then generates, evaluates, and optimizes candidate molecular and material structures for applications spanning carbon capture, energy storage, catalysis, water purification, electric vehicles, and healthcare. CuspAI has raised roughly $130M (a $30M seed and a $100M Series A in September 2025) from investors including Northzone and Prosus Ventures, and maintains open-source scientific computing tooling on GitHub. As of mid-2026 the company operates a placeholder marketing site with no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Cypress
providers.description: Cypress Semiconductor Corporation was a San Jose, California semiconductor company founded in 1982, and an early Mayfield venture investment. It designed and manufactured mixed-signal, embedded, and connectivity silicon — most notably the PSoC programmable system-on-chip microcontrollers, WICED Wi-Fi and Bluetooth wireless combos, USB controllers (EZ-USB), NOR flash and SRAM memory, and automotive Traveo microcontrollers — supported by the ModusToolbox and PSoC Creator developer tooling and the Cypress Developer Community. Infineon Technologies AG acquired Cypress in April 2020 for approximately 9.4 billion dollars; the business, its developer community, and its GitHub repositories have since been folded into Infineon. cypress.com now redirects to infineon.com and the developer resources live at community.infineon.com. Cypress shipped hardware SDKs and embedded toolchains rather than a public web/REST API, so there is no independent HTTP API surface to catalog for this entity — this profile documents it as a historical, acquired provider.

providers.name: Harman International
providers.description: Harman International, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Samsung Electronics, is a global leader in connected technologies for automotive, consumer, and enterprise markets, including connected car systems, audio products, professional solutions, and connected services. Harman does not currently publish a public developer portal or open APIs; integrations with Harman platforms (such as Ignite, Ready Connect, and audio brands like JBL, Harman Kardon, and AKG) are typically delivered through commercial partnerships and OEM agreements.

providers.name: INDEX Robotics
providers.description: INDEX Robotics is a South Korean humanoid robotics startup based in Seongnam (Bundang) building high-precision actuators and upper-body humanoid robots for high-mix, low-volume industrial work. Its core products are the IA Series, a family of high-precision actuators purpose-built for humanoid joints, and INDEX01, a compact upper-body humanoid prototype that deliberately foregoes a mobile base so it can slot into constrained factory workspaces for logistics handling, machining support, and precision assembly. The company treats joint precision, responsiveness under sustained repetitive motion, and long-run performance consistency as the core unsolved problems in humanoid commercialization. In February 2026 INDEX Robotics closed a $1M (KRW 1.5B) seed round led by Futureplay with Bass Ventures and 500 Global co-investing. This is a hardware company with no public API, SDK, or developer program at this time.

providers.name: Kyten Technologies
providers.description: Kyten Technologies is a Seattle, Washington hardware manufacturing startup building a factory to produce custom aerospace-grade battery packs. The founders spent six years at Starlink, where they put more than 5,000 battery packs into space, and are now bringing rapid development and volume production of aerospace-grade battery packs to the wider industry. The company positions itself against a legacy supply chain that cannot keep up with the 100,000+ drones, submarines, and satellites being built in the United States. Kyten Technologies is a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company, classified under Industrials / Manufacturing and Robotics, and was an early-stage two-person team at the time of profiling. As a hardware manufacturer it publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: NVE Corporation
providers.description: NVE Corporation (nve.com, NASDAQ: NVEC) is a leader in the practical commercialization of spintronics, a nanotechnology that relies on electron spin rather than electron charge to acquire, store, and transmit information. NVE designs and manufactures spintronic GMR and TMR magnetic sensors (analog, angle/rotation, current, gear-tooth, and medical sensors), digital signal isolators (CAN, RS-422/485, PLC, battery-management, and power interfaces), and power-management ICs. Its developer surface is hardware-oriented: PDF datasheets, application notes, reference designs, magnetic-field calculators/web apps, a YouTube channel, and Arduino/embedded sample code on GitHub. NVE publishes no software/web API, OpenAPI or AsyncAPI specification, SDK, or developer API platform.

providers.name: onsemi
providers.description: ON Semiconductor (now branded as onsemi) is a global supplier of semiconductor-based solutions for power efficiency, image sensing, and signal processing in automotive, industrial, and other applications. No public APIs are documented at this time.

providers.name: Planqc
providers.description: planqc GmbH is a German quantum computing company building neutral-atom quantum computers, using individual atoms trapped in optical lattices as qubits on what it describes as the most promising path to fault-tolerant, scalable systems. Founded in 2022 as a spin-off of the Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich, the company delivers full-stack quantum computing — hardware, control software, and applications — including its MAQCS (Multicore Atomic Quantum Computing System) line for enterprise and scientific customers across aerospace, automotive, energy, and financial services. planqc operates from Garching and Ulm in Germany and Innsbruck in Austria, and is backed by investors including Speedinvest. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or programmatic cloud-access surface; access is arranged directly through the company. This profile is a portfolio-lead stub in the API Evangelist network, enriched with verified public identity and a domain-security probe.

providers.name: Plexus
providers.description: Plexus is a global manufacturing and product development company that helps customers in highly regulated industries (Aerospace/Defense, Healthcare/Life Sciences, Industrial, and Semiconductor Capital Equipment) design, manufacture, and service their products. Plexus does not currently publish a public developer API; this index tracks customer/supplier portals and corporate web properties.

providers.name: Primesense
providers.description: PrimeSense was an Israeli fabless semiconductor and 3D-sensing company, best known for co-developing the depth-sensing technology behind Microsoft's Kinect and for sponsoring the open-source OpenNI (Open Natural Interaction) framework and its NiTE middleware for skeleton tracking and gesture recognition. The company shipped the PrimeSensor reference design and PS1080 system-on-chip for structured-light depth cameras. Apple acquired PrimeSense in November 2013 for roughly $360M; the OpenNI project and openni.org were subsequently wound down (openni.org now redirects to apple.com) and the company's developer program, website, and API/docs hosts are no longer online. Only legacy Apache-2.0 source repositories (the OpenNI sensor driver and NiTE controls) remain public on GitHub. There is no live web/REST API surface for PrimeSense.

providers.name: PsiQuantum
providers.description: PsiQuantum is a Palo Alto, California photonic quantum computing company founded in 2016 by Jeremy O'Brien, Terry Rudolph, Pete Shadbolt, and Mark Thompson, building utility-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computers based on single-photon qubits at telecom wavelength. Its Omega chipset — a silicon photonic system integrating on-chip single-photon sources, superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors, barium-titanate optical switches, and low-loss fiber couplers — is manufactured on 300mm wafers at GlobalFoundries' flagship fab in Malta, NY, leveraging mature semiconductor processes rather than exotic cryogenic fabrication. The company is constructing two utility- scale, million-qubit, fault-tolerant quantum computing sites: one at Moreton Bay, Queensland, Australia (in partnership with the Australian and Queensland governments) and one at the Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park in Chicago, Illinois (with additional R&D at PsiLabs in Daresbury, UK and assembly at PsiFactory in Milpitas, CA). PsiQuantum exposes a developer surface aimed at fault-tolerant quantum algorithm researchers: Construct, an enterprise platform for FTQC algorithm development, resource analysis, and training; Circuit Designer, a free web tool for prototyping and visualizing fault-tolerant quantum circuits; Circuit Hub, a shared library of `.circuit` files; and two open-source Python projects on GitHub — Bartiq, a symbolic quantum resource estimator that compiles subroutine-level costs to global T-gate, Toffoli, qubit, and circuit-volume estimates, and QREF, an open JSON-Schema-based format for representing quantum algorithms as hierarchical DAGs with a Pydantic validation library and a `qref-render` visualization tool. NVIDIA's CUDA-Q is integrated into Construct for accelerated simulation. PsiQuantum does not currently publish a commercial cloud-access REST API, OpenAPI specification, or a general-purpose quantum-execution SDK comparable to those of gate-model quantum cloud providers — its public developer artifacts are confined to FTQC resource-estimation tooling and algorithm-design surfaces — and there is no public pricing or self-serve tier for the underlying quantum hardware.

providers.name: Vathys
providers.description: Vathys is a deep learning hardware startup developing specialized chips to accelerate deep learning, focusing on data movement rather than computation as the main bottleneck, with the goal of a supercomputer on a chip reaching one petaflop on a single chip. Backed by DCVC (first investment 2018). As of July 2026 Vathys has no discoverable live web presence (vathys.ai and related domains do not resolve) and publishes no public API, developer documentation, packages, or GitHub organization.

providers.name: Alpha Technologies
providers.description: Alpha Technologies is a power-systems manufacturer providing AC, DC, and renewable powering solutions for the telecom, cable-broadband, traffic, security, industrial, and alternative-energy industries. Its product line spans uninterruptible power supplies (UPS), standby and non-standby power systems, batteries, enclosures, network/fiber powering gear, and renewable-energy products. Founded in the 1980s and now part of EnerSys, Alpha operates as a hardware and stored-energy solutions provider rather than a public API platform; it was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as an Accel-associated portfolio lead and carries no public developer or API surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Amphiform
providers.description: Amphiform is an energy technology company redefining the future of energy by developing new materials and manufacturing processes that create clean, abundant, and dense energy sources. Rather than scaling existing technologies, Amphiform engineers entirely new materials using precise manufacturing tools to address energy demands for decarbonization, computing, and space exploration. A General Catalyst portfolio company in the energy-infrastructure sector, it is pre-product and does not currently publish any public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Arcturus
providers.description: Arcturus (Arcturus Technologies) is a Los Angeles advanced-materials company founded by Amir Mashal that infuses carbon nanomaterials into metals to create a new class of conductors, using lasers to embed carbon into copper and dramatically improve its electrical, thermal, and mechanical performance. Positioned in frontier climate/energy tech, its drop-in materials target motor windings, bus bars, heat sinks, data-center infrastructure, electric motors, drones, robotics, and — over time — transmission lines and grid infrastructure. The company emerged from stealth in June 2026 with an $8M seed round led by Initialized Capital, with 1517, Breakthrough Energy Discovery, Toyota Ventures, and Wireframe Ventures participating. This is a deep-tech hardware/materials company with no public API or developer program; the profile is maintained as an API Evangelist network company record.

providers.name: Chariot Defense
providers.description: Chariot Defense is a San Francisco-area defense technology company building high-voltage, hybrid-electric power systems for the modern battlefield. Its AMPHORA family (the 24 VDC / 5 kW A24 and the 400 VDC / 35 kW A400) and the upcoming VANGUARD platform deliver quiet, high-density, transportable power that replaces loud, fuel-hungry diesel generators, cutting energy signature and fuel use while powering distributed systems such as drones, sensors, electronic warfare, command and control, additive manufacturing, and directed-energy weapons. Founded in 2022 by Adam Warmoth, the company has raised $41M (a $34M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz plus an $8M seed) and its systems are fielded by the U.S. Army and the Defense Innovation Unit. This is a hardware/defense company profiled in the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API, portal, or documentation.

providers.name: Linear Labs
providers.description: Linear Labs is an industrial motor technology company headquartered in Fort Worth, Texas, building high-torque motor systems for wind, nuclear, pumps, actuators, mining, and defense applications. Its patented Hunstable Electric Turbine (HET) permanent-magnet architecture uses a circumferential flux design the company states delivers 2x torque density, 97% peak efficiency, and 50% weight reduction versus conventional motors, scaling from 10 kW to 2.2 MW. Its PitchPro 2000 is a complete pitch-system replacement for aging GE 1.5 wind turbines, pairing the HET motor with KEBA drive electronics, a Bachmann PLC controller, and ultracapacitor backup power. Linear Labs is a hardware manufacturer and publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable technical surface; this profile is maintained for network coverage and identity only.

providers.name: Oklo
providers.description: Oklo Inc. is a Santa Clara, California advanced fission company designing and deploying small modular reactors under the Aurora powerhouse brand. The Aurora is a liquid-metal (sodium) cooled, metal-fueled fast reactor derived from the Experimental Breeder Reactor-II (EBR-II) lineage, engineered as a "walk-away safe" passively cooled system that is self-stabilizing and self-controlling under loss-of-coolant and loss-of-shutdown conditions. Oklo's reactors are intended to run on recycled high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) fuel, including legacy EBR-II material, with the company building out three vertically integrated fast-reactor businesses: clean power generation, advanced nuclear fuel fabrication and recycling, and medical radioisotope production. The first commercial Aurora is targeted for operation at Idaho National Laboratory (INL) in late 2027 to early 2028, supported by selection into the DOE Reactor Pilot Program and Fuel Line Pilot Projects, and the company has completed an NRC Phase 1 pre-application assessment. Oklo went public in May 2024 via merger with AltC Acquisition Corp (a SPAC co-founded by Sam Altman, who serves as chairman) and trades on the NYSE under ticker OKLO. Oklo's commercial posture is utility-scale and industrial — selling power, fuel cycle services, and isotopes to data center operators, defense customers, and industrial offtakers — and the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, or open source software.

providers.name: Pulse Space
providers.description: Pulse (Pulse - Space Power Solutions) is a Techstars-backed space technology company building power solutions for spacecraft and satellites. The company operates a WebGL marketing site at pulsespace.com and, as of this enrichment pass, publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; enrichment probing confirmed a marketing-only web presence (TLS 1.3 with HSTS) and no developer or API surface to harvest.

providers.name: Radiant
providers.description: Radiant is a nuclear technology company developing portable, transportable microreactors designed to deliver clean, reliable power to remote sites, military installations, disaster-relief operations, and industrial locations that today depend on diesel generators. Its flagship Kaleidos reactor is a factory-built, containerized ~1 MW microreactor intended to ship by truck, plane, or ship and be operational quickly on-site. Founded by former SpaceX engineers and headquartered in El Segundo, California, Radiant is backed by DCVC and Union Square Ventures. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a corporate and careers web presence but no public developer program, API, SDK, or technical documentation surface.

providers.name: Resilient Power Systems
providers.description: Resilient Power Systems is a power-electronics hardware company known for solid-state and medium-voltage power distribution and conversion systems, including solid-state transformers for grid, EV fast-charging, and industrial applications. The company was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass its web presence (resilientpower.com) has moved and now redirects to Eaton, following acquisition; the company publishes no developer portal, API, documentation, SDKs, or other API-consumable surface, so this profile is identity-only. Enrichment probes confirmed the redirect and captured live domain-security posture for the remaining host.

providers.name: Salient Energy
providers.description: Salient Energy is a Dartmouth, Nova Scotia based clean-energy hardware company developing zinc-ion batteries as a safer, lower-cost alternative to lithium-ion for renewable energy storage and grid applications. Its cells use a non-toxic, water-based electrolyte that eliminates fire risk, and are built from low-cost zinc and manganese materials sourced in North America, with a roughly 50% lower production carbon footprint than lithium-ion. The company positions its technology as a scalable answer to lithium supply constraints for stationary energy storage. Salient Energy manufactures physical battery hardware and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Solactron
providers.description: Solactron, Inc. is a Silicon Valley solar technology company developing high-performance, monolithically integrated thin-film solar modules on glass substrates. Its proprietary "Thin Film 2.0" process uses a tunable compound chemistry targeting greater than 34% efficiency by capturing over 95% of the solar spectrum, aiming for the highest efficiency and lowest cost at gigawatt scale. Backed by 500 Global, Solactron is a deep-tech hardware and materials manufacturer positioned in the renewable energy and utility-scale photovoltaic market. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing website only (Home, Technology, Company, Careers, Contact) and exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable discovery surface.

providers.name: SolarBridge Technologies
providers.description: SolarBridge Technologies was a solar power-electronics company that developed AC photovoltaic (ACPV) technology for residential and commercial solar, including its TrueAC modules, the Pantheon and Pantheon II microinverters, and the SolarBridge Management System for monitoring installed systems. The company was acquired by SunPower in 2014 and no longer operates as an independent business; its former marketing site is preserved at solarbridgetech.com. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. SolarBridge was a hardware and embedded-electronics company and does not publish a public developer program, API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Wi Charge
providers.description: Wi-Charge is a long-range wireless power company that transmits electricity over the air using infrared light, delivering safe, automatic charging to smart devices from thirty or more feet away without cables, batteries, or charging pads. The company sells consumer products such as the Encode Wireless Power Kit for smart locks and licenses its transmitter platform and compact receiver modules to OEMs building smart-home, commercial, IoT, retail, and consumer-electronics devices. Wi-Charge is venture-backed, including by Lightspeed Venture Partners. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; as of this pass Wi-Charge publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — it is a hardware and OEM-licensing business rather than an API-first provider.

providers.name: Zeno Power Systems
providers.description: Zeno Power Systems (Zeno Power) develops radioisotope power systems — compact "nuclear batteries" that convert the decay heat of radioisotopes into long-duration electricity for extreme environments such as the lunar surface, deep-sea infrastructure, and remote defense installations. Backed by Techstars and other investors, Zeno is a hardware and energy-systems company; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public web API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or GitHub organization, so this profile is identity-only.

providers.name: Aethero
providers.description: Aethero designs and manufactures radiation-hardened, space-rated edge computing systems and AI/ML software for satellites, space stations, and orbital data centers, enabling autonomous on-orbit processing of imagery and sensor data rather than downlinking raw feeds. Its NVIDIA Jetson Orin/Thor-based NxN-ECM and NxA-ECM edge computing modules, Titan and Phobos platforms, the Aether fleet-management software framework, and the AMATDT model annotation/training/deployment tool let spacecraft run AI inference in orbit. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in San Francisco, Aethero raised an $8.4M seed round led by Kindred Ventures in June 2025. Aethero exposes no public web API today; this profile captures the company's identity and its live domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Allevi
providers.description: Allevi is a bioprinting company that designs and manufactures 3D bioprinters, bioinks, and accompanying software for tissue engineering, regenerative medicine, and life-sciences research. Its desktop bioprinters and biomaterials let researchers fabricate living tissue constructs for drug discovery, disease modeling, and organ-on-chip work. Allevi was acquired by 3D Systems and operates as part of its regenerative medicine portfolio. The company publishes bioprinting protocols, application notes, webinars, and white papers, but exposes no public web API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: Alsym Energy
providers.description: Alsym Energy is a Malden, Massachusetts battery technology company founded in 2015 by Mukesh Chatter, Rahul Mukherjee, and Kripa Varanasi to develop low-cost, high-performance rechargeable batteries that are free of lithium and cobalt. Its Na-Series is a line of non-flammable, non-toxic sodium-ion batteries aimed at grid and utility-scale energy storage, data-center backup, and industrial applications where safety and supply-chain resilience matter. The company uses a proprietary AI/computational-materials platform to accelerate battery chemistry development, and has raised roughly $111M+ including a $78M round in 2024 led by Tata Limited and General Catalyst. Alsym is a hardware/energy-infrastructure manufacturer and does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity and public web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Altair Semiconductor
providers.description: Altair Semiconductor is a fabless semiconductor company that designs low-power, highly integrated cellular IoT chipsets. Its core products are the ALT1250 (a dual-mode LTE-M / NB-IoT modem and SoC with integrated iSIM, MCU and GNSS) and the ALT1350 (a next-generation 5G LPWA SoC that combines LTE-M/NB-IoT, unlicensed-spectrum and satellite NTN connectivity), used in smart meters, asset trackers, wearables, sensors and vehicle telematics. Altair was acquired by Sony in 2016, operated as Sony's cellular IoT unit, and in 2026 was spun back out as an independent company with $50M in funding led by Pitango. This is a hardware/semiconductor provider: it ships chipsets, evaluation kits and datasheets rather than a public developer API, so it carries no OpenAPI, SDK, MCP or developer-portal surface to enrich.

providers.name: Amprius Technologies
providers.description: Amprius Technologies is a Fremont, California-based developer and manufacturer of high-energy density lithium-ion batteries built on a proprietary 100% silicon anode platform. Its flagship SiCore and SiMaxx cell families are marketed as among the industry's highest gravimetric and volumetric energy density rechargeable cells, enabling longer endurance, faster charging, and higher payload capacity than conventional graphite-anode chemistries. Amprius targets aviation and aerospace (high-altitude pseudo-satellites, unmanned aerial systems, electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft), defense (US Army soldier-worn power, BAE Systems), light electric vehicles, robotics, and AI hardware. Public references include AALTO's Airbus-derived Zephyr HAPS programs, Prismatic's PHASA-35 stratospheric aircraft, Nokia Drone Networks, and Matternet drone delivery. The company runs pilot manufacturing and R&D in Fremont and is scaling a GWh-scale Brighton, Colorado plant alongside contract manufacturing partnerships in Asia. Amprius is publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker AMPX. It is certified to ISO 9001:2015 and AS9100:2016. Amprius sells cells, modules, and engineering services to OEMs and defense primes; it does not publish a developer API, SDK, or open-source battery telemetry interface, and has no public GitHub organization.

providers.name: Architect Labs
providers.description: Architect Labs is an AI lab building an AI system that explores, designs, and provably verifies custom silicon for the world's most demanding AI and compute workloads. The company is developing a platform that automates the chip-design and verification workflow, aiming to let AI model developers, robotics startups, and neocloud operators generate and verify custom chips without deep hardware-engineering expertise. Architect Labs raised a $24M seed round led by Kindred Ventures, with participation from investors including Aravind Srinivas and Lukasz Kaiser, and is scheduled to appear at DAC 2026. As of this profile the company publishes a marketing site (about, blog, careers) but no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Arlo Industries
providers.description: Arlo Industries is a San Francisco defense hardware company (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) building a passive sensing network for detecting and tracking drones and aerial threats without traditional radar. Its product, Mentat, uses a distributed mesh architecture of low-cost sensors that cooperatively detect and track targets in 3D while remaining invisible to the threats they monitor. The company frames its approach around "asymmetric economics" — sensor deployment cost grows linearly while tracking accuracy grows exponentially — making the system more scalable than conventional radar installations. Arlo has demonstrated its technology with Ukrainian military operators on active frontlines and maintains partnerships across the US, Ukraine, and Northern Europe. As an early-stage hardware startup it publishes no public API, developer program, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Aspinity
providers.description: Aspinity is a Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania semiconductor company that develops analog machine learning (AnalogML) technology combining ultra-low-power analog signal processing with machine learning for always-on, battery-operated edge AI event detection and classification. Its analogML processors the AML100 and next-generation AML200 deliver TOPS-level inference in a microwatt power footprint, targeting automotive vehicle-security monitoring, smart-home sensing such as glass-break and water-leak detection, and IoT applications including voice and keyword detection and vibration monitoring. Aspinity is a hardware and semiconductor provider and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile tracks its public web and security posture in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: atantares
providers.description: Atantares (芯宿科技) is a Chinese synthetic-biology company based in Suzhou Industrial Park that builds "silicon-based biology" — semiconductor-driven biotechnology. Its chip-based, high-throughput platform (the EcoSyn synthesizer and ECHOS MicroArray, using electrochemical oligonucleotide synthesis on CMOS/MEMS microelectrode arrays) drives low-cost, high-fidelity DNA synthesis and is expanding into RNA and protein synthesis and detection. Research-service offerings include primer/oligo synthesis, gene synthesis, gene sequencing, cloning and mutagenesis, strain-library preparation, and gene editing, built on an in-house full-workflow automation, sequence-analysis, and order-management platform. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners. The company operates a marketing website only and publishes no public developer program, API, or documentation at the time of this profile.

providers.name: Bellabeat
providers.description: Bellabeat is a femtech and women's wellness technology company founded in 2014 by Urska Srsen and Sandro Mur, headquartered in San Francisco, California. It designs health-tracking wearables and connected devices aimed at women, including the Leaf and Ivy wellness jewelry trackers, the Time hybrid smartwatch, and the Spring smart water bottle, paired with the Bellabeat mobile app that tracks activity, sleep, stress, meditation, menstrual cycle, and overall wellness. Bellabeat operates as a direct-to-consumer wellness brand; it does not currently publish a public developer API, so this profile captures company identity and network provenance rather than API artifacts. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Y Combinator portfolio lead and enriched here.

providers.name: Constelli
providers.description: Constelli (Constelli Signals Private Limited) is a Hyderabad, India based defence and aerospace signal-processing company founded in 2017 by Satya Gopal Panigrahi and Avinash Chenreddy. It designs and manufactures radar systems, radar target and echo simulators, deployable drone-based radar payloads, high-performance radar processors, and IRIG-standard digital telemetry receivers for ground, onboard, and satellite telemetry. Its products serve electronic warfare and defence R&D programs globally, including India's Ministry of Defence and DRDO. Constelli raised a $20M Series A led by General Catalyst (with Pravega Ventures and 360 One). It is a hardware/systems company and does not currently publish a public developer API, portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Daivin
providers.description: DAIVIN! is a deep-tech hardware company (Y Combinator Winter 2026, based in San Francisco and Finland) building tankless diving technology. Its core product, SPRING, is marketed as the "world's first tankless diving technology": instead of carrying heavy pressurized oxygen tanks, a diver wears a lightweight vest of electrolyzers and a battery belt that use electricity to split water on demand into breathable oxygen (O2) and hydrogen (H2), targeting depths up to 200 meters / 650 ft. Founder Leo Kankkunen frames breathing as "fundamentally an energy problem," and the company envisions applications beyond recreational and professional diving across space exploration, high-altitude rescue, hospitals, and aircraft. Added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-capital portfolio lead surfaced via y-combinator. Daivin runs a conceptual marketing website (Wix) and a news blog; it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or other machine-readable developer surface, so no API artifacts apply to this provider.

providers.name: EdgeQ
providers.description: EdgeQ is a fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Santa Clara, California, building a converged "Base Station-on-a-Chip" that integrates 5G, 6G, non-terrestrial network (NTN), custom waveform, CPU, and antenna-controller functions into a single software-defined silicon platform. Its programmable baseband targets small cells, private enterprise 5G, open RAN, satellite (LEO/MEO) communications, and AI-enabled physical devices. EdgeQ is a hardware and silicon provider surfaced as a portfolio company of Threshold Ventures; it publishes a corporate site, a 5G engineering blog, newsroom, and careers, but exposes no public developer portal, API, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Enfabrica
providers.description: Enfabrica is a semiconductor company building networking silicon and systems for large-scale AI and accelerated-computing infrastructure. Its ACF-S ("Accelerated Compute Fabric") SuperNIC targets maximum throughput with fault-tolerant, multipath connectivity across AI clusters, and its EMFASYS elastic memory fabric system provides memory offload for AI inference workloads. Enfabrica is backed by Spark Capital. The company publishes a technical blog and company news, but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal, so this profile carries company identity and domain-security signals rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Etched
providers.description: Etched is an AI hardware company building Sohu, a transformer-only ASIC designed to accelerate inference for large language models by hard-wiring the transformer architecture directly into silicon. Etched markets Sohu as an alternative to general-purpose GPUs for transformer inference, claiming order-of-magnitude throughput improvements on models such as Llama 70B when deployed in eight-chip server configurations. The chip is fabricated on TSMC's 4nm process with 144 GB of HBM3E per package. As of mid-2026 Etched has raised more than 625 million dollars at a 5 billion dollar valuation but has not yet shipped Sohu to customers in volume, and there is no public Etched API or developer surface. This profile is company-and-product-only and intentionally has an empty apis list.

providers.name: Evonetix
providers.description: Evonetix is a Cambridge, UK deep-technology company developing a benchtop DNA synthesis platform built on semiconductor technology. Its core innovation is a silicon chip carrying thousands of independently thermally-controlled reaction sites, allowing many DNA strands to be synthesised in parallel with per-site temperature control, in-process error detection and correction, and assembly of high-fidelity genes at the desktop. The company's goal is to give synthetic biology, life-science, and drug-discovery researchers accurate, on-demand access to synthetic DNA without relying on centralised outsourced gene foundries. Evonetix was surfaced as a portfolio company of the deep-tech venture firm DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK, and its primary web domain (evonetix.com) resolves to a suspended-account placeholder page.

providers.name: Kets
providers.description: KETS Quantum Security is a Bristol, UK deep-tech company (incorporated 2016) building chip-based quantum-safe encryption and networking hardware. Its product line spans Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), Quantum Random Number Generators (QRNG), and the KETS KORE sub-system, delivering security grounded in the laws of physics rather than computational complexity. KETS technology hardens telecommunications networks, satellite and aerospace communications (including Airbus collaborations), data-center backups, and critical infrastructure control systems against the emerging threat of quantum computing. Backed by European quantum-specialist venture investors including Speedinvest and supported by multiple UK government funding awards, KETS is a hardware and photonics company; it does not currently publish a public API, SDK, or developer portal. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a Speedinvest portfolio lead and enriched with identity and domain-security signals.

providers.name: MITO Material Solutions
providers.description: MITO Material Solutions (MITO Materials) is a specialty chemical company that develops patented hybrid additive technology to strengthen composite and thermoplastic materials. Its platform functionalizes graphene and biomaterials to improve strength, durability, flexibility, and sustainability without requiring changes to a manufacturer's existing process. Core products include the MITO hybrid additive platform, MITO E-GO, MITO E-GO Res-1, and MITO ACRE, serving the sports and recreation, transportation, automotive, and infrastructure industries. The company is a Techstars portfolio company and was added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass, MITO publishes no developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Mogassam
providers.description: Mogassam is a digital dentistry company building all-in-one dental 3D printing hardware and software for chairside, single-visit treatment. Its products include the DentCase automated all-in-one 3D printer with integrated CAM, automatic washing, and post-curing, the Microdent 1 Pro printer, and the DentPrint dental 3D printing software, used to produce dentures, dental models, surgical guides, and provisional and permanent restorations. The company was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. No public API, SDK, or developer documentation was found at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Mycotech
providers.description: MYCL (Mycotech Lab) is an Indonesian biomaterials company, founded in 2015 and based in Bandung, that cultivates mushroom mycelium on agricultural waste to produce sustainable, carbon-sequestering alternatives to animal leather, plastics, and construction materials. Its flagship product is Mylea, a mycelium-based leather-like material, alongside Biobo binder board, MYCL Composite for architecture and interior design, and Mylea Sea, a seaweed-based biopolymer. A certified B Corp and Good Design Award winner backed by 500 Global and the Unreasonable Group, MYCL sells physical materials and finished goods rather than software; it publishes no public API, developer portal, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Mythic
providers.description: Mythic is a high-performance analog computing company building Analog Processing Units (APUs) for energy-efficient AI inference. Its compute-in-memory architecture stores AI model parameters directly in the processor to eliminate the memory bottleneck of traditional digital designs, targeting data center, automotive, robotics, edge, and defense workloads with claims of dramatically lower energy use and cost versus GPUs. Surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and Threshold Ventures. As of this enrichment pass Mythic publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Nabhdrishti Aerospace
providers.description: Nabhdrishti Aerospace is a Bangalore-based deep-tech startup building India's first fuel-flex micro gas turbine for aviation and power generation. Its ND 400 engine is a 400 N single-core micro gas turbine designed for UAVs, hybrid-electric aircraft, and small aircraft as well as oil & gas, manufacturing, and vehicle range-extender power generation, running on conventional fuels, biofuels, and hydrogen with an innovative recuperator design that targets greater than 15% efficiency at under half the cost of competing turbines. Backed by Accel, the company raised USD 3M and operates from the IISc Bangalore IHUB. As a hardware manufacturer it publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform; this profile tracks its public web presence.

providers.name: NVision Imaging Technologies
providers.description: NVision Imaging Technologies (now operating as NVision Quantum Technologies) is a deep-tech healthcare company that engineers quantum technology at the molecular level. Its flagship POLARIS platform delivers quantum-enhanced MRI, boosting the magnetic signal of engineered sugar molecules by over 10,000x to image disease metabolism in real time, and its PIQC platform is a quantum-computing architecture built on molecular quantum nodes native to photonic chips. The company is backed by Playground Global. It publishes no public developer API, SDK, or technical integration surface; this profile carries identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Orthocon
providers.description: Orthocon, now operating as Abyrx, is a surgical-therapeutics medical device company that has built a materials-science platform focused on therapeutic devices used during surgical procedures. Its portfolio centers on resorbable and hemostatic bone putties for orthopedic, trauma, spine, sports medicine, cranial, maxillofacial, and cardiothoracic applications, including AHBP (water-soluble hemostatic bone putty), the HemaSorb family (HemaSorb, HemaSorb Apply, HemaSorb Plus with HA/beta-TCP), and MONTAGE settable resorbable bone putty. The company sells directly to surgeons, hospitals, and distributors and does not operate a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or programmatic developer surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and enriched via the API Evangelist pipeline; the honest result is that there is no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Petcube
providers.description: Petcube is a pet-technology company (a Y Combinator alum) that makes interactive Wi-Fi pet cameras and a companion mobile app for remote pet care. Its consumer hardware line includes the Petcube Cam, Bites treat-dispensing camera, and Play laser camera, offering HD video, night vision, two-way audio, motion and sound alerts, and app-controlled treat tossing and play. Petcube also sells the Care subscription (cloud video history, extended alerts) and Online Vet / Emergency Fund telehealth services. As of this enrichment pass Petcube exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or documented integration surface — the primary interface is the consumer iOS/Android app tied to its private cloud backend. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Quantum Systems
providers.description: Quantum-Systems GmbH is a Gilching/Munich, Germany-based dual-use drone manufacturer founded in 2015 by former Bundeswehr helicopter pilot Florian Seibel.
