The company designs, builds, and operates small electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) fixed-wing unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) for reconnaissance, intelligence, surveillance, target acquisition (RSTA), surveying, and mapping. Its flagship platforms include the Trinity Pro (mapping/surveying VTOL with up to 90-minute endurance), the Vector tactical reconnaissance drone (the de facto main small UAS supplier to the German Bundeswehr and, with 619+ systems delivered as of April 2025, one of the most-used Western reconnaissance drones in Ukraine), the Reliant long-range Group 2 ISR/RSTA platform built for the U.S. market with 10+ hours endurance and hot-swappable MOD-compliant payload bays (EO/IR, SIGINT, EW, CRPA), and the Ukraine-manufactured Sparta drone carrier that delivers two FPV drones to a 200 km combat radius. All platforms are operated through QBase 3D, Quantum-Systems' proprietary Windows-based mission planning, control, and post-processing software with integrated ESRI terrain data and direct export to Pix4D, Agisoft, Propeller, and Trimble Business Center. The Vector tactical line is built on Auterion's flight stack. Backed by HV Capital, DTCP, Thiel Capital, Project A, Airbus Ventures, and Omnes Capital, the company reached unicorn status in May 2025 as "Europe's first dual-use unicorn." Quantum-Systems supplies the militaries of Germany, the United States, Ukraine, Australia, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Romania, and Spain. There is no public developer API, REST endpoint, SDK, or open-source release for QBase 3D or any Quantum-Systems platform; integration with Pix4D/Agisoft/Propeller/Trimble is via standard photogrammetry file exchange (GeoTIFF, RAW imagery, flight logs), not a programmable API.

providers.name: Quintessent Communications
providers.description: Quintessent is a deep-tech photonics startup based in Goleta, California, developing optical connectivity solutions that address the communication bottlenecks in large-scale computing and AI infrastructure. The company builds chip-to-chip optical interconnect technology grounded in quantum-dot laser epitaxy, and has established supply chains for quantum-dot epitaxial wafers used in AI optical interconnects. Quintessent is a hardware and semiconductor photonics company rather than a software/API provider; it exposes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface. Backed by Battery Ventures, Entrada Ventures, Foothill Ventures, and Sierra Ventures, with research funding from DARPA, ARPA-E, and the NSF, the company was surfaced as a venture-portfolio lead and profiled here for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Reach Labs
providers.description: Reach Labs (operating as Reach Power Inc.) is a wireless power transmission company that delivers electrical energy through the air without physical connections, describing its mission as "doing for power what Wi-Fi did for data." Its patented approach combines energy-transmission hardware, a custom delivery algorithm, and adaptive software controls to beam power to devices across varying distances and conditions. The company targets three primary sectors: defense and intelligence (powering sensors, autonomous vehicles, and drones in remote environments), manufacturing and logistics (energizing robotics and IoT devices in industrial settings), and public safety (enabling continuous drone operations for first responders). Reach was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable metadata surface.

providers.name: Shape Shapescale
providers.description: Shapescale is a consumer body-scanning company that builds ShapeScale, a home 3D body scanner and companion mobile app. The device slowly rotates around a standing user, captures a photorealistic 3D model of the body, and measures body composition, weight, and circumference metrics so users can track fitness and body changes over time. Shapescale is a Y Combinator portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer product website but no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: Standard Kernel
providers.description: Standard Kernel Co. is an AI infrastructure company building a system that automatically generates optimized low-level kernel code — the programs that execute computations on GPUs and TPUs. It aims to eliminate the kernel-engineering bottleneck across the AI stack by combining LLMs with program analysis to produce hardware kernels (matmul, attention, fused feed-forward networks) that match or exceed hand-tuned libraries such as cuBLAS and FlashAttention3, including reported results at 99–116% of cuBLAS on H100 BF16 matmul. Backed by a $20M seed round with participation from General Catalyst, the company is early-stage and does not yet publish a public API, SDK, or developer platform.

providers.name: TAE Technologies
providers.description: TAE Technologies (formerly Tri Alpha Energy) is a Foothill Ranch, California fusion energy company founded in 1998, pursuing commercial fusion power using aneutronic hydrogen-boron (p-B11) fuel in an advanced beam-driven field-reversed configuration (FRC). Because the p-B11 reaction is aneutronic, TAE's approach produces virtually no neutron flux or on-site radioactive waste compared with conventional deuterium-tritium concepts. The company has built a progression of plasma machines — Sewer Pipe, CBFR-SPS, C-2, C-2U, and C-2W ("Norman") — and is constructing Copernicus in Irvine, California to demonstrate net energy gain, with Da Vinci planned as the grid-connected power-plant demonstration. TAE has raised more than USD 1.2 billion from investors including Google, Chevron, NEA, Goldman Sachs, Vulcan, Venrock, Wellcome Trust, and the Kuwait Investment Authority, and runs research collaborations with Japan's National Institute for Fusion Science (NIFS). Two operating subsidiaries commercialize spin-off technology: TAE Life Sciences develops accelerator-based Boron Neutron Capture Therapy (BNCT) systems for cancer treatment, and TAE Power Solutions builds modular, software-controlled power-management systems for e-mobility and battery applications. TAE is a private hardware and deep-science company; it does not publish a developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or public open-source code repository.

providers.name: Thrive Agritech
providers.description: Thrive Agritech is a horticultural lighting company that designs and manufactures high-efficiency LED grow lights and related power systems for commercial indoor farming, greenhouses, and vertical farming operations. Its product line includes fixtures such as Strata, Boost XE, and a 1050W LED grow light, along with a Remote Power System, backed by lighting design services, rebate assistance, and multi-year warranties. The company positions itself around energy efficiency, ROI, and long-term grower partnerships rather than a developer or API offering. Surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network, this profile was enriched by probing the public web surface; no public API, developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable specification was found.

providers.name: VINNO
providers.description: VINNO Corporation (飞依诺科技股份有限公司) is a Chinese medical device manufacturer, headquartered in Suzhou, that develops and produces digital color ultrasound (Doppler) imaging systems — cart-based, portable, and handheld/pocket devices — for clinical diagnostics and research. Product lines include the ULTIMUS and VINNO R-series ultrasound platforms plus Stream-series CPAP respiratory devices, built on proprietary soft beamforming and ultra-high-resolution micro-vascular imaging technology, with remote-diagnostic center and support services across 50+ countries. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. As of enrichment the company publishes no public API, SDK, or developer surface (medical-device hardware manufacturer).

providers.name: Volt14
providers.description: Volt14 Solutions Pte Ltd is a Singapore-based deep-tech startup developing silicon-majority anode materials for lithium-ion batteries. Its fully integrated, tunable, and ready-to-use anodes replace conventional graphite to deliver large gains in energy density and lower normalized cell cost, while remaining compatible with existing battery cell manufacturing infrastructure. Target application markets include electric vehicles, consumer electronics, appliances, and power tools. The company is a materials-science and battery-technology producer; it publishes a corporate and careers website but exposes no public developer or API product surface. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Zetwerk
providers.description: Zetwerk is a global contract-manufacturing and B2B supply-chain company that connects original equipment manufacturers with a vetted network of manufacturing partners across processes including CNC machining, die casting, forging, injection molding, and sheet-metal stamping. It serves industries such as aerospace and defense, automotive, consumer electronics, renewable energy, and industrial equipment, offering production sourcing, quoting, and program management. Backed by Accel, D1 Capital, Khosla Ventures, and Lightspeed Venture Partners, Zetwerk operates as a manufacturing services marketplace rather than a developer platform: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or programmatic integration surface.

providers.name: Entegris
providers.description: Entegris is a global supplier of advanced materials and process solutions for the semiconductor and other high-technology industries. The company develops and manufactures specialty chemicals, gases, filtration and purification systems, advanced materials handling, and process control products. No public developer API or developer portal has been identified at the corporate level; technical integration is typically supported through sales engineering, the supplier portal, and product documentation.

providers.name: 3com
providers.description: 3Com Corporation was a networking-technology pioneer founded in 1979 by Robert Metcalfe, the co-inventor of Ethernet, and colleagues; its name derived from "Computer, Communication, and Compatibility." 3Com built Ethernet network interface cards, switches, routers, and enterprise networking and security hardware, and at one point owned the Palm handheld computing business. An early Mayfield Fund portfolio investment (seed participation in 1981, alongside NEA, Venrock, and Sequoia), 3Com later operated the 3Com, H3C, and TippingPoint brands before being acquired by Hewlett-Packard in 2010 for roughly $2.7 billion, after which the standalone brand was wound down. This record is a historical company profile; 3Com no longer operates an independent developer portal, public API, or live product surface (the 3com.com domain now serves a placeholder page).

providers.name: 6thSense
providers.description: 6thSense is a physical-AI hardware company building the touch layer for dexterous robots. It designs and manufactures wearable tactile-sensing data gloves that capture how human hands interact with the world — pressure, contact, grip, and 3D hand pose — alongside custom tactile skin molded to robot hands. Its capture stack synchronizes eight aligned modalities (tactile and pressure proxies, egocentric video, depth/RGB-D, hand pose, motion and IMU dynamics, wrist and scene cameras, dense labels and commentary, and success/failure outcomes) into model-ready demonstration datasets used to train the next generation of dexterous, manipulation-capable robots. Founded in 2026 in San Francisco and backed by Y Combinator (S26).

providers.name: 9 Mothers Corporation
providers.description: 9 Mothers Corporation is a defense technology company founded in 2024 and based in Austin, Texas, building AI-powered counter-drone (C-sUAS) point defense systems for the FPV drone era. Its flagship product, EDDA, is a small, low-power, autonomous-capable point-defense turret that engages Group 1 suicide drones at 10-100+ meter range to protect soldiers, vehicles, and critical assets. A Y Combinator Spring 2026 company with reported sales to the U.S. Department of War, its roadmap includes Vor (passive acoustic sensor), Atla (belt-fed shotgun system), and Gleipnir (counter-drone for larger platforms). This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. The company publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Advanced Analogic Technologies (AnalogicTech)
providers.description: Advanced Analogic Technologies Incorporated (AnalogicTech, formerly NASDAQ: AATI) was a fabless semiconductor company founded in 1997 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California, with design centers in Santa Clara and Shanghai. The company designed total power-management solutions built on proprietary analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits and discrete power MOSFETs, shipping a portfolio of more than 500 power-management application-specific standard products (ASSPs) and general-purpose analog ICs across four application areas: display and lighting, voltage regulation and DC/DC conversion, interface and power management, and battery management, primarily for mobile and portable consumer electronics. Advanced Analogic Technologies was acquired by Skyworks Solutions, Inc. in January 2011 and no longer operates as an independent company; it is a hardware semiconductor manufacturer with no public web API, developer platform, or API artifacts. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a company record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Advanced Metal Research
providers.description: Advanced Metal Research is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) company based in Los Angeles building machine intelligence for American welding. The company develops American-made robotic welding cells that pair computer vision with real-time seam tracking and post-weld inspection, turning welding from a scarce manual craft into a closed-loop manufacturing system that learns from every weld as it happens. Founded in 2025 by Julian Fried, Stephen Lin, and Angus Muffatti, it targets the projected shortage of skilled welding professionals across US industrial manufacturing. The company is early-stage and hardware-focused; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Advent Solar
providers.description: Advent Solar was a silicon photovoltaic company founded in 2002 and headquartered in Albuquerque, New Mexico, that designed and manufactured crystalline-silicon (c-Si) solar cells and modules, pioneering emitter-wrap-through cell architectures and streamlined back-contact module assembly. Backed by Battery Ventures, EnerTech Capital, @Ventures and others across roughly $109M in venture funding (including a $70M Series D in 2007), the company's assets and intellectual property were acquired by Applied Materials in late 2009 / 2010. As a physical solar-hardware manufacturer that is no longer operating independently, Advent Solar exposes no public API, developer portal, or software surface; this profile is retained as a network identity record with no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: airquality
providers.description: AirQuality (爱优特) is a Shanghai-based manufacturer of high-efficiency electrostatic air purification and disinfection products, including central air filtration systems, commercial kitchen exhaust (hood) cleaners, odor-elimination units, and smart air-quality detection systems for schools, hospitals, offices, shopping malls, and hotels. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. It is a hardware/manufacturing business that publishes a consumer website and online shop but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time, so most enrichment artifacts are not applicable.

providers.name: Akash Systems
providers.description: Akash Systems is an Oakland, California deep-tech semiconductor company that pioneers Diamond Cooling thermal-management technology, integrating synthetic diamond directly with semiconductors such as Gallium Nitride (GaN) to remove heat up to five times faster than copper. Its Chip-on-Diamond and diamond-cooled server products target AI and data-center compute, while its GaN power amplifiers and satellite radios serve space communications, radar, cellular, and automotive/EV markets. Akash Systems is a hardware and materials company with no public developer API or documentation surface; it was surfaced as a DCVC portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment.

providers.name: Aliena
providers.description: Aliena is a Singapore-based space-technology company, incorporated in 2018, that designs and manufactures compact electric propulsion systems for small satellites. Its MUSIC plasma thruster line delivers high thrust-to-power ratios at very low power budgets with high specific impulse, enabling small satellites to operate and sustain very low Earth orbit (VLEO) for high-resolution remote sensing. Aliena is a hardware manufacturer with no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a 500 Global portfolio lead.

providers.name: Alphion
providers.description: Alphion Corporation is a broadband access equipment manufacturer that develops fiber-optic and wireless networking solutions for network operators, enterprises, and community networks. Founded in 2000 and based in Princeton Junction, New Jersey, the company builds GPON-based fiber-to-the-x (FTTx/FTTH) access systems, optical network terminals (AONT/ONT), and secure GigaWi-Fi broadband access products that deliver voice, data, video, and wireless services over passive optical networks. Alphion is a photonics and telecommunications hardware provider; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. It does not currently publish a developer portal, public API, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Amalfi Semiconductor
providers.description: Amalfi Semiconductor was a fabless developer of high-performance CMOS radio frequency (RF) and mixed-signal semiconductors for cellular handsets. Its proprietary CMOS-based AdaptiveRF architecture delivered power amplifiers that extended battery life and talk time while reducing the size and cost of front-end cellular handset designs, shipping over 100 million CMOS power amplifiers. Battery Ventures led the company's $24M Series C in 2009, with further investment in 2012 alongside DCM and Globespan Capital Partners. Amalfi Semiconductor was acquired by RF Micro Devices (now part of Qorvo) in November 2012 for $47.5M in cash. The company is defunct as an independent entity and publishes no developer portal, documentation, or public API; this profile is retained for network and portfolio-graph completeness rather than API enrichment.

providers.name: Amber Wave
providers.description: AmberWave, Inc. (formerly AmberWave Systems Corporation) is a Lowell, Massachusetts deep-technology company that researches, develops, and licenses semiconductor and photovoltaic materials technology. It originated strained-silicon and aspect-ratio-trapping techniques from MIT and Bell Labs research, and today develops Ultra-Thin Silicon (UTSi) flexible solar cells and modules that weigh roughly 90% less than conventional panels, targeting lightweight commercial rooftops, off-grid power, building integration, vehicle, and aerospace applications. AmberWave is a Battery Ventures portfolio company. It publishes a corporate website but exposes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation surface, so there are no machine-readable API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: AMCC
providers.description: AMCC (Applied Micro Circuits Corporation, also known as AppliedMicro or APM) was a fabless semiconductor company founded in 1979 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California. It designed network and embedded Power ISA processors, ARMv8-A server processors (the X-Gene line), and optical transport, connectivity, and storage silicon for telecommunications, data center, and industrial markets. Backed by Matrix Partners, U.S. Venture Partners, and other venture investors, AMCC traded on NASDAQ under the ticker AMCC. It was acquired by MACOM Technology Solutions (NASDAQ: MTSI) in January 2017 and no longer operates as an independent company. As a fabless chip designer with no public developer platform, AMCC exposes no APIs, SDKs, or developer documentation; this profile is retained as a historical company record and Matrix Partners portfolio lead.

providers.name: AMCC (Applied Micro Circuits Corporation)
providers.description: Applied Micro Circuits Corporation (AMCC) was a California-based semiconductor company founded in 1979, originally producing application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) for the military market before diversifying into commercial mixed-signal, networking, storage, and embedded processor products. AMCC went public on NASDAQ in 1997, acquired MMC Networks in 2000, and bought IBM's PowerPC 400 processor line in 2004. Under the AppliedMicro brand it later developed the X-Gene ARM 64-bit server-on-chip family. AMCC ceased to exist as an independent entity when MACOM completed its acquisition on January 26, 2017; the X-Gene compute business was subsequently spun out to form Ampere Computing. As a fabless silicon/hardware company (now defunct), AMCC published no public developer API surface, so this profile carries company identity only and no API artifacts.

providers.name: Anobit Technologies
providers.description: Anobit Technologies was an Israeli fabless semiconductor company, founded in 2006, that developed flash-memory Memory Signal Processing (MSP) controller technology to extend the endurance, reliability, and performance of consumer-grade NAND flash used in SSDs and mobile devices. Backed by Battery Ventures among others, Anobit was acquired by Apple in early 2012 and no longer operates as an independent company. It has no public developer surface, API program, or live web presence, and remains in the API Evangelist network only as a historical portfolio-company record.

providers.name: Apex Space
providers.description: Apex Space (Apex) is a Los Angeles based satellite manufacturing company that builds productized, configurable spacecraft bus platforms for proliferated constellations across LEO, MEO, and GEO orbital regimes. Apex offers three product lines: Aries (small satellites up to 150 kg payload), Nova (medium satellites up to 300 kg payload), and Comet (large satellites up to 3,000 kg payload), and operates Factory One, a high-rate manufacturing facility in Los Angeles with the capacity to produce more than 200 satellites annually. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network. Apex does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or developer documentation; customers configure satellite platforms through the on-site Configurator and direct sales inquiries.

providers.name: Apigy
providers.description: Apigy, Inc. is the company behind Lockitron, an early keyless smart-lock startup that let people lock, unlock, and share access to their doors from a smartphone. Backed by 500 Startups (now 500 Global) and known for a large 2012 crowdfunding campaign, Apigy built connected door-lock hardware and companion mobile apps before the Lockitron product line was wound down. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; its public website (lockitron.com) is currently unreachable and no active developer or API surface could be located.

providers.name: Arilinc
providers.description: Aril Inc. (Arilinc) is a fabless semiconductor company in Los Gatos, California designing efficient AI processors and memory technology for edge inference. Its two core products are the Aril Standard Cell Memory, a patented on-chip memory offering roughly 40% lower active power and 3.6x smaller area, and a scalable RISC-V-based AI Processor Engine delivering hundreds of TOPS of inference per block with integrated vector and matrix engines. The company targets robotics, industrial automation, drones, defense and aerospace, autonomous vehicles, and edge vision systems where power efficiency is critical. Founded by a team of engineers who have collectively shipped 20M+ processors and worked on silicon for Cisco, Intel, AMD, and Google. Arilinc sells custom silicon and IP to hardware makers rather than a public developer API; it publishes no API, SDK, developer portal, or programmatic surface at this time.

providers.name: asgoodasnew
providers.description: asgoodasnew is a German e-commerce retailer of refurbished and pre-owned consumer electronics, including smartphones, tablets, laptops, cameras, and related accessories, sold with warranty through its online store at asgoodasnew.de (asgoodasnew.com redirects there). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Point Nine and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. Probing the public surface found no developer portal, API documentation, or API host — this is a consumer-facing storefront with no public API program at this time. The profile is retained as a portfolio lead; only mechanical domain-security signals for the web host could be captured.

providers.name: Atrisa
providers.description: Atrisa (formerly Refortifai) is a Y Combinator (P26) startup building AI agents for analog circuit design. The product is a chat-based assistant engineer that lets hardware and analog design teams ask it, in natural language, to create a design, debug a circuit, or run simulations. Atrisa is designed to fit into existing workflows: teams bring their own toolkit, PDKs (process design kits), and design documents, which Atrisa reads, understands, and adopts to produce schematic-level outputs and iterate on analog designs. As an early-stage company it currently ships a hosted web application rather than a public developer API, so this profile captures its identity, domain-security posture, and public surface pending any future API release.

providers.name: Avegant
providers.description: Avegant is an augmented reality display technology company that develops light engine technology bringing high-performance visuals to lightweight AR glasses designed for everyday wear. Its flagship product, the AG-30L2 LED light engine, is described as the world's smallest LED light engine for augmented reality. Avegant is a venture-backed hardware company (a portfolio company of 500 Global) focused on the optical and display components that power the next generation of AR eyewear rather than on a public developer platform. No public API, SDK, or developer documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Avnera
providers.description: Avnera Corporation was a fabless semiconductor company founded in 2004 and headquartered in Beaverton, Oregon, that designed low-power analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits and audio system-on-chip (SoC) solutions for wireless headphones, headsets, soundbars, speakers, and gaming audio devices. Backed by venture investors including Redpoint Ventures, Avnera was acquired by Skyworks Solutions in 2017 and now operates as part of Skyworks. It maintains no independent developer program or public API surface; the avnera.com domain resolves to a parked/inactive page with no product site.

providers.name: Awavesemi
providers.description: Awavesemi (Awave Semiconductor) is a semiconductor company originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass, its domain awavesemi.com issues a 301 redirect to https://www.qualcomm.com/data-center, indicating the company and its data-center silicon effort have been absorbed into Qualcomm. Awavesemi publishes no independent developer portal, public API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or MCP surface — it is a hardware/silicon company, not an API provider, so the enrichment pipeline finds no API artifacts to harvest beyond domain-level security posture.

providers.name: Bear Flag Robotics
providers.description: Bear Flag Robotics is an autonomous-tractor company that retrofits existing farm tractors with sensors, onboard compute, and path-planning software to enable driverless field operations such as tillage and row-crop work. Founded in 2017 and backed by Y Combinator and True Ventures, the company was acquired by John Deere in August 2021 and now advances Deere's autonomy roadmap. It is a hardware and agricultural-robotics business with no public developer API, SDK, documentation portal, or GitHub surface; its website redirects to John Deere.

providers.name: Bedrock Materials
providers.description: Bedrock Materials was a Chicago-based deep-tech startup founded in 2023 by Spencer Gore (CEO, previously Tesla and Enovix) and Rafael Vila (CTO, Stanford battery scientist) to manufacture engineered sodium-ion cathode active materials as a low-cost, easy-to-source alternative to lithium-ion — built from abundant sodium, manganese, iron and aluminum, and designed to drop into existing lithium-ion cell manufacturing lines for low-voltage, starter-lighting-ignition, micromobility and industrial-traction applications. It raised a $9M seed round led by Trucks Venture Capital with Refactor Capital and Version One Ventures. In April 2025 the company wound down and returned the majority of that seed capital to its investors: CEO Spencer Gore concluded that sodium-ion could not be produced cheaply enough to beat lithium iron phosphate (LFP) after lithium oversupply collapsed prices, and that energy-density gains carried steep trade-offs. Bedrock Materials was a materials-science manufacturer and never operated a developer program, public API, or developer portal; both bedrockmaterials.com and its former bedrock.inc website are now parked/for-sale domains with no company content. This profile is retained as a verified-defunct record in the API Evangelist network — there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Beyond Reach Labs
providers.description: Beyond Reach Labs is a Brooklyn, New York aerospace company building deployable solar arrays and thermal radiators for spacecraft that expand from compact launch sizes to enormous structures in orbit. Its patented geometry-changing panels grow from the size of a dining table to a football field once deployed, giving satellites, orbital data centers, commercial space stations, and lunar outposts up to 10x more usable power without adding launch mass or volume. Founded by two aerospace engineers, the company is targeting its first in-space demonstration in Q2 2027 and is a Y Combinator portfolio company. Beyond Reach Labs is a hardware manufacturer and does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Bilimber Pte. Ltd.
providers.description: Bilimber Pte. Ltd. is a Singapore-based private company (exempt private company limited by shares) incorporated on 2020-11-17, operating in research and experimental development on electronics. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global (an early/seed-stage investor alongside a Hong Kong government program) and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public website, developer portal, documentation, or API surface -- the bilimber.com domain is currently unregistered and does not resolve -- so no first-party API artifacts could be searched, derived, or generated. This profile remains a lead awaiting a public API surface.

providers.name: Bridgeco
providers.description: BridgeCo Inc. was a fabless semiconductor company founded in 2000 that built networked-audio silicon and software for consumer electronics. Its JukeBlox platform — a system-on-a-chip paired with a software development kit — let wireless speakers, A/V receivers, home-theater systems and docking stations stream music from tablets, smartphones and PCs, and was designed into products from Pioneer, Philips, Denon, Marantz, JBL and Harman/Kardon. Earlybird Venture Capital was the company's first institutional investor in 2000. BridgeCo was acquired by Standard Microsystems Corporation (SMSC) on 19 May 2011 in a deal worth up to $67.5 million, and SMSC was in turn acquired by Microchip Technology on 2 August 2012, where the JukeBlox wireless-audio line was folded into Microchip's portfolio. BridgeCo no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer portal, documentation or public API; the bridgeco.com domain today is an unrelated domain-for-sale parking page.

providers.name: Briko Robotics
providers.description: Briko Robotics (Briko Robotica) was a Mexican educational technology startup founded in 2014 in San Luis Potosi, Mexico, that sold a modular programmable electronics kit paired with an online learning platform teaching robotics and programming to children from roughly age eight. The company was accelerated by 500 Startups LatAm (batch 7) and raised a small seed amount. Third-party company databases now classify Briko Robotics as deadpooled, and its former domain brikorobotics.com has been hijacked and serves unrelated SEO spam. No developer portal, documentation, API, or machine-readable specification was ever published, so this profile carries identity and provenance only.

providers.name: Britesemi
providers.description: Britesemi (Brite Semiconductor / 灿芯半导体（上海）股份有限公司, Shanghai, stock ticker 688691) is a one-stop custom chip and silicon IP supplier. It provides ASIC design services spanning chip specification definition, SoC and mixed-signal design architecture, backend design, and final product delivery, alongside a family of proprietary YouIP interface IP cores (YouDDR, YouSerdes, YouUSB, YouMIPI, YouPCIe, YouONFI, YouIO, YouRF, YouADC). This is a semiconductor / ASIC design-services business, not a public web-API provider: enrichment found no developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, or other machine-readable API surface. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of norwest-venture-partners.

providers.name: Bumblebee Spaces
providers.description: Bumblebee Spaces is a San Francisco smart-home robotics company that builds app-controlled motorized storage systems for compact urban living. Its ceiling-mounted robotic units lift beds, closets, and storage bins up and out of the way, reclaiming floor space in small apartments, while a built-in camera and mobile app track and retrieve stored belongings on demand. The company sells and installs hardware plus a companion consumer mobile application; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. Backed by Bloomberg Beta and Canaan Partners, the profile is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead.

providers.name: Calista Technologies
providers.description: Calista Technologies was a desktop and GPU virtualization startup founded in 2006 in San Jose, California by Neal Margulis, backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Greylock, and Western Technology Investment. Its software improved the user experience of 3-D and multimedia delivery for virtualized desktop deployments and server-hosted applications running on Windows Server Terminal Services (Remote Desktop). Microsoft acquired the company in 2008 and folded its GPU-virtualization technology into RemoteFX. The company is defunct and publishes no live developer, documentation, or API surface; its former domain (calistatechnologies.com) is now a parked domain listed for sale.

providers.name: Cambridge Aerospace
providers.description: Cambridge Aerospace is a UK-based defense technology company, incorporated in September 2024, developing scalable interceptor missiles and sovereign air-and-missile-defense systems for European nations. Its first product, Skyhammer, is a tube-launched subsonic interceptor with a Cambridge-developed radar seeker, positioned as an affordable, mass-producible counter to drones and cruise missiles (often likened to an Iron Dome-style layered air defense). The company operates in the aerospace and defense/security sector and is backed by a venture syndicate including Accel, Lakestar, Lux Capital, Spark Capital, and the D3 fund. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel; it is a hardware-first defense company with no public API or developer surface at this time.

providers.name: Cavium
providers.description: Cavium, Inc. was a fabless semiconductor company founded in 2000 and headquartered in San Jose, California, that designed multicore processors and networking silicon for enterprise, data center, cloud, and service-provider infrastructure. Its product families included OCTEON multicore MIPS and ARM network and security processors, ThunderX ARM-based server SoCs, Nitrox security processors, LiquidIO intelligent adapters and smart NICs, and the FastLinQ Ethernet and Xpliant switch lines it gained through its 2016 acquisition of QLogic. Cavium was a publicly traded company (NASDAQ: CAVM) before being acquired by Marvell Technology Group in July 2018 for roughly 6 billion US dollars. Its technology now ships as part of Marvell's networking and infrastructure processor portfolio. As a silicon and hardware vendor, Cavium never operated a public developer API program or web API surface.

providers.name: Cencorp
providers.description: Cencorp (Zhuhai) Industrial Technology Co., Ltd. is a process-automation equipment manufacturer that designs and builds high-end laser processing, dispensing, automated optical inspection (AOI), and system-integration & automation systems for the consumer electronics, automotive electronics, semiconductor, and new-energy industries. Formed in 2020 and combining the acquired Finland-based Cencorp automation business with operations headquartered in Zhuhai, China, the company runs 12 offices worldwide with 400+ R&D engineers and 300+ patents, and is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. It exposes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — this is a physical automation-equipment business.

providers.name: Circularity Fuels
providers.description: Circularity Fuels builds AI-controlled, mass-manufacturable reactors that turn waste carbon and cheap renewable power into drop-in hydrocarbons, starting with affordable sustainable aviation fuel (SAF). Its Ouro Reactor reforms waste carbon (methane and CO2 off-gassed by dairy farms, agricultural plants, and industrial facilities) into clean syngas, and its Aion Reactor uses next-generation Fischer-Tropsch synthesis to assemble that syngas into liquid fuels. The company is a portfolio company of DCVC and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. It is a hardware and process company with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Citadel
providers.description: Citadel (also branded Citadel Defense / Drone Citadel) is a counter-unmanned-aircraft-system (C-UAS) company founded in 2016 that built an automated, modular drone-defense solution using proprietary machine-learning algorithms to detect, classify, and defeat unauthorized drones. It raised a Lightspeed Venture Partners Series A in 2017 and was subsequently acquired by BlueHalo. The company operates no public developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface, and its standalone domains (citadeldefense.com, dronecitadel.com) are now parked or no longer resolve.

providers.name: Coinmine
providers.description: Coinmine is a consumer cryptocurrency-mining hardware company known for the Coinmine One, a plug-and-play home mining device that let non-technical owners mine and hold crypto assets from a simple companion app. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the coinmine.com storefront is offline (the Shopify store returns "unavailable"), so no live developer portal, API, or documentation surface could be confirmed. The registrable domain remains active for email (SPF/DMARC configured), and this profile captures the honest, probed security posture of that domain.

providers.name: Compaq
providers.description: Compaq Computer Corporation was a personal-computer manufacturer founded on February 16, 1982 in Houston, Texas by Rod Canion, Jim Harris and Bill Murto, three former Texas Instruments executives. It legally reverse-engineered the IBM PC BIOS and shipped the Compaq Portable in March 1983, then built out the Deskpro desktop line, the LTE notebook line, the Presario consumer line, and the SystemPro and ProLiant server lines, becoming the world's largest PC maker by 1994. Losing ground to Dell's direct-sales model and hit by the dot-com collapse, Compaq agreed to merge with Hewlett-Packard on September 4, 2001 in a $24.2 billion deal that closed on May 3, 2002. HP retired the Compaq brand entirely in North America and Europe in 2013 and has since licensed it regionally to third parties (Positivo Tecnologia in Brazil, Grupo Newsan in Argentina, Triden Corp in Mexico, Ossify Industries in India). Compaq predates the public web-API era and never published a developer program, public API, or SDK of its own; the compaq.com domain is still registered to HP Inc. but serves no website. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Compaq Computer Corporation
providers.description: Compaq Computer Corporation was an American personal-computer company founded in 1982 in Houston, Texas by Rod Canion, Jim Harris, and Bill Murto. It pioneered IBM PC-compatible portable computers with the 1983 Compaq Portable and grew into one of the largest PC manufacturers of the 1990s, acquiring Digital Equipment Corporation in 1998. Compaq merged with Hewlett-Packard in 2002; the brand was gradually retired and its operations absorbed into HP. It survives in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-company profile (backed by kleiner-perkins); it operates no present-day developer portal, public API, or SDK surface, as compaq.com now resolves to HP infrastructure.

providers.name: Congruent
providers.description: Congruent builds AI-native radar hardware and simulation tooling for self-driving cars and end-to-end autonomy. The company pairs a radar architecture that exposes raw sensor data with a world-model-based generative simulator, producing both real and synthetic raw radar returns to train autonomy stacks. Radar is the only depth sensor cheap enough to scale to every vehicle while still working in rain, fog, snow, and dust, where camera and lidar systems degrade. Congruent is an early-stage Y Combinator (W26) company founded in 2025 by Clement Barthes and Evan Scope Crafts, based in the San Francisco Bay Area. It was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this profile the company operates a single marketing website and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or specification.

providers.name: Cornami
providers.description: Cornami is a Santa Clara, California high-performance computing company building morphable silicon and a stream-centric software stack for privacy-preserving and AI workloads. Its FracTLcore Fabric and TruStream dataflow programming model power the Tigris 16nm ASIC, MX8 board, and rack-scale MX64 system, delivering real-time Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE), private LLM inference, blockchain, and signal-processing acceleration at greatly reduced power and latency. Cornami is a frontier-tech company backed by SoftBank Vision Fund; this profile tracks its public developer and API surface within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Cray
providers.description: Cray is the high-performance computing (HPC) and supercomputing brand, originally Cray Research and later Cray Inc., now part of Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) following HPE's 2019 acquisition. The cray.com domain 301-redirects to HPE's HPC/compute pages, and Cray no longer operates an independent public developer portal, API reference, or API surface — its supercomputing systems, ClusterStor storage, and Slingshot interconnect are marketed and supported under HPE. Enrichment found no first-party Cray API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or documentation to harvest. The norwest-venture-partners backing recorded on this stub is a legacy venture-history association, not a current independent company relationship.

providers.name: Creopop
providers.description: CreoPop is a consumer 3D-printing pen that lets you draw three-dimensional objects freehand. Unlike filament 3D pens it has no hot parts or melting plastic; instead it uses photopolymer "cool ink" cartridges that are solidified by built-in LEDs, and it is battery operated and charged over mini-USB. The product line includes specialty inks (elastic, magnetic, glow-in-the-dark, aromatic, temperature-sensitive, and electrically conductive). CreoPop is a hardware/consumer-electronics brand with a marketing and direct-to-consumer e-commerce website; it publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation.

providers.name: Crossbar
providers.description: Crossbar, Inc. is a Santa Clara semiconductor company founded in 2010 that develops resistive random-access memory (ReRAM), a non-volatile memory built on RRAM patents licensed from the University of Michigan. Its CMOS-compatible ReRAM targets faster write performance, lower power consumption, and higher endurance than NAND flash at roughly half the die size, and is offered as embedded and standalone memory IP to OEMs and system-on-chip developers across consumer, mobile, enterprise, industrial, and IoT markets. Crossbar is a hardtech portfolio company backed by Kleiner Perkins. As a silicon-IP provider it exposes no public developer API surface; this profile carries company identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Crystal
providers.description: Crystal (Crystal Semiconductor) was a hardtech company that designed audio and mixed-signal semiconductor chips. Kleiner Perkins partnered with the company in 1986 at the early stage, and Crystal was subsequently acquired by Cirrus Logic. The company was surfaced from the Kleiner Perkins portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. It operated as a fabless chip designer rather than a software or platform business, and no longer exists as an independent entity: it publishes no website, no developer portal, and no public API surface of any kind. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio record and is not an API provider.

providers.name: CYGIA
providers.description: CYGIA (Zhuhai CYGIA Automation Equipment Co.) is an intelligent-factory equipment and solution provider founded in 2006 and headquartered in Zhuhai, China. It develops, manufactures, and services intelligent automation and automated-test equipment for consumer electronics, semiconductor and integrated-circuit, automotive, medical, and new-energy industries. Once backed by Qiming Venture Partners, CYGIA became a subsidiary of publicly traded CYG (Changyuan Group, Shanghai Stock Exchange 600525.SH) in 2015. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead; enrichment found no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDK surface for CYGIA, which is a hardware/automation-equipment manufacturer rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Damon Motorcycles
providers.description: Damon Motorcycles (Damon Inc.) is a Vancouver, British Columbia electric motorcycle company founded in 2017 by Jay Giraud and Dominique Kwong, and an alumnus of the Techstars accelerator. Damon builds high-performance electric motorcycles led by the HyperSport and HyperFighter models, and is known for two safety and ergonomics technologies: CoPilot, a 360-degree advanced warning system that uses radar, cameras, and sensors to alert riders to surrounding hazards, and Shift, a transformable ergonomics system that adjusts the riding position between commuter and sport stances. The company has faced significant financial and going-concern difficulties, and its public web presence at damon.com currently returns errors, so no developer portal, documentation, or public API surface could be verified during enrichment. This profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Danger
providers.description: Danger, Inc. was a Palo Alto, California mobile computing company founded on December 9, 1999 by Andy Rubin, Joe Britt, and Matt Hershenson, all former Apple, WebTV, and Philips engineers. Danger built the Danger Hiptop, sold in the United States as the T-Mobile Sidekick, an early client-server ("cloud") smartphone whose downloadable application catalog prefigured the app stores later shipped by Android and iOS. Andy Rubin left Danger in 2003 to found Android. Microsoft acquired Danger on February 11, 2008 for a price reported at roughly $500 million and folded the team into "Project Pink," which shipped as the short-lived Microsoft Kin. Most former Danger staff had left Microsoft by October 2009 and the company was wound down by approximately 2011. Danger was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a historic Redpoint Ventures portfolio holding. It is defunct: the danger.com domain no longer resolves and there is no developer portal, documentation, or API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Deice
providers.description: De-Ice Technologies is an aviation deep-tech company that develops a fast, chemical-free aircraft de-icing system to replace traditional glycol chemical spray methods. Spun out of MIT in 2015 by co-founders Alexander Bratianu-Badea and Ruben Toubiana, the Somerville, Massachusetts company uses gallium nitride (GaN) semiconductors to generate high-frequency electric current through tape-like strips attached to an aircraft's exterior, melting snow and ice during the boarding window instead of the usual 30-45 minute glycol spray delay. The approach eliminates glycol spraying costs and the carbon emissions from idling and chemical production/transport, improving airline on-time performance. Air Canada is the launch customer, and the technology was featured in Time's Best Inventions of 2024. De-Ice is a portfolio company of Playground Global. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; De-Ice publishes no public API, SDK, or developer surface at this time.

providers.name: Discovered Materials
providers.description: Discovered Materials (legally matforge inc) is a Y Combinator-backed (Spring 2026) startup based in San Francisco building AI scientists for the semiconductor industry. The company uses swarms of AI agents to run the full materials-discovery pipeline - generating candidate materials, synthesizing them, and testing them in physical laboratories - to find novel materials for datacenters and fabrication facilities. Their stated goal is to compress a process that traditionally takes 10+ years of lab work into months, targeting 10x-better alternatives for applications such as nanoscale interconnects. Founded by Akash Ramdas (Stanford materials-science PhD/postdoc) and Advaith Sridhar (Carnegie Mellon AI, formerly Luma Labs and Persona AI). At the time of profiling the company exposes no public API, developer portal, or documentation; this entry is an enrichment lead maintained in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Earendil Robotics
providers.description: Earendil Robotics is a Y Combinator-backed defense technology company registered in England and Wales that builds AI-powered situational-awareness and counter-drone systems for tactical units. Its product line includes IVAS, an edge-AI vision-augmentation system fusing night vision, thermal imaging, and laser ranging for total-darkness operation; Aeglos, an autonomous high-speed (300+ km/h) interceptor drone for counter-UAS defense with autonomous target locking and all-weather thermal tracking; and Holo, an ultra-lightweight dual-mode tactical sight combining high-resolution thermal imaging with a fiber-optic reticle. As of this profile the company exposes only a public marketing website and a contact form, with no published developer surface, API, SDKs, documentation, or GitHub organization.

providers.name: EDGE Sound Research
providers.description: EDGE Sound Research is an audio technology company building intelligent audio infrastructure, as stated by its own tagline. Backed by Techstars, the company operates from edgesoundresearch.com. As of this enrichment pass no public developer portal, API, SDK, CLI, MCP server, or machine-readable specification (OpenAPI/AsyncAPI) was found on its web presence, and the site is a fully client-rendered Next.js application. This profile captures the company's identity and web/domain security posture within the API Evangelist network pending any future developer surface.

providers.name: eigencomm
providers.description: Shanghai Eigencomm Technology Co., Ltd. is a fabless semiconductor company founded in 2017 and headquartered in the Zhangjiang district of Shanghai, China, dedicated to the research, design, and sale of cellular Internet of Things (IoT) communication chipsets and their supporting software. Eigencomm has mass-produced NB-IoT and Cat.1bis chip series that power smart meters, smart security, mobile payment, shared devices, asset trackers, charging piles, wearables, smart firefighting, and smart home appliances, and is developing 5G silicon. The company is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund II, Qiming Venture Partners, and others, having raised roughly USD 171M across multiple rounds. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; it publishes no public web API, developer portal, or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Eka Robotics
providers.description: Eka Robotics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts robotics-AI company founded in 2025 that is building intelligence for the physical world in its native language: force. Its Vision-Force-Action (VFA) model combines vision, force sensing, and action to give robots generality, performance, and safety for close human-robot interaction. The team pioneers self-supervised robot learning, large-scale robot learning, world models, reinforcement learning, and sim-to-real transfer, drawing talent from MIT, Berkeley, Harvard, DeepMind, and Boston Dynamics. Co-founded by MIT professor Pulkit Agrawal (Improbable AI Lab), the company is an early-stage research-and-hardware venture and does not yet publish a public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation. This profile was surfaced as a venture-portfolio lead and enriched with the company's public identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Elephint
providers.description: Elephint is an electronics-photonics integration company building integrated photonic systems-on-a-chip (SoC) technologies. Its focus areas span photonic integrated circuits, silicon photonics, free-space optical communication, fiber optics, optical amplifiers, coherent beam combining, wavefront control, photonic signal processing, photonic computing, and artificial intelligence. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network, Elephint is a deep-tech hardware company that presently publishes only a company website (https://elephint.ai) and does not expose a public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Energy Micro
providers.description: Energy Micro was a Norwegian fabless semiconductor company, founded in 2007 and headquartered in Oslo, best known for its EFM32 "Gecko" family of energy-friendly 32-bit ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers and the EFR radio products targeting low-power embedded and IoT applications. The company was acquired by Silicon Labs in 2013 and fully absorbed into that company's product lines; its former energymicro.com domain now redirects to silabs.com. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment found no independent, first-party API, developer portal, OpenAPI, SDK, or MCP surface for Energy Micro as a standalone entity — the developer tooling for its EFM32 line lives under Silicon Labs today.

providers.name: Enjoy Technologies
providers.description: Enjoy Technology (Enjoy Technologies) was a "commerce at home" mobile-retail startup founded in 2014 by Ron Johnson, the former Apple senior vice president of retail and JCPenney CEO, and headquartered in Palo Alto, California. The company brought the retail store experience to customers' homes, dispatching mobile experts to deliver, set up, and demonstrate consumer electronics on behalf of partners such as carriers and device makers. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Oak Investment Partners, and Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Enjoy went public via SPAC in 2021 and declared bankruptcy in 2022, with its assets subsequently acquired. Enjoy never operated a public developer program or API; this profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company record.

providers.name: Enpirion
providers.description: Enpirion was a fabless semiconductor company specializing in high-frequency power-management integrated circuits, best known for its PowerSoC family of integrated DC-DC converters that combined the controller, MOSFETs, and inductor in a single package for point-of-load power conversion in networking, computing, and industrial systems. The company was acquired by Altera in 2013 and subsequently absorbed into Intel with Altera in 2015; the Enpirion brand and its enpirion.com developer/product site are now defunct. It never operated a public developer API, documentation portal, or SDK program, so this record is retained as a company identity stub rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: FangTek
providers.description: FangTek (Shanghai Fangtek Electronics Co., Ltd.) is a Chinese fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Shanghai. It designs highly integrated analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits for mobile phones, portable devices and consumer electronics, with a product line spanning audio power amplifiers, voice and audio processing, image processing, LED drivers, power management ICs, analog switches and DC boost converters. Qiming Venture Partners lists FangTek in its portfolio as "a leading provider of highly integrated circuit solutions for cell phone, portable device, voice processing, audio processing and image processing." FangTek is a silicon component vendor that reaches customers through electronics distributors; it publishes no public developer platform, web API, SDK or machine-readable API surface, so this profile carries identity and domain-security data only.

providers.name: Figure
providers.description: Figure is a Sunnyvale, California humanoid robotics company building general-purpose bipedal robots for the home and the workplace. Its current flagship product is Figure 03, marketed as an everyday general-purpose humanoid robot, succeeding Figure 01 and Figure 02. Figure develops Helix, an in-house Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model that unifies perception, language understanding, and learned control to drive a full upper humanoid body at 35 degrees of freedom and 200 Hz, with capabilities including novel-object manipulation from natural-language commands and multi-robot task coordination. Figure has run commercial pilots with partners such as BMW and previously collaborated with OpenAI on language models. The company's revenue model is robot sales/leasing and enterprise deployments; Helix is a proprietary on-board model and there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for Figure or Helix.

providers.name: Finisar
providers.description: Finisar Corporation was a manufacturer of optical communications components and subsystems (optical transceivers, semiconductor lasers, and related fiber-optic hardware). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures. Finisar was acquired by II-VI Incorporated in 2019, and the combined company was subsequently rebranded as Coherent Corp. The Finisar brand is retired (finisar.com issues a 301 redirect to coherent.com, verified 2026-07-19) and has no independent public developer, API, or documentation surface. No API artifacts are applicable to this stub.

providers.name: Freescale Semiconductor
providers.description: Freescale Semiconductor, Inc. was an American semiconductor manufacturer headquartered in Austin, Texas, created in 2004 from the spin-off of Motorola's Semiconductor Products Sector. Freescale designed and produced embedded processing hardware — microcontrollers (Kinetis, S08), i.MX applications processors, ColdFire and QorIQ/PowerPC communications processors, digital signal processors, RF, analog, and sensor products — for the automotive, networking, industrial, and consumer markets. In December 2015 Freescale merged with NXP Semiconductors in a roughly $11.8B deal and ceased to exist as an independent company; its freescale.com domain now redirects to nxp.com. Freescale was a hardware/silicon company, not a web-API provider: it published no public REST/HTTP API, developer portal, or OpenAPI, so there is no live API surface for the enrichment pipeline to harvest.

providers.name: Fungible
providers.description: Fungible Inc. was a Santa Clara, California startup founded in 2015 by Pradeep Sindhu (Juniper Networks co-founder) and Bertrand Serlet that built Data Processing Units (DPUs) — programmable microprocessors (the F1 and S1 chips plus the FS1600 NVMe storage array) designed to offload networking, storage, and security workloads from data-center CPUs. Its DPU cluster control plane ran Linux and exposed internal REST APIs for management, but Fungible never published a public developer API, developer portal, or SDK registry. Microsoft acquired the company in January 2023 (reported ~$190M), folded the team into its Azure data-center infrastructure engineering organization, and wound down the independent product line. The fungible.com domain no longer resolves and there is no live public API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Fusion I/O
providers.description: Fusion-io (branded Fusion I/O) was an enterprise storage company founded in 2005 and based in the Salt Lake City area of Utah, best known for its ioMemory and ioDrive PCIe flash acceleration cards that placed NAND flash directly on the server bus to speed databases and data-center workloads. Steve Wozniak served as chief scientist; the company listed on the NYSE in 2011 and was acquired by SanDisk in 2014, later becoming part of Western Digital. It exposes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface today; fusionio.com no longer resolves to a live site. Retained in the network as a defunct a16z portfolio company for record.

providers.name: Fusion-io
providers.description: Fusion-io was a computer hardware and software systems company founded in 2005 in Salt Lake City, Utah, that pioneered PCIe-based flash memory (NAND) storage for enterprise data centers under the ioMemory, ioDrive, ioFX and ioScale product lines. Steve Wozniak served as its Chief Scientist. The company IPO'd on the NYSE under the ticker FIO in June 2011 and was acquired by SanDisk in 2014 for roughly 1.1 billion dollars; SanDisk (and the Fusion-io technology) was in turn acquired by Western Digital in 2016. It was venture-backed by New Enterprise Associates, Lightspeed Venture Partners and Accel. Fusion-io no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no public developer API surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company record.

providers.name: galbot
providers.description: Galbot (银河通用机器人, "Galaxy Universal Robotics") is the official site of a general-purpose, embodied-AI robotics company. It was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of the venture firm Qiming and profiled here for API and developer-surface enrichment. As of this enrichment pass Galbot publishes only a marketing website rendered as a client-side single-page app; no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, or MCP surface could be discovered. The only machine-readable signals captured are the DNS, TLS, and email-authentication (SPF/DMARC) posture of the galbot.com domain.

providers.name: Galileo Technology
providers.description: Galileo Technology was a fabless semiconductor company founded in 1993 that designed and marketed complex semiconductor devices for high-performance embedded control systems, principally in the area of data communications. Co-founded by Avigdor Willenz (CEO), Manuel Alba (President), and Eyal Waldman (VP Engineering), the company completed an IPO in 2000 and was acquired by Marvell Technology, Inc. in 2001 for approximately $2.7 billion. It was an early Lightspeed Venture Partners investment (1995). The company no longer operates independently and exposes no public developer surface, API, or documentation; this profile is retained for network/portfolio lineage only.

providers.name: Generalastro
providers.description: General Astronautics (Generalastro) is a Y Combinator (W26) space-robotics company founded in 2025 by Bram Schork, based in San Francisco, building autonomous dexterous robotic arms that perform laboratory research and manufacturing tasks in microgravity without astronaut intervention. Its systems handle work like pipetting, sample prep, plate handling, and reagent mixing, targeting microgravity production of pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, and fiber optics where crew time on orbital stations is the bottleneck (NASA estimates ISS crew time at ~$130K/hour). The company is pre-product hardware, backed by Y Combinator and Planet Ventures (~$7.1M raised), and currently exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or other machine-readable surface; this profile captures company identity only.

providers.name: Ghost Robotics
providers.description: Ghost Robotics designs and manufactures quadrupedal unmanned ground vehicles (Q-UGV), with its flagship Vision 60 platform deployed across defense, public safety, law enforcement, industrial, construction, and education customers. The platform supports modular payloads for sensing, comms, and manipulation. Ghost Robotics provides a developer SDK only to vetted partners and integrators and does not operate a public developer portal, open API, or public GitHub organization.

providers.name: Graft Concepts
providers.description: Graft Concepts was a consumer-electronics accessories company best known for the "Leverage" modular iPhone case, a latched aluminum-and-polycarbonate bumper frame with interchangeable backplates that let owners swap in kickstands, bike mounts, and 3D-printed backs. The company was a Y Combinator startup based in the San Francisco Bay Area and was acquired by Inseego (formerly Novatel Wireless) in January 2014, after which the independent product and brand were wound down. This profile was surfaced by the venture-portfolio scraper and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment found no live developer surface, API, SDK, or documentation for the company. The original graftconcepts.com domain no longer serves the company and now resolves to a parked content page, so there are no API artifacts to catalog.

providers.name: Greypoint Industries
providers.description: Greypoint Industries is a Canadian defense-technology company (Y Combinator S26) building passive RF mapping software that charts the electromagnetic spectrum so operators can see every signal, track every threat, and act first — "built in Canada for those who protect." Founded in 2026 by Nic Chu, Jordan Khoo, Steven Xu, and Darcy Zhang, the company also develops mass-produced autonomous counter-drone interceptors designed to defeat drone-swarm saturation at a fraction of the cost of the targets. As an early-stage hardware and software startup, Greypoint currently publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification; this profile captures the company's identity for the API Evangelist network and awaits a developer surface to enrich.

providers.name: Growth Networks
providers.description: Growth Networks was a networking-silicon startup founded in the late 1990s that developed a new category of switching hardware it branded Internet Switching Fabrics — scalable, multi-service capacity silicon for high-speed network switches and routers. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners (co-founded by Barry Eggers), the company was acquired by Cisco Systems in 2000 and folded into Cisco's core routing and switching business. It operates no independent developer platform or public API today; this profile is retained as a venture-portfolio historical record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Hardware Intelligence
providers.description: Hardware Intelligence is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) startup based in San Francisco building an end-to-end, agent-native toolchain for chip design. Founded in 2026 by Athreya Anand, the company applies agentic AI and ultrafast feedback loops to the semiconductor design and verification workflow. Its first product, Wave, is a terminal-native waveform debugger with a verification agent built in, aimed at accelerating hardware debugging and design iteration. At the time of profiling the company is pre-launch with early-access pilots and a waitlist; it publishes no public API, developer documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI, so this API Evangelist profile captures company identity only and awaits a developer surface to enrich.

providers.name: Hlabs
providers.description: Hlabs (Harrison Laboratories, Inc., operating as hlaboratories.com) is a US-based, Y Combinator-backed (Winter 2026) manufacturer of plug-and-play robotics components. The company produces a domestically-manufactured, integrated hardware ecosystem for robot builders — including the RB1 main board (powered by Nvidia Jetson), wireless communication modules, field-oriented control (FOC) boards, pancake motors, and actuators. Its stated goal is to eliminate the complexity of sourcing mismatched components from overseas and integrating them, so roboticists can focus on design rather than electronics debugging. Hlabs targets teams building medium-to-large robots such as quadrupeds, humanoids, and robot arms, and serves customers across household robotics, defense, and other robotic platforms. This is a hardware manufacturer with no public developer/API surface at the time of profiling.

providers.name: Humane
providers.description: Humane was a consumer AI hardware startup, founded by former Apple engineers, best known for the AI Pin — a screenless, wearable AI-powered device — and its companion Cosmos operating system and Humane.Center cloud service. The company was acquired by HP in early 2025, the AI Pin was discontinued, and its cloud services and humane.com domain were taken offline. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Kindred Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass the company has no reachable web, developer, or API surface.

providers.name: Hydro Wind Energy
providers.description: Hydro Wind Energy develops offshore renewable energy infrastructure at the convergence of dispatchable clean power, grid-scale energy storage, and freshwater production. Its OceanHydro Omni deep-sea offshore wind platform converts wind into mechanical lift with built-in storage; SubSea RO Wind couples wind energy directly to subsea reverse-osmosis desalination; and the Offshore AI Power Plant integrates both with floating data centres for off-grid AI infrastructure. The company also ships QuenchSea, a portable hand-powered desalination device deployed across 60+ countries. Backed by Techstars, Republic, and Shell StartUp Engine. The company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: IBEX Process Technology
providers.description: IBEX Process Technology was a semiconductor-industry technology company based in Lowell, Massachusetts, founded around 2000, that developed neural-network-based process control systems for semiconductor fabrication. The company raised roughly $6.8M across two funding rounds and is now defunct (deadpooled), with an Involuntary Revocation status on its Massachusetts registration. It was surfaced as a portfolio-lead stub from battery-ventures data; enrichment finds no live website, no developer/API surface, and no machine-readable specifications to harvest.

providers.name: Iceberg Quantum
providers.description: Iceberg Quantum is a quantum architecture firm building fault-tolerant quantum computing systems around LDPC (Low-Density Parity-Check) error-correction codes. Its designs aim to cut the hardware overhead of quantum error correction by more than an order of magnitude, and its Pinnacle architecture claims roughly 10x lower overhead through modular lattice surgery and time-overhead compression. The company is hardware- and architecture-focused rather than a software/API provider; it partners with qubit hardware makers (PsiQuantum, Diraq, Oxford Ionics) and is backed by DCVC, Blackbird, and LocalGlobe. Surfaced as a DCVC portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for tracking; there is no public API, SDK, or developer surface to enrich at this stage.

providers.name: icerasemi
providers.description: Icera Semiconductor (icerasemi.com) was a British fabless semiconductor company known for soft-modem and baseband processor chipsets for wireless devices, and was acquired by NVIDIA in 2011. It was surfaced as a portfolio lead of balderton-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The company no longer operates independently; as of this enrichment pass the domain www.icerasemi.com returns a shared-hosting error page with no live product, developer, API, or documentation surface, so there is nothing beyond domain-level metadata to enrich.

providers.name: Imara
providers.description: Imara Corporation was a lithium-ion battery technology startup founded in 2006 in Menlo Park, California, that grew out of research at SRI International. It designed and manufactured high-power lithium-ion battery cells and packs based on patented cathode materials science, targeting power tools, outdoor power equipment, hybrid electric vehicles, specialty applications, and power-grid energy storage. Backed by Battery Ventures and Nth Power, it raised roughly $15.65M and reached commercial cell production in 2009 before shutting down around 2010-2011 for lack of manufacturing funding. It is a hardware company with no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface, and is now defunct.

providers.name: Impossible Aerospace
providers.description: Impossible Aerospace is a deep-tech aerospace hardware company founded in 2016 by Spencer Gore in Santa Clara, California. It builds the US-1, a long-range all-electric quadcopter whose lithium-ion cells form part of the airframe structure, giving it up to roughly two hours of flight time for aerial imaging, surveillance, and public-safety missions with law enforcement and first responders. The US-1 runs the third-party Auterion OS flight stack (built on the PX4 open autopilot). The company was later acquired and operates as a small team. Enrichment note (2026-07-19): the company publishes no public API, SDK, or developer surface, and its primary domain impossible.aero no longer resolves in DNS.

providers.name: Industrial Safety Technologies
providers.description: Industrial Safety Technologies (IST) was a hardware-focused industrial safety platform, founded in 2011 and built by Battery Ventures through acquisitions of gas-detection and hazard-monitoring businesses including Gas Measurement Instruments (GMI), Detcon, DSA Detection, and Simtronics. Its products centered on fixed and portable gas detectors, flame detectors, and hazardous-environment safety instrumentation for industrial sites. IST was acquired by Scott Safety, a Tyco business, from Battery Ventures for $329.5 million in December 2014 and no longer exists as an independent company; the enrichment pipeline found no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or documentation surface to profile.

providers.name: Innovium
providers.description: Innovium, Inc. was a Santa Clara, California semiconductor company founded in 2014 that designed high-bandwidth Ethernet switch silicon (the TERALYNX family) for cloud and enterprise data centers, competing with Broadcom on high-radix, low-latency switching with deep buffers and built-in telemetry/analytics. Backed by Greylock and other deep-tech investors, Innovium was acquired by Marvell Technology in 2021 (~$1.1B) and its switching technology continues inside Marvell's portfolio. The company shipped hardware silicon, not a public developer API — innovium.com now redirects to marvell.com, and there is no developer portal, OpenAPI, or programmatic API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Inphi
providers.description: Inphi Corporation (formerly NYSE: IPHI) was a fabless semiconductor company that designed high-speed analog and mixed-signal interconnect components -- SerDes, PAM4 DSPs, optical DSPs, and coherent DSPs -- used to move data across networks and inside data centers, from cloud and telecom infrastructure to long-haul and metro optical transport. Founded in 2000 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California, Inphi was acquired by Marvell Technology in April 2021 and folded into Marvell's data-center and connectivity portfolio; its former inphi.com domain now 301-redirects to marvell.com. As a semiconductor hardware company, Inphi did not publish a public developer API, portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio company record.

providers.name: IPtronics
providers.description: IPtronics A/S was a fabless semiconductor company founded in 2003 in Copenhagen, Denmark, designing integrated circuits (laser drivers, transimpedance amplifiers, and CMOS ICs) for parallel optical interconnects used in high-speed computing, storage, and datacenter communications. Backed by Creandum, Sunstone, and 10i10, the company was acquired by Mellanox Technologies in 2013 (now part of NVIDIA) and no longer operates as an independent entity. It is a hardware chip vendor with no public API, developer portal, SDK, or programmatic surface; the former iptronics.com domain now redirects to NVIDIA Networking. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio identity record only.

providers.name: IQI Inc (Beijing AIQI Technology)
providers.description: IQI Inc, operating as Beijing AIQI Technology Co., Ltd. (北京爱其科技有限公司), is a mobile-internet company founded in April 2013 that develops smart hardware and robotics products under a "Create more & More fun" philosophy. It is best known for its ONEBOT building-block robots and construction sets — including the Mi Tu (米兔) block robots in the Xiaomi ecosystem and heritage-architecture sets such as the Millennium Mortise-and-Tenon (千年榫), Qinian Hall (祈年殿) and Forbidden City Corner Tower kits. The company sells through its own store, Tmall (ONEBOT flagship) and JD.com. It is a consumer smart-hardware/toy brand; as of this profile it publishes no public developer platform, API, SDK or documentation surface.

providers.name: JAKA
