providers.description: Zymergen was a synthetic-biology and bio-manufacturing company founded in 2013 in Emeryville, California, that used machine learning and automation to engineer microbes and discover novel bio-based materials and molecules. It went public on NASDAQ in 2021 and was acquired by Ginkgo Bioworks in October 2022; the zymergen.com domain now 301-redirects to Ginkgo Bioworks. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC, Kindred Ventures, and Obvious Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Enrichment found no public developer portal, API, documentation, or event surface — the company has no independent API footprint following the acquisition. This profile is retained as a portfolio/history record.

providers.name: Dow
providers.description: Dow Inc. is a global materials science company headquartered in Midland, Michigan. Dow combines science and technology to develop innovative products and solutions for packaging, infrastructure, mobility, and consumer applications. This entry is an alias of dow-chemical and covers the same parent company.

providers.name: Jabil Circuit
providers.description: Jabil (formerly Jabil Circuit) is a global manufacturing services and solutions company providing comprehensive electronics design, production, and product management services to electronics and technology companies in a broad range of industries.

providers.name: Fourier
providers.description: Fourier is an energy technology company building on-site, on-demand hydrogen production systems. Its core product is a modular, scalable device that generates hydrogen where it is needed, removing the transport and storage barriers of conventional hydrogen supply. Fourier targets three application areas: long-duration distributed storage for renewable energy, alternative fuels for heavy transportation, and cleaner feedstock for chemical and manufacturing industries. The company commercially launched its onsite hydrogen system in late 2025 and raised an $18.5M Series A led by Paramark Ventures and General Catalyst. Fourier is a hardware and infrastructure company and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or other software developer surface.

providers.name: PEI-Genesis
providers.description: PEI-Genesis is a privately held, Philadelphia-headquartered global authorized distributor and value-added assembler of interconnect components (cable and circular connectors), founded in 1946. The company self-describes on LinkedIn as providing "Engineered Solutions for Connectors and Cables" in the Appliances, Electrical, and Electronics Manufacturing industry, with 501-1,000 employees. The public-facing peigenesis.com web property is a product catalog and quote-request portal protected by an interstitial JavaScript challenge; no public REST API, OpenAPI specification, developer portal, EDI integration documentation, PunchOut catalog, or GitHub organization could be located. Public API documentation has not yet been catalogued in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Peloton Interactive
providers.description: Peloton Interactive is a connected fitness company that produces interactive exercise equipment and a streaming subscription service. The company sells connected stationary bikes, treadmills, rowers, and a digital app offering live and on-demand fitness classes. Peloton has built a large community of members who participate in instructor-led workouts and track performance metrics through its platform.

providers.name: AnalytiChem
providers.description: AnalytiChem is a global manufacturer of laboratory supplies, producing certified reference materials, specialized laboratory consumables, and sample-preparation systems for life sciences, environmental, materials, and lab-essentials markets. Its product families span ready-to-use culture media for microbial monitoring in pharmaceutical, food, beverage and environmental testing; laboratory standards for measuring heavy metals, pesticides and other contaminants; reference materials for the petrochemical, mining, metals and EV-battery industries; and reagents and solvents for chemical work and sample analysis. The company operates under ISO 17034, ISO 17025 and ISO 9001 quality accreditations. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass AnalytiChem publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Ascend Communications
providers.description: Ascend Communications, Inc. was an Alameda, California manufacturer of wide area networking equipment, founded in 1988 and taken public in 1994. It developed, manufactured and sold WAN access solutions — remote-access concentrators, ISDN and frame relay gear, and the MAX family of access servers — to telecommunications carriers, Internet service providers and corporate customers worldwide, becoming a leading supplier during the dial-up internet build-out of the 1990s. On January 13, 1999 Lucent Technologies announced a definitive agreement to merge with Ascend in a stock deal valued at roughly $20.3 billion, and the merger completed on June 24, 1999, when Ascend became a wholly owned subsidiary of Lucent. The company has not operated independently since. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Kleiner Perkins portfolio company; it predates the public web API era and publishes no developer surface today.

providers.name: Atlas Wearables
providers.description: Atlas Wearables was an Austin, Texas fitness-technology startup founded in 2013 by Peter Li, Mike Kasparian, and Alex Hsieh. It raised over $500,000 on Indiegogo in 2014 for the Atlas Wristband, a motion-tracking gym wearable whose "Exercise ID" technology automatically recognized strength exercises and counted reps and sets. The company shipped the Atlas Wristband and Wristband 2 and historically promoted an open developer API and integrations with apps such as MapMyFitness and Fitocracy. Atlas Wearables was acquired by Peloton Interactive in late 2020; the company no longer operates independently and the atlaswearables.com domain no longer resolves (it is now held by Peloton Interactive). This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical record of a former Techstars-associated portfolio lead; no live developer surface, API specification, or documentation remains available to enrich.

providers.name: Avanex
providers.description: Avanex Corporation was a fiber-optic components manufacturer founded in 1997 and headquartered in Fremont, California, backed by Mayfield along with Crosspoint Venture Partners, JAFCO America and Sequoia Capital. Avanex designed and built photonic processors, optical components, modules and subsystems used to raise the speed and capacity of fiber-optic communication networks, and went public on NASDAQ in February 2000 raising $216 million. In April 2009 Avanex merged with Bookham Technology to form Oclaro, and Oclaro was in turn acquired by Lumentum in December 2018. Avanex is no longer an operating company: it publishes no developer portal, documentation, or API of any kind, and the avanex.com domain is now a parked GoDaddy for-sale listing. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lineage record only.

providers.name: Cinta Networks
providers.description: Cinta Networks, Incorporated was a venture-backed optical networking equipment startup of the dot-com era, funded in part by Battery Ventures and led by CEO John Vaughan. The company built the patented WAVEJunction product family, an architecture that integrated DWDM optical transport with optical switching in a single network element for metro, regional, and long-haul carrier networks, claiming capital-expense savings of more than 50 percent and operational savings of over 70 percent through modular, port-at-a-time growth, universal transponder cards, and dynamic wavelength reconfiguration across ring and mesh topologies. Public activity is visible from roughly 2000 to 2002, including a January 2002 WAVEJunction field-trial agreement with Pacific LightNet and a component supply arrangement with ADC. Cinta Networks appears to have ceased operations in the post-telecom-bust period: archived captures of cintanetworks.com show the site replaced by a parked domain-search page by 2004, and the domain no longer resolves in DNS as of July 2026. Cinta was a hardware manufacturer and never published a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts, so there is no API surface for this profile to describe. It is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical Battery Ventures portfolio record.

providers.name: Concord Data Systems
providers.description: Concord Data Systems was a telecommunications equipment manufacturer founded in 1979 by Ken Miller (previously Director of Modem Development at Codex) and based in Marlborough, Massachusetts. The company designed and sold high-speed full-duplex dial-up telephone modems for transmitting digital computer data in analog form over the public switched telephone network. As the modem hardware market commoditized, the business pivoted from industrial data communications to the emerging market for network performance management software and was renamed Concord Communications, best known for its eHealth network management suite. Battery Ventures was one of thirteen investors in that company. Concord Communications was acquired by CA (Computer Associates) on 2005-06-07 for approximately $350 million ($330M cash plus roughly $20M of assumed net debt); CA was itself acquired by Broadcom in 2018. Concord Data Systems is therefore a historical, defunct entity: it operates no website, no developer portal, and no API surface today. It is retained in the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lineage record only.

providers.name: Conexant Systems
providers.description: Conexant Systems, Inc. was an American fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Irvine, California. Spun off from Rockwell Semiconductor Systems in 1999, it designed mixed-signal and system-on-chip products for audio, voice, imaging, modem, and networking applications, and was best known for its dial-up modem chipsets, audio codecs, and far-field voice-input processors used in smart-home and IoT devices. Conexant's audio and imaging business was acquired by Synaptics in 2017 and the standalone Conexant brand has since been retired. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead; the company publishes no public developer portal, API, or machine-readable API surface (its former conexant.com domain no longer resolves to an active site), so there are no API artifacts to enrich at this time.

providers.name: Copper Mountain Network
providers.description: Copper Mountain Networks was a telecommunications equipment maker founded in 1996 by Mark Handzel and Joe Markee that led the 1990s DSL (Digital Subscriber Line) wave in North America, building central-office DSL concentrators (the CopperEdge platform) and customer-premises modems that delivered high-speed broadband over existing copper telephone lines. The company was venture-backed by Canaan Partners and InterWest, held its IPO in 1999, weathered the telecom downturn of 2001, and was acquired by Tut Systems in 2005 (later absorbed into Motorola in 2007). It shipped hardware and network equipment, not a public web/developer API; the company is defunct and operates no live developer platform today.

providers.name: Cortina Systems
providers.description: Cortina Systems, Inc. was a venture-backed fabless semiconductor company founded in 2001 and headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, that designed high-speed communications and networking integrated circuits for optical transport, carrier Ethernet, framer/mapper and PHY devices, and broadband access (EPON/GPON and DSL). The company grew through acquisitions and was itself acquired by Inphi Corporation in 2014; Inphi later merged into Marvell Technology in 2021, and the cortina-systems.com domain now redirects to Marvell. Cortina was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners. It is a hardware semiconductor business with no public developer platform or API surface, so no API artifacts apply.

providers.name: Crane
providers.description: Crane Co. (NYSE: CR) and its sister company Crane NXT (NYSE: CXT) are industrial manufacturing companies that resulted from the 2023 split of the legacy Crane Holdings, Co. Crane Co. is a diversified manufacturer of highly engineered industrial products serving aerospace and electronics, process flow technologies, and engineered materials markets. Crane NXT is a global leader in trusted technology solutions for payment, security, and authentication including currency, banknote, and authentication products. No public APIs or developer portals are published; integrations with industrial customers are arranged through enterprise channels.

providers.name: Echelon
providers.description: Echelon Corporation was a pioneer in energy control networking and semiconductors, known for its LonWorks control networking platform and IoT edge computing products. Surfaced as a Mayfield portfolio company (listed as an energy-control-networking milestone/exit), the company is no longer an independent entity — its product lines were acquired (Adesto Technologies, 2018) and now live under EnOcean. There is no live Echelon developer portal or public API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Estes Energy
providers.description: Estes Energy is a US-based manufacturer of advanced battery packs for heavy-duty transport. Its magnesium-alloy Magnus platform (proprietary MgCarbonit thermo-structural body) delivers roughly 225 Wh/kg for rail, marine, aviation and off-highway applications, with chemistry-agnostic (sodium, LFP, nickel) packs manufactured entirely in the United States. Backed by DCVC, Fortescue Ventures, BMW and New System Ventures. A hardware/manufacturing company with no public API, developer portal, SDK or software product surface at this time.

providers.name: Gainspeed
providers.description: Gainspeed, Inc. was a Sunnyvale, California networking startup that developed a Virtual Converged Cable Access Platform (Virtual CCAP) built on a Distributed Access Architecture (Remote PHY / DAA) for cable multiple-system operators (MSOs). The company was backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and was acquired by Nokia in 2016, after which its virtual CCAP technology was folded into Nokia's cable access portfolio. It was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Gainspeed operated no public developer program, API, or live developer portal; its domain no longer resolves.

providers.name: Heartstream
providers.description: Heartstream is an emergency-care and defibrillation brand, now part of Philips, that makes automated external defibrillators (AEDs) and professional monitor/defibrillators for public-access, home, and EMS use. The company originated as a Mayfield-backed medical-device startup that pioneered automatic external defibrillators and was later acquired by Hewlett-Packard; today the Heartstream name lives on across the HeartStart AED and Tempus ALS product lines sold in more than 50 countries and regions. Its public site publishes product support, a document center (instructions for use), and a newsroom, but it exposes no public developer portal, API, or documentation surface, so there are no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: In Charge One, Inc.
providers.description: In Charge One, Inc. is a hardware startup behind "Socket to Pocket," a paid charging system for electronic devices in public spaces. The device lets visitors charge smartphones, laptops, drones, e-bikes, and scooters at cafes, shops, clinics, stadiums, airports, and other venues by tapping a card and paying for access, while venue owners monetize the outlet and earn a commission per plugged socket. It ships in wall-mounted, extension-cord, and anti-vandal street versions. Founded in 2023 by Danylo (Daniel) Tonkopii, co-founder of Delfast electric bikes, and Andriy Zinchuk, the company is based in Los Angeles, California and was developed by Ukrainian engineers. It is a consumer/commercial hardware and payments business, not an API provider: no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface has been published, and its incharge.one domain is currently non-resolving and in registrar redemption/pending-delete status. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and is retained as an identity record.

providers.name: LightLogic
providers.description: LightLogic was an optoelectronics company founded in January 1998 and headquartered in Newark, California. It designed and manufactured highly integrated optical modules — transmitters and receivers — for high-speed (10 Gb/s and up) fiber optic telecommunications equipment, specializing in the integration of lasers, micro-optics and high-speed electronics. Its marquee products were 10 Gb/s transponders providing optical-to-electrical conversion for SONET OC-192 and 10 Gigabit Ethernet applications, sold to optical networking OEMs building primarily metro-market systems. The company raised $57.5M and was backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Cisco Systems, Infineon Technologies, Dassault Developpement, Infinity Capital, Lightspeed Venture Partners (then Weiss, Peck and Greer), Optical Capital Group, Ridge Ventures, Siemens Mustang Ventures and Viventures. LightLogic was acquired by Intel Corporation; by mid-2002 lightlogic.com redirected to Intel's optical transceiver product pages. This is a hardware component maker with no API, developer or software surface — historically or today — and the lightlogic.com domain no longer resolves.

providers.name: Lumius
providers.description: Lumius is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) medical-imaging startup building fast, smart, accessible real-time 3D ultrasound systems — described as "a 3D camera for the body." The technology aims to move ultrasound beyond traditional 2D imaging to intelligent, AI-assisted 3D visualization across larger volumes, with an initial focus on vascular access and central-line placement (where roughly half of first attempts fail among new clinicians) and future targets including blood-clot detection, tumor diagnosis, and biopsy guidance. The company partners with academic institutions such as Duke University and Columbia University. Lumius is a hardware/device company with no public API, SDK, or developer platform; its products are pre-market and not intended for medical use. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a VC portfolio lead and has been reviewed by the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Newport Communications
providers.description: NewPort Communications was a fabless semiconductor startup that developed mixed-signal integrated circuits for the high-speed optical networking market, including CMOS-based transceivers for 2.5-Gbit/s (OC-48) SONET/SDH applications. Founded in 1999, the company was backed by Mayfield Fund, Bessemer Venture Partners, and Cisco Investments (roughly $28M across Series A and B) before being acquired by Broadcom on October 4, 2000 to strengthen Broadcom's networking semiconductor portfolio. It is a defunct company with no standalone public web presence and no API surface; this record is retained as a historical portfolio-company lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Omniome
providers.description: Omniome was a San Diego genomics company that developed Sequencing By Binding (SBB) technology, a proprietary chemistry aimed at highly accurate short-read DNA sequencing. Surfaced as a portfolio company of dcvc, Omniome was acquired by Pacific Biosciences (PacBio) in 2021, and its site now redirects to pacb.com. It builds laboratory sequencing instruments and chemistry rather than a public developer platform, and exposes no public API surface.

providers.name: Oni Systems
providers.description: ONI Systems Inc. was an optical networking equipment company that built optical switching and transport systems for metropolitan-area networks during the fiber-optic boom of the late 1990s and early 2000s. Backed by Canaan Partners and other venture investors, the company went public and was acquired by Ciena Corporation in 2002, after which its product line was absorbed into Ciena's metro optical portfolio. It operated as an equipment maker and has no standalone developer program, public API surface, SDKs, or online documentation of its own. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical/defunct portfolio-lead record.

providers.name: Phoenix Wireless
providers.description: Phoenix Wireless (Phoenix Wireless Group) was a manufacturer of wireless telecommunications accessories and hardware, founded in 1994 and headquartered in West Chester, PA. Its product lines included antennas, Bluetooth headsets, phone clips, mounts and fasteners, induction chargers, travel chargers, and batteries. The company was acquired by Communications Test Design, Inc. (CTDI) on September 26, 2008 and no longer operates as an independent entity. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment; the enrichment pass found no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or other machine-readable developer surface to catalog.

providers.name: Playbrush
providers.description: Playbrush is a consumer oral-care technology brand that makes smart, gamified electric and sonic toothbrushes for children (ages 3+), pairing a Bluetooth-connected brush with a companion mobile app that turns brushing into interactive games and coaching to build good dental-hygiene habits. Founded as a UK/Austria startup and backed by Speedinvest, the Playbrush product line has since been acquired by SUNSTAR and is now sold under the GUM Playbrush brand; the former playbrush.com domain 302-redirects to a Sunstar GUM product page. Playbrush is a hardware/consumer-app company and exposes no public developer portal, API, specification, or /.well-known/ discovery surface. This profile was surfaced as a Speedinvest portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; enrichment confirmed there is no API surface.

providers.name: Sila
providers.description: Sila Nanotechnologies (silanano.com) is a battery materials company that develops and manufactures Titan Silicon, a next-generation silicon anode that replaces graphite in lithium-ion batteries to increase energy density and enable fast charging. Sila operates silicon anode manufacturing facilities and also offers battery engineering services, targeting electric vehicles, consumer electronics, aerospace, data centers, robotics, and defense. The enrichment pass found no developer API, API documentation, or developer portal: Sila is a B2B advanced-materials hardware company with no public API surface.

providers.name: AMD
providers.description: A multinational semiconductor company designing high-performance processors, graphics cards, and adaptive computing solutions. Competes in data center, gaming, and embedded markets with its Ryzen, EPYC, and Radeon product lines.

providers.name: Dow Chemical
providers.description: Dow Chemical, now operating as Dow Inc., is a global materials science company headquartered in Midland, Michigan. Dow develops innovative products and solutions across three segments - Packaging and Specialty Plastics, Industrial Intermediates and Infrastructure, and Performance Materials and Coatings - serving packaging, infrastructure, mobility, and consumer applications.

providers.name: DuPont
providers.description: DuPont is a leading solutions provider for healthcare, water, and a broad range of industrial segments, powered by high-performance engineered products, leading-edge application development, and top-tier manufacturing. No public developer APIs or developer portal have been identified at this time; this index captures DuPont's web presence for monitoring future developer activity.

providers.name: hhgregg
providers.description: hhgregg is an electronics retailer offering products such as televisions, cameras, professional video equipment, laptops, headphones, drones, and more, with free shipping and installation services on many products.

providers.name: Modulus Video
providers.description: Modulus Video is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of trinity-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: hardware. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Northpoint Communications
providers.description: Northpoint Communications is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of accel and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: hardware. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: SiTera
providers.description: SiTera is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of matrix-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: semiconductors. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Qorvo
providers.description: Profile for Qorvo in the API Evangelist network. Fortune F1000 (rank 765).

providers.name: Lam Research
providers.description: Lam Research is a global supplier of innovative wafer fabrication equipment and services to the semiconductor industry, providing systems used in the production of integrated circuits.

providers.name: TSMC
providers.description: The world's largest dedicated semiconductor foundry manufacturing chips for leading technology companies. Produces the most advanced processor chips used in smartphones, data centers, and AI applications for clients including Apple, NVIDIA, and AMD.

providers.name: Microchip Technology
providers.description: Microchip Technology is a leading provider of smart, connected, and secure embedded control solutions, offering microcontrollers, mixed-signal, analog, and Flash-IP solutions.

providers.name: Micron Technology
providers.description: Explore Micron Technology, leading in semiconductors with a broad range of performance-enhancing memory and storage solutions.

providers.name: GameStop
providers.description: GameStop is a global multichannel video game, consumer electronics, and gaming merchandise retailer operating retail stores and e-commerce sites.

providers.name: Kla
providers.description: KLA is a leader in process control using advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, and computational analytics. Keep Looking Ahead.

bands.label: Not Yet Rated
bands.blurb: Providers we have not scored yet — unknown, not zero.

providers.name: ConnectDER
providers.description: ConnectDER is a Philadelphia-based clean energy hardware company and the leading US manufacturer of meter socket adapters (MSAs, also called meter collars) for the residential market. Founded in 2011 as Infinite Invention LLC after a DOE SunShot Incubator grant, it builds plug-and-play devices that install at the utility meter socket to interconnect distributed energy resources — rooftop solar, battery storage and EV charging — without panel upgrades, line-side taps or circuit relocations. Its product line is the IslandDER MSA (a microgrid interconnect device for solar-plus-battery and whole-home backup, integrated by SolarEdge, FranklinWH, Lunar Energy, EcoFlow and Fox ESS), the Solar MSA and the EV MSA. ConnectDER helped author UL 414 Supplements A, B and C, the standards governing meter socket adapters, and has surpassed 40,000 devices installed across US utility territories including PG&E, SCE and SDG&E. ConnectDER publishes no public developer API, SDK or machine-readable API contract; its devices communicate with partner battery systems over discrete hardwired sensing, control and status signals rather than a network interface. It does publish an llms.txt at its web root.

providers.name: Devialet
providers.description: Devialet is a French high-end audio company founded and headquartered in Paris, known for the Phantom active loudspeaker range, the Dione soundbar, the Mania portable speaker, the Gemini earbuds, and the Expert Pro amplifier line, and for patented acoustic technologies including ADH (Analog Digital Hybrid), SAM (Speaker Active Matching), and the EVO embedded platform. Its developer-facing surface is the Devialet IP Control API — an unauthenticated HTTP API served by the speakers themselves on the local network under the /ipcontrol/v1 path, introduced with DOS 2.14 firmware and documented by Devialet as a PDF reference for system integrators. It exposes device, system, and group state plus playback, volume, equalizer, night mode, Bluetooth pairing, and power and factory-reset commands, with mDNS/DNS-SD discovery. Devialet also ships certified home-automation drivers for Crestron and Control4 alongside the raw API.

providers.name: Ethernovia
providers.description: Ethernovia is a San Jose, California semiconductor company building deterministic Ethernet networking silicon for software-defined vehicles, robotics and physical AI. Its portfolio spans single-pair (T1) Ethernet PHYs from 1G to 10G (ENT11100, ENT11025, ENT14100, ENT14025), deterministic packet processors and switches, and the High-Speed Sensor Bridge platform that bridges GMSL 2/3 cameras and CAN FD/XL onto 10GBASE-T1 Ethernet for NVIDIA Holoscan, Orin and Thor compute. Ethernovia publishes no public product API: its software binaries, source-code drivers, header files and plug-in APIs are distributed to customers under NDA and a separate EULA through the Ethernovia Customer Portal. The one machine-readable contract reachable without credentials is the Customer Portal's own backend API, whose Swagger UI is served publicly at portal-admin.ethernovia.com/documentation.

providers.name: Fnatic
providers.description: Fnatic is a London-headquartered global esports performance brand founded in 2004, fielding 20+ professional players across five game titles, operating four offices and facilities in London, Berlin, Belgrade and Tokyo with 100+ staff, and claiming $16m+ in prize money, 33m+ social followers and $55m raised from institutional investors. Beyond competition it runs two commercial businesses: Fnatic Gear, an award-winning esports hardware line (mice, keyboards, headsets and pads) launched in 2016, and an apparel and merchandise store. Fnatic operates no developer program and publishes no OpenAPI, no developer portal and no API documentation — fnatic.com is a Next.js front end over a Sanity CMS with a first-party member-account system ("Fnatic ID") that exposes no discovery document. Its one machine-readable surface is the Shopify-hosted store at shop.fnatic.com, which serves an anonymously introspectable Storefront GraphQL API, a Universal Commerce Protocol merchant profile with a UCP MCP commerce endpoint, OpenID Connect and RFC 8414/9728 discovery for customer accounts, and a provider-authored /agents.md (mirrored at /llms.txt) that tells AI agents which surface to use and requires explicit buyer approval before any agent completes a payment.

providers.name: Foundry Group
providers.description: Foundry Group is a Boulder, Colorado venture capital firm founded in 2007 by Brad Feld, Seth Levine, Ryan McIntyre, and Jason Mendelson. The firm invests in early-stage technology startups across the United States, organizing its work around long-lived, horizontal investment themes (such as "glue", "protocol", "distribution", and "human computer interaction") rather than narrow verticals, with a particular affinity for hardware, robotics, consumer internet, developer tools, and B2B SaaS. Foundry pioneered a "network-driven" model that operates both as a direct investor in startups and as a limited partner in a curated network of more than 40 partner venture funds. The firm manages more than $3.0B for its limited partners, has made 320+ investments and 70+ exits, and is known for radical transparency through the books, blogs, and podcasts of its partners. Notable investments include Fitbit, Zynga, SendGrid, MakerBot, Gnip, Mapbox, SeatGeek, and WHOOP. In 2022 the partners announced Foundry would not raise another fund, continuing to steward its existing funds and portfolio through their life.

providers.name: Gradiant
providers.description: Gradiant is a global water and wastewater infrastructure company founded in 2013 out of MIT and headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, that designs, builds and operates end-to-end industrial water systems from intake to discharge. It positions itself as "the Water Layer of the AI Economy", supplying ultrapure water, process water, wastewater recycling, minimal- and zero-liquid-discharge and resource-recovery systems to semiconductor fabs, AI data centers, energy producers and applied industries including pharmaceuticals, mining, food and beverage, refining and chemicals, textiles and renewables. Its proprietary technology portfolio includes Counterflow Reverse Osmosis (CFRO), Semi-Batch Reverse Osmosis (SBRO), Carrier Gas Extraction (CGE), Selective Contaminant Extraction (SCE), Free Radical Oxidation (FRO), Bio Infinity, the ForeverGone PFAS destruction process, the HyperSolved data-center cooling-water platform, the CURE Chemicals specialty-chemicals line and SmartOps AI, a machine-learning platform for optimizing and predicting plant operations. Gradiant raised a Series E at a $2 billion valuation in May 2026. It is an industrial equipment, chemicals and build-own-operate services company: it publishes no public developer portal, no developer API, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract, and SmartOps AI is delivered as a customer-facing operations platform rather than as a public API.

providers.name: High Tech
providers.description: High Tech indexes the APIs, data services, and reference artifacts that power the electronics, semiconductor, hardware, and IoT industries. The landscape covers electronic component data and distribution (Octopart / Nexar, Digi-Key, Mouser, Arrow Electronics, Avnet, Newark / element14), ECAD and PCB design data (SnapEDA, Ultra Librarian, Altium 365 via Nexar Design), hardware lifecycle and IoT device management (AWS IoT, Azure IoT Hub, Particle, Golioth), bill-of-materials and component-search workflows used across hardware product engineering, and the authoritative manufacturer data that anchors a component record (manufacturer part number, manufacturer, datasheet, lifecycle status, RoHS / REACH compliance, real-time inventory and pricing across distributors). This index captures the canonical providers, the shape of a component record as JSON Schema, a JSON-LD context aligning with schema.org Product / Offer / Organization, and the domain vocabulary used across the high-tech component supply chain.

providers.name: Matrix Partners
providers.description: Matrix Partners (now branded simply "Matrix") is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 1977 by Paul Ferri, investing from idea through Series A. Headquartered in San Francisco at 535 Mission Street with a long-standing East Coast office in Cambridge, Massachusetts, the firm is run by former founders and company builders who describe themselves as "contrarians who invest with conviction," backing founders with deep technical expertise and a specific vision of the future. Matrix is a generalist early-stage investor across AI / frontier tech, B2B and enterprise software, fintech, consumer, healthtech, infrastructure, and semiconductors, typically writing seed and Series A checks and leading rounds. Over nearly five decades the firm has backed foundational technology and consumer companies including Apple, HubSpot, Zendesk, Canva, Afterpay, Oculus, Fivetran, Flock Safety, Quora, Postmates, GOAT, and Suno, with a track record spanning semiconductors and networking through today's AI-native startups.

providers.name: Mayfield Fund
providers.description: Mayfield Fund is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 1969 and headquartered on Sand Hill Road in Menlo Park, California, with a presence in Mumbai, India. One of the oldest continuously active Silicon Valley firms, Mayfield describes itself as "people first, from inception" and reports that roughly 70% of its investments begin at company inception, positioning it as the first institutional investor for early-stage founders. The firm invests primarily at the Seed, Series A, and Series B stages across artificial intelligence, enterprise software, cloud and cybersecurity infrastructure, semiconductors, consumer and social commerce, and human and planetary health. Mayfield reports approximately $3B in assets under management (and states it has committed $3B to AI investments), has backed more than 550 companies over its history, and counts 120+ IPOs and 225+ M&A exits including Genentech, Lyft, HashiCorp, Poshmark, Marketo, Couchbase, SolarCity, Intuitive Surgical, and Compaq. In 2023 the firm raised $955M across two new funds dedicated to early-stage investing.

providers.name: Modal
providers.description: Modal is a serverless cloud platform for AI and data workloads. Modal lets developers write ordinary Python and run it on remote GPUs and CPUs with sub-second cold starts, instant autoscaling, and declarative container images. The platform's primitives — Functions, Sandboxes, Volumes, Images, Secrets, Dicts, Queues, Schedules, and Web Endpoints — cover inference, fine-tuning, multi-node training, batch processing, agent code execution, and HTTP/web APIs. Modal sells per-second metered compute across the full NVIDIA GPU lineup (T4 → B200) under Starter, Team, and Enterprise plans. Modal Labs raised a $355M Series C in 2026 and is used in production by Decagon, Runway, Physical Intelligence, Suno, Chai Discovery, Lovable, Quora, Reducto, and many others.

providers.name: Parasail
providers.description: Parasail is an AI Supercloud — a pay-per-token GPU inference platform aimed at AI startups and developers. Parasail orchestrates rented GPU capacity across 40+ data centers in 15+ countries to serve open-weight LLMs, vision/multimodal models, embedding models, and TTS/STT models on a serverless, dedicated, or batch basis. The platform exposes OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoints for chat completions, completions, embeddings, batch, and models, plus a control-plane /api/v1 for managing dedicated GPU deployments of any Hugging Face or custom model. Parasail serves 500B+ tokens per day and is positioned as up to 30x cheaper than legacy cloud providers, with no quotas, no rate-limit penalties, and no long-term contracts. Co-founded by Mike Henry (ex-Mythic) and Tim Harris (ex-Swift Navigation); raised a $32M Series A in April 2026 (Touring Capital and Kindred Ventures) bringing total funding to $42M.

providers.name: Playground Global
providers.description: Playground Global is an early-stage deep tech venture capital firm founded in 2015 by Andy Rubin, Bruce Leak, Matt Hershenson, and Peter Barrett, and headquartered at 380 Portage Ave, Palo Alto, California. The firm invests "somewhere between improbable and impossible," backing technical founders who take large technology risks and build companies from first principles. Playground concentrates on four pillars: next-gen compute (quantum computing, novel AI chip architectures, advanced interconnects, and semiconductors), automation (robotics, supply-chain and industrial automation with tangible ROI), energy transition and decarbonization, and engineered biology (AI-driven drug discovery, RNA editing, and next-generation therapies). It invests at the earliest stages, often at company formation, and operates Studio Palo Alto, a lab and prototyping environment for hardware and deep-science founders. Reported assets under management are over $1.2 billion across its funds. Notable portfolio companies include PsiQuantum, Relativity Space, Ultima Genomics, d-Matrix, Velo3D (NYSE), and MosaicML (acquired by Databricks).

providers.name: Qiming Venture Partners
providers.description: Qiming Venture Partners is a leading China-based venture capital firm founded in 2006 by Duane Kuang and Gary Rieschel, headquartered in Shanghai with additional offices in Beijing, Suzhou, Hong Kong, Singapore, and a U.S. affiliate (Qiming Venture Partners USA) in Seattle, Washington. The firm invests at the early and growth stages, with roughly 70% of its investments concentrated in Series A and Series B rounds, across two core practice areas: Technology (mobile internet, consumer, AI, robotics, semiconductors, enterprise software, autonomous driving) and Healthcare (biotech, pharmaceuticals, medical devices, diagnostics, and digital health). Qiming manages 11 U.S. Dollar funds and 7 RMB funds with approximately $9.5 billion in capital raised, and has backed more than 580 companies, of which over 210 have exited via IPO on the NYSE, NASDAQ, HKEX, Shanghai, or Shenzhen exchanges, or through M&A. It is an early backer of some of China's most influential technology companies, including Xiaomi, Meituan, Bilibili, Zhihu, Roborock, Hesai Technology, UBTech, WeRide, Insta360, and Zhipu AI (Z.ai), alongside a deep healthcare portfolio spanning Zai Lab, Gan & Lee Pharmaceuticals, CanSino Biologics, Tigermed, and Insilico Medicine.

providers.name: Spark Capital
providers.description: Spark Capital is a multi-stage venture capital firm founded in 2005 by Paul Conway, Santo Politi, Todd Dagres, and Bijan Sabet, with offices in San Francisco, New York, and Boston. Spark is a generalist firm that partners with founders from seed through growth across consumer internet, enterprise software, artificial intelligence, gaming, crypto, fintech, infrastructure, hardware and semiconductors, life sciences, aerospace, and the future of work. The firm invests from a family of early-stage funds (most recently a $700M fund in 2024) and dedicated growth funds (most recently a $1.4B fund in 2024), and press reports have placed its assets under management in the range of $12-15 billion. Spark first became widely known for leading Twitter's Series B in 2008 and has since backed a run of defining companies including Slack, Discord, Snap, Coinbase, Affirm, Plaid, Cruise, Oculus, Scale AI, Ramp, Deel, and Anthropic, whose Series C investment the firm turned into one of venture's largest recent markups. Spark rebranded in 2020 with design studio Pentagram around its distinctive dog-themed identity, and publishes a curated set of portfolio companies rather than a full list.

providers.name: True Ventures
providers.description: True Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2006 by Jon Callaghan and Phil Black and headquartered in Palo Alto / San Francisco, California. Operating under a "first to believe" thesis, True writes the initial institutional check and stays invested through every subsequent stage of a company's journey, concentrating on pre-seed, seed, and Series A rounds with check sizes reported in the roughly $500K-$15M range. The firm invests broadly across technology and founder-led categories including software and developer infrastructure, consumer products and internet, healthcare and life sciences, hardware and robotics, climate and energy, security, and AI. With more than $3.8B in committed capital, True has backed 1,050+ founders across 500+ companies since inception, with notable early checks into Fitbit, Peloton, Ring, Automattic/WordPress, HashiCorp, Duo Security, Sweetgreen, Bluesky, and Splice. True is known for its founder-first platform, the True University founder camps, and long-term conviction-led early ownership.
